author: Valerie Anne
title: Everything You Need To Know About the Lesbians of ‘Silo’
content:
For the first two and a half seasons of the post-apocalyptic Apple TV epic Silo, we only had two lesbian characters, buried deep in the ground: a badass mechanic, Martha, played by Harriet Walter who rarely left her apartment, and her ex-wife Carla, head of Supply, played by Clare Perkins. Their relationship was not a major plotline, but I was happy for the representation anyway. Elder lesbians! The best at their respective jobs! Love to see it.

This season, we got introduced to some more lesbians, this time in the aboveground storyline. Congressman Daniel Keene finds out his younger sister Charlotte (Jessica Brown Findlay, who played queer on Harlots) had been in an accident while she was working as a Navy pilot. After she recovered, she joined her brother and the reporter Helen Drew (Jessica Henwick) to learn more about what brought her plane down, and there she met the Senator’s daughter Anna (Morven Christie). The two hit it off and were flirting on a private plane and I kind of thought that was the most we were going to get, but then the aboveground timeline had a little time jump and the next thing we know, Charlotte and Anna are married! They have a cute double-date night with Daniel and Helen and gosh you’d almost forget this was an apocalypse show.

However, at the end of the episode, Charlotte is nowhere to be found. Daniel tries to text her and gets a response that makes him suspicious she doesn’t have access to her own phone. I texted my friend, LESBIAN IN PERIL. Though based on how the episode ended…a lot more people than just Charlotte are in peril.

Now, for the majority of this season, I held onto a bonkers theory: I thought the aboveground and belowground timelines were running concurrently. I was so convinced the silos were a social experiment being done before any nukes had ever gone off. My theory was kiboshed by the end of the episode, HOWEVER, I still don’t think 300 years have passed between the aboveground timeline and what Juliette Nichols is up to. I think it’s possible it has only been 50 years, or fewer, and the Vitamin D+ they use to erase everyone’s memories, combined with the Pact and the “AI” voice, led them to believe it’s been a lot longer, telling them fictional stories about past rebellions and other resets. I think that’s why artifacts and relics were outlawed, lest they trigger memories. Otherwise, what would it matter if they had things from the old world? So now, my newest unhinged theory is: what if Charlotte IS Martha. This week, they talked about how the Vitamin D+ shakes memories up so bad some parents forgot to feed their own children. So it’s not unreasonable to think a person or two forgot their own name. And Navy pilot to mechanic isn’t an insane pipeline…JUST SAYING.

Anyway, I’ve been having a lot of fun trying to untangle the mysteries of this world, going full red string murderboard about it, and I am STRESSED but excited to see what Silo‘s season finale brings this week. Fingers crossed all lesbians will be found and accounted for, safe and sound and underground.

+ Olivia Rodrigo’s Daisy Chain Fields festival was a success, featuring some queer artists among its star-studded list and raising $20 million for women’s health organizations

+ A podcast host assumed actress and singer Maia Reficco was straight and she was QUICK to correct him; the Pretty Little Liars: Original Sin/Summer School star says original Liar Lucy Hale is one of her gay awakenings

author: Eden Fineday
title: Help us keep the syilx Okanagan beat strong
content:
At the bottom of kɬúsx̌nítkʷ (Okanagan Lake) in snpink’tn (Penticton) on Aug. 26, community members gather and pray for the health of the land and for those affected by wildfires this summer.

Photo by Aaron Hemens


This story was reprinted from our newsletter. Subscribe for updates

here

 and learn more about our Okanagan campaign

here

.


The Okanagan was the very first community IndigiNews committed to covering.


When we launched in 2020, we made a promise to report on syilx Okanagan communities week after week with a consistency that shows our care and respect for the peoples and their territories. 


For the past four years, that promise has been kept by our reporter in the region, Aaron Hemens.


Today, his work is at risk.


Aaron on the ground in April 2024, reporting on a cultural burn.

Photo by Aaron Hemens


The funding that supported Aaron’s incredible reporting has ended. Without new support, IndigiNews will no longer be able to provide the same quality of dedicated storytelling we’ve offered in syilx Okanagan communities. 


Our goal

is to raise 

$35,000

 from our community of IndigiNews readers to keep Aaron covering the Okanagan. If we can reach our goal, we’ll be able to keep Aaron on the Okanagan beat for another full year — ensuring his vital reporting continues without interruption.


Keep the syilx Okanagan beat strong


We need to raise

$35,000

 to keep Aaron Hemens reporting from syilx Okanagan territory.


Help sustain independent, Indigenous-led local journalism.


Donate today


Aaron, a settler of mixed Filipino and European heritage, approaches his work with IndigiNews by centering the communities he’s reporting on. He believes journalism should be done in a good way — through building relationships that centre community protocol and accountability. 


As a man of colour, Aaron is very aware of what it means to be overlooked, misrepresented, and excluded in news media and beyond. This knowledge inspires him to show up at community gatherings, council meetings and court hearings to sensitively document the conversations that rarely make national headlines but nevertheless inform them.


nkwancinem Kim Montgomery dances at the Similkameen powwow arbour grounds on July 23, after being honoured for her 20 years of service with the Okanagan Nation Alliance.

 Photo by Aaron Hemens


This trust wasn’t built overnight. It took years of showing up for the people of the Okanagan. 


Across “Canada,” local journalism is disappearing. News deserts are spreading, hitting Indigenous communities particularly hard. As a result, important decisions are going undocumented, local histories are getting left unwritten, and people are less and less able to hold powerful institutions accountable. 


Stories disappear and, with them, access to the beating hearts of entire communities. 


At IndigiNews, we believe all communities deserve reporters who know the people they serve — not only during moments of crisis.


That’s why

we’re asking for your help

.


Community members exit a canoe after arriving in Penticton on July 30. The canoe was carved by Herman Edward, who participated in the original journey in 2001.

Photo by Aaron Hemens


As a registered Canadian charity, every eligible donation receives a charitable tax receipt. Whether you become a dependable monthly

 Firekeeper

 or make a one-time gift, your support directly sustains independent Indigenous journalism.


Every dollar protects the relationships IndigiNews has created — relationships that cannot simply be replaced.


If you’ve ever read one of Aaron’s stories, shared our reporting, or believe Indigenous communities deserve devoted local journalism, please consider making a gift today.


Together, we can ensure the Okanagan continues to have the journalism it deserves.


$35,000 Goal


Donate

Help us keep the syilx Okanagan beat strong

Indiginews

author: Elizabeth Weill-Greenberg
title: Shaken Baby Syndrome Has Been Largely Debunked. Courts Are Still Catching Up.
content:
This story was co-published with


Truthout

.


  By the time Mason Tucker Smith was 2 years old, his mother, Mary Katherine Smith, had taken him to the doctor dozens of times.


  Tucker had frequent ear infections, high fevers, and episodes of vomiting. On at least six occasions, he had seizures, but the doctors repeatedly reassured his mother, who goes by Katie, that these were benign “breath-holding spells” that would resolve on their own.


  On the day of his collapse, July 30, 2014, Tucker had another seizure while Katie’s housemate, Jeremy Kitchens, was watching him in their bedroom and Katie was making dinner, according to her statement to the police.


  As she approached the bedroom door, she heard a “thud.” Katie entered the room and Kitchens told her that Tucker was having another “episode.” Katie told police that she found Tucker unconscious on the ground. Believing that this was another breath-holding episode, she picked him up and put him on the bed. She left him in Kitchens’s care while she drove her daughter to meet a friend. While she was gone, Tucker vomited.


  She returned to the house about 20 minutes later and checked Tucker’s oxygen level. When it began to drop, she called 911 and attempted to resuscitate him.


  At the hospital, a physician concluded Tucker had been shaken. He was declared dead on August 2 and Katie was charged with his murder.


  Two years later, Katie went to trial in Richmond County, Georgia, and was found guilty. The judge sentenced her to life in prison.


  Shaken baby syndrome (SBS), also known as abusive head trauma (AHT), has been largely debunked, with one New Jersey judge

calling it

 “akin to ‘junk science.’” While some courts have started to take a more critical look at SBS/AHT cases,

prosecutions have continued

 and

many people

 are still fighting their convictions.


The Appeal in Your Inbox


Subscribe to our newsletters for regular updates, analysis and context straight to your email.


Sign Up


  The so-called

triad of symptoms

 associated with SBS/AHT — bleeding around the eyes, bleeding between the skull and brain, and brain swelling —

can be caused by

 strokes, short-distance falls, seizures, and disease, among other things.


  Katie’s attorneys with the Southern Center for Human Rights say their investigation has revealed that she was convicted of a crime that never occurred.


  Experts retained by her legal team — a neurologist and a forensic pathologist — have concluded that Tucker died of undiagnosed epilepsy, which was caused by an undetected arteriovenous malformation (AVM) in his brain. AVM is a life-threatening condition that typically develops in utero, in which a person has abnormally tangled blood vessels that disrupt blood flow, deprive tissue of oxygen, and face risk of rupture.


  Forty-four people have been exonerated in SBS/AHT cases, according to the

National Registry of Exonerations

.


  Katie’s attorneys have filed a motion for a new trial and, on August 24, they will present their new evidence before the Superior Court of Richmond County.. The Augusta District Attorney’s Office is opposing Katie’s petition. The office did not respond to emails or calls seeking comment.


  “Tucker’s death was a tragedy, not a crime,” Katie’s lawyers wrote in their motion. “Tucker was sick from birth, and was living with an undiagnosed and untreated deadly brain condition.”


Tucker’s Medical Records


Truthout

reviewed Tucker’s medical records, which total about 278 pages. They reveal that Katie took him to the pediatrician more than 25 times, in addition to visits to specialists and the emergency room.


  The physicians reassured Katie that Tucker was a healthy child. They told her that when he became upset he held his breath until he passed out, but that this was nothing to be concerned about.


  Tucker’s first witnessed seizure occurred at daycare when he was five months old. Katie picked him up from daycare and took him to the pediatrician.


  “Patient was reported to have had eyes roll back and lose consciousness while eating baby food in a highchair (sort of slumped),” the doctor wrote.


  The pediatrician sent him to the hospital for an overnight observation. During the observation, Tucker “ate and slept well,” according to the medical records. Katie told the doctor that Tucker’s father, who had died shortly after Tucker’s death, and nephew each had experienced one seizure. The report does not recommend any further …

author: Kevin Carson
title: La Lagna della “Economia” che la Sinistra “Non Capisce”
content:
Di

Kevin Carson

. Originale:

On Larken Rose: The “Economics” the Left “Doesn’t Understand” Gets Dumber Every Day

, del 3 agosto 2026. Tradotto da

Enrico Sanna

.


Se frequentate internet e siete di sinistra, vi sarà certamente capitato di essere deriso da qualche simpaticone di destra (magari con la testatina in nero e oro e #Bitcoin nel profilo) che vi dice: “voi non capite l’economia” o “ma andate a studiarvi l’economia!”. Quando, per qualche meccanismo perverso, tra le raccomandazioni di YouTube mi è comparso un podcast di Larken Rose (

Appreciating Capitalism

), ho deciso, data l’enorme stima dei suddetti simpaticoni per le sue nozioni di “economia”, di migliorare la mia conoscenza del soggetto.


È difficile dare un’idea di un suo podcast, o del suo livello di stupidità, visto che molte delle peculiarità stanno nel podcast stesso. Lo stile è Rush Limbaugh puro. La voce trasuda disprezzo. S’inventa un interlocutore di sinistra (“ignorante di economia”, ovviamente) facendo la vocina infantile, e risponde facendo la voce autorevole e spiegando quella che nella sua testa passa per “economia”, tutto quel genere di argomenti mediocri e prevedibili tipici di Thomas Sowell.


Inizia col classico cliché di destra: “non è capitalismo, è aziendalismo!” (o “capitalismo clientelare”):


Se non apprezzate il capitalismo è perché non sapete cos’è…


Molti di quelli che accusano il capitalismo parlano praticamente di aziendalismo delle grandi società che sfruttano la forza dello stato per ottenere favoritismi e arricchirsi e rubare risorse da altri paesi e tutto il resto. Questo, soprattutto nell’informazione tradizionale, è ciò che passa per capitalismo. Se siete contro, tutto bene, anch’io, perché lo stato che li favorisce significa costrizione.


E subito, senza sosta, passa a dire che dobbiamo ringraziare il “capitalismo” per quasi tutta la tecnologia che abbiamo.


Voi mi ascoltate perché esiste il capitalismo. Lo schermo che avete davanti esiste solo grazie al capitalismo. I cavi che lo collegano esistono solo perché esiste il capitalismo. E anche l’elettricità che passa nei cavi e tutto il resto, tutto quello che è in questa stanza, in questo palazzo.


E però alla base del modello di profitto aziendale che produce tutte quelle cose ci sono le connessioni con lo stato. Microelettronica, cibernetica e infrastrutture delle telecomunicazioni sono il prodotto delle ricerca finanziata dallo stato, soprattutto a fini militari, e dipendono fortemente dai brevetti; quello che Rose chiama “capitalismo clientelare”, insomma. Ma sono

anche

 esempi dei benefici del capitalismo. Che immagino sia come il gatto di Schrödinger. Sembra che il tipo non riesca a dire due frasi di seguito senza contraddirsi.


Il concetto di elettronica secondo Rose (che esiste grazie a un “capitalismo” che non comporta lo stato) non è lo stesso di chi ha qualche nozione di storia industriale. La cosa non si discute neanche. Il ruolo dello stato nello sviluppo dell’industria tecnologica è stato descritto bene da David Nobe in

America by Design

. Lo sviluppo della cibernetica, della microelettronica e di quella che sarà l’ossatura di internet sono frutto della ricerca del dipartimento della difesa.


Ad onor del vero, Rose condivide l’errore logico praticamente con tutti i polemisti di destra. Tutti dicono che le attività che fanno profitti grazie ad aiuti o protezionismi statali o grazie alla proprietà artificiale non sono “capitalismo reale”; dopodiché fanno dietrofront e celebrano come “

merito del capitalismo

” prodotti come l’iPhone, inventato da un’azienda il cui modello di profitto dipende dalla proprietà intellettuale, gli aiuti di stato e una politica estera neoliberale.


Rose non fa che ripetere tutto un miscuglio di argomenti della destra libertaria sull’imprescindibilità del capitalista. Se esiste la tecnologia complessa, o anche solo un’esistenza appena migliore di quella dei cavernicoli, spiega…


ecco che subito qualcuno il dito contro [fa la vocina di bambino arrabbiato] l’azienda miliardaria cattiva come il cattivo del film che inquina l’ambiente ed è prepotente e ingordo [fine della vocina], ma la realtà è che qualcuno ha qualcosa che tu non hai e può usarla per fare cose come questo computer, ad esempio, o il monitor o la videocamera che mi riprende. Come pensate che si possano fare queste cose o anche un microchip senza la megafabbrica che fa microchip per computer?


* * *


Pensate a quello che non avreste se non ci …

author: Sara Connors
title: Advocates suspect rise in overdoses in Whitehorse linked to new synthetic opioid
content:
Harm reduction and public health advocates are raising the alarm over an emerging synthetic opioid they believe is likely linked to an increase in overdoses in Whitehorse.


Cychlorphine is a highly potent synthetic opioid up to 10 times stronger than fentanyl and tied to a growing number of overdose deaths in the United States.


The drug was detected in British Columbia’s toxic illicit drug trade in June, and has also been identified in other jurisdictions like Newfoundland and Labrador and Quebec.


Jill Aalhus, executive director of Whitehorse-based harm reduction non-profit

Blood Ties

, said it’s likely the drug is behind a recent surge of intense, rapid on-set overdoses.


“It is a concern, particularly when we see that severity of overdose happening in the community,” Aalhus said.


She said side effects of cychlorphine can include nausea and vomiting, which can cause airway complications during an overdose.


“With the unpredictable and unregulated supply, people don’t know what they’re getting in their sample,” she said. “They don’t know usually what substance is in there, and so if they’re expecting to be using fentanyl, and something like cychlorphine shows up that is significantly more potent, that can significantly increase the likelihood of an overdose.”


Often mixed with other drugs, cychlorphine can be difficult to detect on routine fentanyl testing strips.


Aalhus said that’s because it often only appears in small quantities and no immunoassay testing strips exist for it yet.


She also noted it’s not yet clear how cychlorphine reacts to naloxone, though those responding to an overdose are still encouraged to administer it.


Despite the uncertainty surrounding cychlorphine, Aalhus said no fatal overdoses have occurred at the territory’s supervised consumption site.


“It’s too early to know sort the scope and scale of it’s impact on the territory,” she said. “But we are very concerned.”


Public health non-profit

One Yukon Coalition

 first detected cychlorphine in Whitehorse’s wastewater earlier this summer.


The organization uses wastewater sampling to test for a variety of pathogens and chemical substances to help inform public health partners.


“Sadly, as soon as we started testing for it, we started detecting it, and it has been present in all of the wastewater samples so far since June,” said Carolina Koutras, a health researcher and chief operating officer for One Yukon.


Koutras said the organization began testing for cychlorphine following global drug trends in places like Europe and the U.S.


She said she was surprised to see the drug had arrived in the Yukon, noting it’s only been found in a few places in Canada.


Koutras said while it’s impossible to say with certainty why the drug is appearing in Whitehorse, she suspects the city’s geographic location and the fact it intersects with the Alaska highway might have something to do with it.


“It connects the United States and the rest of Canada. It’s a major route, and that’s interesting,” she said. “It’s the same pattern that we see with other jurisdictions in Europe, for example, where there are port cities.”


She also noted it’s possible cychlorphine may be in the territory’s rural communities, but the organization is unable to test outside of Whitehorse due to a lack of federal funding.


Beyond cychlorphine, she noted other opioids of concern have been detected in Whitehorse’s wastewater, including para-fluorofentanyl, a potent synthetic opioid, and 7-hydroxymitragynine, commonly known as 7-OH, an opioid-like alkaloid associated with kratom.


Koutras said 7-OH has been detected in all wastewater samples since testing for it began, and that One Yukon has filed a formal complaint with Health Canada concerning its availability.


“It cannot normally be sold to the public, but it is very accessible and can be delivered through Canada Post, according to our research,” she said. “We find that very concerning.”


Aalhus said people who use drugs can reduce their chances of overdose and death by not using alone and carrying a naloxone kit.


“Overdoses are preventable deaths,” she said. “We have strategies that are very evidence-based that we know work.


The post

Advocates suspect rise in overdoses in Whitehorse linked to new synthetic opioid

 appeared first on

APTN News

.

title: Agenda cultural: primera semana de septiembre
content:
Hoy comienza el festival en el CAFF, donde se presentan las mejores bandas de Tango. Y hasta el 06 de septiembre continúa el de la Revista Llegás, con más de 500 artistas y 50 funciones a mitad de precio. Hay mucho para ver, gratuito o a precios módicos. 

No dejes de recorrer nuestra agenda, hay mucho para ver, pensar, disfrutar. Elegí compartir cultura. Si tenes propuestas, podés enviarlas a nuestor mail: culturasanred@gmail.com. Revisamos la casilla hasta el lunes previo a la publicación.

Por ANRed.


Jueves 03


FACAFF. 

Octava edición del multitudinario encuentro donde

más de veinte agrupaciones ofrecen una mirada auténtica e innovadora del tango actual

.  Va del jueves 03 al domingo 27 de septiembre en el Club Atlético Fernández Fierro (CAFF), Bustamante 772, CABA. Entradas populares en efectivo en boletería del club o por PlanOut.

Jubiladxs entrada sin cargo y promoción 2×1 para estudiantes.

Acá, toda la programación que necesitás para no perderte nada de este Festival increíble:

www.caff.ar


9° Edición del Festival Llegás.

Este año reunirá más de

50 obras de la cartelera teatral

 de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires con entradas a mitad de precio. Durante una semana, 

más de 500 artistas

 participarán de una programación que se desplegará en 10 salas de la Ciudad para celebrar el encuentro entre artistas, obras y espectadores. En esta edición, el Festival incorpora clases magistrales, actividades especiales, un circuito de obras en espacios no convencionales, espectáculos invitados y producciones seleccionadas mediante convocatoria, además de una amplia selección de propuestas del circuito comercial.

Todas las funciones tendrán entradas a mitad de precio, con el objetivo de ampliar el acceso a las artes escénicas.

 El Festival Llegás es una iniciativa de Revista Llegás, coproducida junto a LEM Asociación Civil, que busca visibilizar las artes escénicas, promover el trabajo interdisciplinario y fortalecer la gestión del arte en la sociedad. «El festival no es el fin: el festival es un medio para generar encuentro. Las obras nos convocan, pero lo que permanece es el encuentro. Queremos compartir una experiencia que nos cambie. Lxs esperamos en esta novena edición del Festival Llegás con el mismo espíritu festivo de siempre. La cultura nos encuentra», expresan Ricardo Tamburrano y Melina Seldes, directores y curadores del festival. Las entradas ya están a la venta en el sitio web oficial del Festival Llegás. Allí puede consultarse la programación completa, los horarios, las sedes y

toda la información sobre esta novena edición:

 

www.festival-llegas.com.ar

.

Del 31 de agosto al 6 de septiembre

saca su nuevo single: “Le Pertenezco a Sus Ojos”, con el que abre los festejos por los 25 años de “A Los Que Se Han Apagado”, disco bisagra de la banda. Con más de 30 años de trayectoria ininterrumpida, Eterna Inocencia es

una de las bandas más importantes del hardcore punk latinoamericano

. Integrada por Guillermo Marmol (voz), Roy Ota (guitarra), Alejandro Navajas (bajo), Tomás Portela (guitarra) y Germán Rodríguez (batería), combina melodías con

letras de contenido social

 desde la ética del Do It Yourself y la autogestión. Con nueve discos de estudio, un disco en vivo y un DVD, giró por Chile, Uruguay, Perú, Colombia, Ecuador, España, Francia, Suiza y Brasil, y hoy atraviesa uno de sus mejores momentos, celebrando los 25 años de su álbum

A Los Que Se Han Apagado

.


Viernes 04


Mala Madre. 

Una obra documental sobre maternidad, duelo y deseo. Relato de una madre que atravesada por la muerte temprana de su hermano, revisa su historia personal para poner en crisis los mandatos, culpas y contradicciones que rodean a la maternidad. A partir de su historia personal y de material audiovisual registrado durante años, la pieza indaga en las zonas menos idealizadas de maternar. Laa obra abre una conversación íntima y colectiva. Protagonizada por la multipremiada actriz 

Raquel Ameri

 y con dirección de 

Paola Luttini.

Se estrena el viernes 4 de septiembre 22.30 HS en Nün Teatro Bar (Juan Ramírez de Velasco, 419, CABA).

Entradas por Alternativa.


Alabanza

. Una performance audiovisual que explora los estados físicos y emocionales del ciclo menstrual. Una investigación escénica que tensiona lo íntimo y lo colectivo, donde los cuerpos se transforman, se expanden, se repliegan y vuelve a comenzar, reivindicando sus naturalezas cíclicas como forma de existencia, percepción y potencia …

title: Lanzan campaña por el sobreseimiento de 19 manifestantes llevados a juicio por participar del “Jujeñazo”
content:
A tres años del “Jujeñazo”, 19 de sus protagonistas serán llevados a juicio en una causa que comenzará el 26 de octubre y se extenderá durante diez jornadas, hasta el 6 de noviembre. Organizaciones de derechos humanos, sindicales, sociales y políticas, comunidades originarias y personalidades lanzaron un llamamiento nacional para exigir su absolución y sobreseimiento y denunciar un nuevo avance de la criminalización de la protesta social. “No puede haber una Justicia para quienes lucharon y otra para quienes ejercían el poder y dieron órdenes ilegítimas”, remarca el llamamiento, que reclama además investigar e imputar a los funcionarios implicados en la represión. “Abajo la reforma, arriba los salarios” fue la consigna que sintetizó el “Jujeñazo” de junio de 2023, una masiva movilización que reunió el reclamo de docentes y estatales por salarios con la defensa de los territorios de las comunidades originarias y el rechazo a la reforma constitucional impulsada por Gerardo Morales, y que tuvo como respuesta una brutal represión que dejó más de cien personas detenidas, numerosas heridas y manifestantes con gravísimas lesiones.


La represión en Jujuy en 2023 ante el rechazo a la reforma constitucional. Foto: Guillermo Castro


A tres años del “Jujeñazo”, 19 de sus protagonistas serán llevados a juicio, en una causa cuyo debate comenzará el próximo lunes 26 de octubre y se extenderá durante diez jornadas, hasta el viernes 6 de noviembre. Ante esta situación, organismos de derechos humanos, organizaciones sindicales, sociales y políticas, comunidades originarias y personalidades lanzaron un llamamiento nacional para exigir el sobreseimiento y la absolución de quienes son perseguidos judicialmente, y cuyo petitorio se puede firmar aquí:

https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfkb1m0Gx_iOMImsl7g7HnbDYy94smyilmGIW9gKWGCxzre6A/viewform


La consigna “Abajo la reforma, arriba los salarios” fue la consigna que sintetizó las jornadas de junio de 2023, cuando la lucha de docentes y trabajadores estatales por salarios confluyó con la resistencia de las comunidades originarias en defensa de sus territorios y con el rechazo de organizaciones sindicales, sociales y políticas a la reforma constitucional impulsada por Gerardo Morales. Según el llamamiento, aquella movilización “arrancó uno de los aumentos salariales más importantes para los estatales jujeños y puso en jaque al gobierno provincial”.


Imagen: Originarios.ar


La respuesta del gobierno de Morales en ese momento fue una fuerte represión, recuerda el documento del llamamiento: “una brutal represión, con detenidos, numerosos heridos y manifestantes que sufrieron gravísimas lesiones, entre ellas pérdida de visión. Mas de 100 detenciones que luego derivaron en libertades y sobreseimientos”. Aquel año, organizaciones de derechos humanos y organismos antirrepresivos también documentaron detenciones irregulares, el uso desproporcionado de la fuerza y lesiones graves durante aquellos operativos.


La persecución judicial, sin embargo, continuó después de la represión porque, tres años más tarde, 19 personas que participaron de aquellas protestas son llevadas hoy a juicio. El proceso está atravesado, denuncian desde el llamamiento, por “graves cuestionamientos de las defensas respecto del derecho de defensa, el debido proceso y la imparcialidad judicial”. Además, se cuestiona el modo en que fue fijada la audiencia: “el 21 de agosto de 2026 fue rechazado el pedido de no fijar audiencia y apenas seis días después, con quejas en trámite, el 27 de agosto, se notificó un debate de enorme magnitud concentrado en diez jornadas”.


Mientras se acelera el proceso contra quienes participaron de la movilización, las organizaciones reclaman que la Justicia avance sobre quienes ordenaron la represión: “seguimos reclamando que se investiguen las responsabilidades políticas y penales por la represión de junio de 2023, que dejó manifestantes con gravísimas lesiones, y que se avance también en la causa de Caspalá, donde se debate sobre el territorio de la Comunidad Originaria y la corrupción de los funcionarios del gobierno provincial”. Así, la campaña por el sobreseimiento de quienes participaron de la pueblada del “Jujeñazo” vuelve así a inscribirse en una disputa más amplia por el territorio, los recursos naturales y el derecho a protestar.


Asimismo, el juicio que comenzará en octubre no es solamente el capítulo judicial de una protesta ocurrida tres años atrás. Para las organizaciones …

author: Darío Aranda
title: El Niño despertó: lluvias extremas y olas de calor para un planeta en crisis climática
content:
Por Silvia Oliviero Ghietto*


La Organización Meteorológica Mundial (OMM) emitió un comunicado en el que advirtió que el fenómeno climático El Niño, que ya está en marcha, puede alcanzar una intensidad mayor que la habitual. En Argentina, a partir de noviembre-diciembre, aumenta la posibilidad de que ocurran

eventos de precipitaciones extremas en la Cuenca del Plata

 (integrada por Corrientes, Misiones, Formosa, Santa Fe, Entre Ríos, Buenos Aires, Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires y Chaco)

y en el Noroeste de la Patagonia

.


El Niño continúa intensificándose de forma constante combinado con océanos globales excepcionalmente cálidos y la probabilidad de un dipolo positivo en el Océano Índico, lo que determina una

probabilidad

de casi el 100 por ciento

 de un evento “muy fuerte”

. Por lo tanto, se espera que domine los patrones climáticos globales durante la temporada 2026-2027, con

aumento de probabilidad de temperaturas superiores a lo normal

 en gran parte del mundo y con cambios significativos en los patrones de lluvia, segúnel

C

entro de Predicción Climática de la Administración Nacional Oceánica y Atmosférica de Estados Unidos.


Las proyecciones científicas actuales sugieren que este El Niño podría convertirse en un evento comparable con algunos de los episodios más impactantes de las últimas décadas superando incluso el ocurrido en 1998. Los eventos de El Niño suelen alcanzar su punto máximo hacia finales del año, con la máxima influencia que suele sentirse entre noviembre y febrero.


Vale la pena aclarar que la Organización Meteorológica Mundial y las Instituciones de Referencia Climática clasifican los eventos de la Oscilación El Niño-Sur (ENSO) como débiles, moderados, fuertes o muy fuertes. Por lo tanto, el término "súper El Niño" utilizado por los medios de comunicación no forma parte del sistema de clasificación operativo y oficial.


Infografía: Organización Meteorológica Mundial


¿Que sabemos del fenómeno del Niño?


El Niño y La Niña son fases opuestas de

un patrón climático natural

 conocido como la Oscilación El Niño-Sur (ENSO), que

implica fluctuaciones de las temperaturas oceánicas en el Pacífico ecuatorial central y oriental, junto con cambios en la atmósfera

 suprayacente. Cuando la “Circulación Walker” (un flujo masivo de aire de este a oeste impulsado por las diferencias de temperatura y presión entre los océanos cálido occidental y el frío del este) se modifica desplazándose hacia el este en dirección a Sudamérica y la temperatura oceánica supera los 0,5 °C, se declara El Niño.


La transición entre estas fases extremas suele ocurrir cada dos a siete años. Tanto El Niño como La Niña generalmente comienzan a desarrollarse entre marzo y junio y alcanzan su máxima intensidad entre noviembre y febrero.


El Niño se caracteriza por temperaturas superficiales oceánicas inusualmente cálidas en el Pacífico

 central y oriental.

El nombre proviene de pescadores y marineros peruanos que notaron una corriente cálida

, asociada a la reducción de capturas de pescado, y la llamaron El Niño (probablemente porque se hacía visible en torno a Navidad).


El Niño se predice mediante el monitoreo de las condiciones en el océano Pacífico tropical. A través de modelos climáticos, la comunidad científica puede estimar cómo puede evolucionar en los próximos meses y

predecir patrones climáticos con seis meses de anticipación

. Se basa en una red global de observaciones, incluidos satélites, buques de océano, barcos de investigación y medidas atmosféricas operadas por los Servicios Meteorológicos y Hidrológicos Nacionales y Organizaciones Internacionales.


Desde la década de 1980, el enfoque dominante para medir o identificar El Niño ha sido el uso del Índice Oceánico Niño (ONI), que calcula a lo largo de un promedio de tres meses la Anomalía de Temperatura Superficial del Mar en una región específica del Pacífico llamada región Niño. En los últimos años y con la presencia del calentamiento global, una métrica más reciente llamada Índice Relativo Oceánico Niño (RONI) ha ganado terreno. Este enfoque mide el calentamiento relativo, no solo el absoluto, ayudando a la comunidad científica a evaluar si un evento de calentamiento está impulsado por el ENSO o se debe principalmente al calentamiento global oceánico.


La OMM indica que, según las proyecciones de la Oficina Nacional de Administración Oceánica y Atmosférica (NOAA) de Estados Unidos y el Programa Copernicus de la Unión Europea,

author: A.N.A.
title: Sou a Anarquia!!!
content:
Nasci com a primeira revolta insubmissa, inquieta, desgrenhada. Construí a mim mesma desnuda, bela, irreverente. Desde meus ossos inermes partiu a primeira blasfêmia ao criador… Neguei-me a ser submetida, dirigida, apadrinhada. Transformei-me em apóstata, fui acusada de irreligiosidade. Fui condenada, mas minhas asas eram de fênix, e rapidamente abandonei as fogueiras e atravessei os oceanos… Vi jugos em todo lugar, dores e fome, discursos e lamentos, aprendi o desespero. Cavei com as unhas uma trincheira de sonhos e me embriaguei com esse bando de jovens loucos, poetas náufragos de volta à Espanha de trinta e seis… Olhei à esquerda, olhei à direita e vi rostos sujos escondidos atrás de limpos uniformes vertendo o sangue dos povos em nome da justiça, da dialética e outras quintessências enjoativas… E peguei a raiva e afiei-a e lancei raios contra os tronos, inimiga dos governos, inimiga das pátrias, inimiga da dor. Abraço o mundo, vivo e não imploro, amo e resisto suas tiranias.


Sou a Anarquia!!!


(Anônimo)

author: Andrés
title: A un año de la muerte de Octavio Buccafusco, en manos de la policía
content:
El 3 de septiembre de 2025 murió asfixiado Octavio Buccafusco, luego de una intervención arbitr

aria,

 desproporcionada y violenta de la Patrulla Municipal de Vicente López. Las cámaras de la vía pública muestran el registro casi completo, desde que detienen a la víctima con su caniche en brazos hasta cuando los efectivos, operando como una patota lo tiran al piso y lo aplastan, entre tres, contra el cordón. Luego de dejarlo en el piso

 sin signos vitales, tardan varios minutos en llamar a la ambulancia

. Se cumple un año y los oficiales no recibieron condena. Texto y fotos p

or @citruspressok para ANRed.


El 3 de septiembre de 2025, murió Octavio Buccafusco en manos de los integrantes de la Patrulla Municipal de @solemartinez, Yamila Flores, Gustavo Acosta y Eduardo Jaime (familiar del actual Concejal del Pro, José Jaime) y el efectivo de la bonaerense, Maximiliano Maguayar.


Según el informe pericial aportado por uno de los querellantes de la causa, la Comision Provincial por la Memoria, y firmado por el médico legalista Marcelo Nenkies, Buccafusco murió como consecuencia de una asfixia por sofocación posicional relacionada directamente con la intervención de los tres patrulleros y el policía bonaerense.


Sin embargo, Alejandro Adrián Guevara, fiscal de San Isidro, calificó el hecho, después de una demora de 10 meses, como “homicidio culposo en concurso ideal con severidades”.


¿Y qué quiere decir esto? Que para el Fiscal Guevara los empleados municipales y el efectivo de la policía no tuvieron intención de matar a Octavio.


Si la intención no era matarlo, ¿por qué lo aplastaron entre cuatro personas, y presionaron hasta que dejó de respirar?


¿Y por qué llamaron al Same varios minutos después de que Octavio, tirado en el cordón de la vereda, no reaccionara ni registrara signos vitales? ¿Y por qué ante esa evidencia ninguno intentó reanimarlo?


El hecho es que Octavio está muerto. Su familia, sus hijas y vecinos merecen justicia.


Por la memoria de Octavio y para que los procedimientos policiales dejen de operar como patotas violentas, haciendo gala del abuso de poder y se ciñan a estrictos protocolos.


@justiciaxoctavio

author: Duda Sousa
title: Contando com memória curta do brasileiro, candidatos ora cassados voltam às urnas em 2026
content:
Investigamos o que importa para os brasileiros além do que passa na campanha eleitoral. Leia mais reportagens como essa clicando

aqui

.


Vinte e dois anos depois de perder o mandato de deputado distrital, Carlos Pereira Xavier (DC-DF) está novamente pedindo votos no Distrito Federal. Em 2004, ele foi cassado pela Câmara Legislativa em meio a acusações de envolvimento na morte de Ewerton da Rocha Ferreira, um adolescente de 16 anos.

Segundo a acusação, Xavier teria encomendado a dois executores a morte do garoto, apontado como amante de sua então esposa. Xavier foi condenado a 15 anos de prisão por homicídio

, mas a sentença foi anulada em 2024 após revisão criminal. Ele nega ter sido o mandante do assassinato. E agora tenta voltar à Câmara Distrital.


Agora, filiado ao Democracia Cristã, Xavier disputa novamente uma vaga de deputado distrital enquanto o processo criminal continua em aberto. O caso reúne duas histórias que, embora relacionadas, têm consequências jurídicas diferentes: a perda do mandato parlamentar e o processo criminal. A cassação interrompeu sua trajetória na Câmara Legislativa, mas não impediu que ele voltasse a disputar eleições décadas depois. Já a situação criminal segue sendo discutida nos tribunais.


Em declaração sobre o processo para a

Rádio Metrópoles

, em junho deste ano,  Xavier afirmou que: “Para mim, que sou criado na igreja, a vida quem dá é Deus e só ele tem o dever e o poder de tirar, mais ninguém.” Um novo julgamento pelo Tribunal do Júri está marcado para 9 de setembro deste ano.

A direção nacional do Democracia Cristã informou à reportagem que não possui, até o momento, posição oficial sobre a continuação da candidatura de Xavier e que a situação será avaliada diante do novo julgamento.


Deputado distrital Carlos Pereira Xavier (DC-DF) foi cassado em 2004 por acusações de envolvimento em assassinato


“Não há necessidade de que exista uma ação criminal pelo motivo qualquer que tenha levado a essa cassação”, explica o especialista em direito eleitoral Fernando Neisser. Segundo ele, uma cassação por quebra de decoro pode acontecer mesmo quando não há crime investigado. “Não há necessidade de que exista uma ação criminal pelo motivo qualquer que tenha levado a essa cassação”, explica Neisser. A existência de uma punição eleitoral, portanto, não significa necessariamente que exista uma condenação criminal – que também não teria consequências automáticas na situação eleitoral.


O fato de Xavier estar apto a disputar uma eleição não significa que a acusação criminal tenha desaparecido. Da mesma forma, o processo criminal não reabre automaticamente a cassação ocorrida há mais de 20 anos. São situações que precisam ser analisadas separadamente pela Justiça.


Antes da cassação, Xavier também construiu uma trajetória política ligada à comunidade evangélica do Distrito Federal. Ele foi responsável pelo projeto que deu origem à lei que instituiu o Dia do Evangélico no Distrito Federal

, celebrado em 30 de novembro. A data passou a integrar o calendário oficial do Distrito Federal e permanece como parte do legado político associado ao ex-deputado.


A trajetória de Xavier não é caso isolado. Em 2026, outros políticos que perderam mandatos, tiveram registros de candidatura cassados ou foram alvo de decisões eleitorais que interromperam suas trajetórias voltam a buscar espaço nas urnas. As situações jurídicas são diferentes: em alguns casos, a punição terminou; em outros, uma decisão foi revertida ou modificada; há ainda quem tenha conseguido autorização judicial para disputar a eleição enquanto a discussão continua. 


Romano e Luana foram sequestrados em 2020. Jalser Renier foi apontado como suposto mandante do crime


Sequestro, quebra de decoro e volta às urnas


O casal de jornalistas Romano dos Anjos e Luana Leão foi sequestrado dentro de casa em outubro de 2020. Romano, que havia publicado reportagens e denúncias sobre problemas em Roraima, foi posteriormente encontrado com lesões e múltiplas fraturas.

 As investigações apontaram o então deputado estadual Jalser Renier, à época filiado ao Solidariedade, como suposto mandante do crime.

 Policiais militares também foram investigados e denunciados por participação no caso.


A investigação levou à identificação de uma possível estrutura criminosa envolvendo agentes públicos e pessoas ligadas à Assembleia Legislativa de Roraima (ALE-RR). Jalser, que naquele período ocupava posição de destaque na política estadual, teve o …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Endeudamiento familiar: la oposición en Diputados ratificó la sesión del miércoles 9
content:
Así lo determinaron legisladores y legisladoras en la reunión de la Comisión de Finanzas convocada por La Libertad Avanza en la que participaron como expositores varios especialistas afines al gobierno.


El oficialismo planteó un cronograma de reuniones hasta el 30 de septiembre pero la intención de los bloques de oposición es sesionar el miércoles que viene y aprobar el emplazamiento a las comisiones con un nuevo cronograma para arribar a un proyecto unificado y luego a una nueva sesión para conseguir la media sanción.


El presidente de la Comisión de Finanzas, Santiago Pauli. Foto: @DiputadosAR


El diputado de Provincias Unidas Pablo Juliano, se expresó al respecto:


Se tiene que dar una agenda seria para poder tratar un tema que se lleva puesto la realidad diaria, diaria y cuando digo diaria es diaria. No nos podemos dar tres meses, seis meses para tratar este tema de un montón de argentinos que están angustiados y no se empeñaron por diversión o porque no vieron que la tasa de mercado libre era tanto por ciento. Se empeñaron porque no llegan a fin de mes.


No le tomen el pelo a la gente que está empeñada


El espíritu de la sesión del 9 de septiembre está intacto. Está claro que el tema del sobreendeudamiento no tiene dueño y que requiere coordinación y una respuesta. Pero hay una urgencia que es transversal. Es difícil no pensar…

pic.twitter.com/XFQOFmDs1N


— Pablo Juliano (@PabloJulianoLP)

September 2, 2026


Por su parte, la diputada del Frente de Izquierda Miriam Bregman, dijo que hay una emergencia por el sobreendeudamiento familiar y ratificó la sesión del miércoles: “Que vengan ahora con un cronograma que llega hasta navidad resulta insólito, señor presidente; hay una emergencia, 20 millones de endeudados, es urgente declarar la emergencia, urgente determinar que no se puede continuar con las ejecuciones, urgente investigar la usura y mientras tanto no se puede cobrar absolutamente nada y después de eso vamos a empezar a discutir los proyectos”.


Son 133 los diputados y diputadas de distintos bloques que acordaron convocar a la sesión del miércoles. Con ese número está garantizado el quórum y los votos para aprobar el emplazamiento. El otro tema con el que se intentará avanzar en esa sesión es la prórroga de la emergencia en discapacidad hasta diciembre de 2027.

content:

Su trabajo de autodefensa digital, consiste en dar servicios de cuentas de correos electrónicos y blogs, de manera anónima y segura. title: 249 people killed in Syria in eight months
content:
According to information provided by the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights, 249 people (9 women, 92 children and 148 men) have been killed in Syria since the beginning of the year due to explosions of war remnants. Another 388 people were injured.

In other areas under the control of the interim government, 228 people were killed and 368 were injured.

In the regions of North and East Syria, 21 people were killed and 20 were injured as a result of explosions involving war remnants.

author: Menchani Tilendo
title: Kasibu people stand their ground
content:
The mountains are not simply places where minerals can be extracted.


KASIBU, Nueva Vizcaya — For nearly four months, Indigenous Peoples and farmers in Barangay Paquet, Kasibu, Nueva Vizcaya have maintained a barricade against the entry of North Luzon Mineral Resources Corporation (NLMRC) which seeks to conduct large-scale mining exploration in their mountains.


Leading the barricade is Kasibu Inter-Tribal Response Ecological Development (KIRED), a local organization founded in 2007 out of the community’s long struggle against mining. Its historic fight began when Australian mining firm Royalco Resources Ltd., through its subsidiary Royalco Philippines Inc., started mineral exploration in the area despite opposition from local communities. According to community leaders, NLMRC is now the seventh mining company to attempt exploration in their area without the community’s free, prior, and informed consent (FPIC) or genuine consultation.


Together with local organization Alyansa ng Novo Vizcayano para sa Kalikasan (ANVIK), KIRED keeps the barricade every day, sustained by donations and solidarity from various people’s organizations, NGOs, and nearby communities in Nueva Vizcaya and beyond.


On August 28, 11 people were arrested when police moved to clear the barricade which served to prevent fuel from entering the area for NLMRC’s exploration activities. They were charged with grave coercion, as well as resistance and disobedience. The residents were later released on bail after four days.


For the people of Kasibu, the mountains are not simply places where minerals can be extracted. They are home, livelihood, and life itself.


Aside from being rich in significant gold and copper deposits, Kasibu is known as the Citrus Capital of the Philippines, with farmers also cultivating dragon fruit and other crops. It is also home to an 18,417-hectare protected forest and watershed.


For farmers, one failed harvest can mean losses of P25,000 ($399) to P150,000 ($2,340) in a single cropping cycle, on top of already high production costs, particularly for fertilizers. Mining-related contamination of soil and water could make an already difficult livelihood even harder.


They also fear landslides, worsening droughts and floods, and the environmental damage associated with open-pit mining as these operations continue to expand.


Kasibu already has active Financial and Technical Assistance Agreements (FTAAs) or government contracts that allow foreign-owned mining companies to explore and develop mineral resources, including those involving FCF Minerals and OceanaGold. Meanwhile, 15 more exploration permit applications are reportedly ongoing.


For community leaders, NLMRC’s entry is another attempt to push mining into their ancestral lands, undermining the consent and consultation to which they have a right.


The barricade is not always a scene of confrontation. What proves to be fundamental is why they are forced to resist in the first place.


The barricade is their line of defense for their ancestral land, their livelihood, their environment, and their basic right to live with dignity.

 (CAM, DAA)


Kasibu residents set up a makeshift checkpoint to monitor NLRMC personnel and police forces entering the community amid the mining exploration threat.


A large tarpaulin at the Kasibu barricade declares the community’s land as private property.


Ka Donny, a landowner in Brgy. Paquet, Kasibu, leads a community meeting at the barricade opposing the proposed mining site.


Barricade members gather to hear updates from community leaders during their regular meetings.


Bugcalot tribe chieftain Ka Maddela shows a map of NLRMC’s proposed exploration, saying he makes sure the community understands how the mining operations will be carried out.


Ka Maddela says he always carries printed copies of the community’s land titles and resolutions opposing NLRMC’s mining exploration.


Kasibu is known as the Citrus Capital of the Philippines, with local varieties of citrus often served fresh alongside everyday meals.


Clean, free-flowing water is a staple in Kasibu, home to critical sub-watersheds that feed the Cagayan Valley’s headwaters.


Kasibu’s forests and watersheds sustain diverse crops, but farmers can lose P25,000–P150,000 per harvest cycle due to high production costs with soil and water contamination adding to their burden.

author: Brian Hioe
title: Chinese Government Forces Artists to Withdraw from the Gwangju Biennale
content:
THE CHINESE GOVERNMENT has forced the withdrawal of Chinese artists from the Gwangju Biennale. This took place after the Gwangju Biennale reversed course on its decision to force Taiwanese artists to participate under the name “NTMOFA”, rather than as the “Taiwan Pavilion”, as they were originally supposed to.

As organized by the National Taiwan Museum of Fine Arts, that the Taiwanese artists were to participate as the “Taiwan Pavilion” was agreed on beforehand with organizers. Taiwanese artists had participated in the 2025 Gwangju Design Biennale under the name “Taiwan Pavilion” without incident.

Nevertheless, promotional images released by the Gwangju Biennale on its website instead censored any mention of Taiwan, so as to refer to the artists as displaying under “NTMOFA.” NTMOFA is an abbreviation of the National Taiwan Museum of Five Arts.

In response, ten Taiwanese artists and curators released a statement criticizing the Gwangju Biennale. The artists stated that efforts to negotiate with the Gwangju Biennale were ignored, and criticized what was termed “political censorship.”

Afterward, a group of South Korean artists, who referred to themselves as “Artists Against Censorship,” released their own statement. This statement criticized the actions of the Biennale, particularly as the Biennale was formed as a response to the 1980 Gwangju Uprising, which opposed the military dictatorship of Chun Doo-hwan. As such, the statement emphasized that it was “disheartening to learn that such political censorship is being carried out in Gwangju, which is called the ‘hometown of Korean democracy.’”

The statement by Artists Against Censorship hit out at artistic censorship as a whole. The statement reads, “[I]n today’s international art world, artworks are being unilaterally altered or removed, exhibitions and speeches are being canceled, and artists and cultural workers are being forced into silence based on discriminatory and exclusionary perceptions of their nationality, race, gender, religion, and political stance. In particular, in a situation where the political and diplomatic pressures and economic influence of some countries unfairly interfere with the realm of cultural arts, the Biennale has the duty to […] to ensure the autonomy of exhibitions and creations.”

It proves disappointing, then, that the response from the Chinese government has been to instead punish Chinese artists by forcing them to withdraw from the exhibition–so as to pin the blame on Taiwanese artists for standing up for themselves. This would not be the first time that this has occurred.

In 2018, when the documentary Our Youth in Taiwan–which depicted the 2014 Sunflower Movement–won the Golden Horse Award for Best Documentary, the response from Chinese authorities was similar. Chinese participants in the award ceremony were forced to immediately depart. In the years to come, Chinese filmmakers were banned by their government from participating in the Golden Horse Awards.

It can be seen, then, that the Chinese government has a history of punishing its own artists as a way to hit back at Taiwan, depriving them of opportunities and forcing them to withdraw from international events that they are participating in. This more broadly reflects the Chinese government’s views of artists, seeing them as its property, and forcing them to comply with its will whenever it wishes to express geopolitical angst.

author: groundxero
title: The Next Election May be Our Last
content:
Donald Trump is determined to subvert the midterms. All that can save us, if he succeeds, is a national strike.


 


CHRIS HEDGES


Aug 31, 2026


 


The Trump White House has put into place a series of mechanisms to fix or invalidate the midterm elections. Congress will not save us. The courts will not save us. Our only hope — should the election be rigged or stolen — is nationwide strikes. Our only hope is to cripple the machinery of commerce and government, although this militancy will be met with savage state repression.


 


Otherwise, we are doomed. There will be no exit.


 


If the measures advocated by the Trump administration are implemented, 

emergency powers

 will be invoked to assert unprecedented federal control over voting. Federal agents will seize election materials. They have already 

seized

 ballots from previous elections.


 


The U.S. Postal Service will only send ballots to those 

included

 on federally approved eligibility lists drawn from state voter rolls. These rolls, subject to citizenship checks, will 

deny

 election-mail services entirely in states that 

refuse

 the administration’s demands for voter data.


 


Trump-

backed

 mid-decade 

gerrymandering

 has already dismantled Democratic-held districts and created new ones for the Republican.


 


Federal ID and citizenship-document requirements will disenfranchise 

millions

 of eligible voters, including lower-income Americans who lack access to the required documents and married women whose current names do not match those on their citizenship records.


 


Federal troops and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) — with $113.5 billion in additional funding 

allocated

 by Congress through September 2029 — will be deployed to or near polling stations which have a traditional Democratic Party majority. Those branded as “anti-capitalist” and “anti-Christian” or charged with belonging to 

antifa

 will be intimidated or blocked from voting.


 


The Republican majority in the House — regardless of the vote — will use its authority to certify election results to retain power, gaming the Electoral College and refusing to seat newly elected members of the opposition.


 


Overseeing the massive election fraud will be 

loyalists

 seeded by the Trump administration across state and federal election offices.


 


Trump — who attempted to overturn the 2020 election results and said he would 

refuse

 to accept the outcome of the 2024 election if he lost — 

ruminates

 about defying the Constitution in order to serve a third term. He has also floated the idea of canceling the upcoming election, 

telling

 Reuters “when you think of it, we shouldn’t even have an election.”


 


When Volodymyr Zelensky — whose presidential term 

ended

 in May 2024 — informed Trump that elections would not be held in Ukraine because of the war, Trump

 

responded, “So you’re saying, during the war you can’t have elections…So, let me just say, three and a half years from now, so you mean if we happen to be in a war with somebody, no more elections? Oh, that’s good.”


 


Trump

 

told

 The New York Times in January he 

regretted

 not directing the National Guard to seize voting machines after the 2020 election. Trump not only wants to

 

abolish

 mail-in ballots – Democrats vote by mail in higher numbers than Republicans – but voting machines and tabulators which allow election boards to post results on election night.


 


Trump laid the groundwork for federal interference in his national address in July on election fraud, 

charging

 that the elections are dangerously exposed to “hacking, exploitation, and foreign interference.”


 


This assault has been decades in the making. It did not begin with Trump.


 


I warned about the Christian nationalist movement and its latent fascism in my book “

American Fascists: The Christian Right and the War on America

.” These Christian fascists are enemies of the open society. They seek to disenfranchise huge segments of the public, demand the deregulation of industry and the elimination of all social services, including public education, public health programs and consumer protection. The only proper tasks for the federal government, they believe, are tax collection, war and domestic security.


 


These goals are laid out in numbing technical detail in 

Project 2025

title: India’s Gen-Z Movement: Challenges Ahead for the Teachers and the Buddhist Way Forward
content:
The resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan, Minister of Education, Government of India (a Gen-X person born between 1965–1980), has come as a shock, as it was considered impossible to get a resignation from any minister of the Narendra Modi-led NDA government from 2014 till now. However, the students of Gen-Z (born between 1997–2012, now in the age group 14–29) made it possible, along with the Millennials (born between 1981–1996), Gen-X, and Gen-Alpha (born between 2013–2020). The Gen-Z students would be mostly from class 10th onwards, and some may be working professionals as well. The protests (mostly) by Gen-Z have shown the other generations that they have accomplished something that other generations could not have achieved in the last 12 years (although the support of other generations cannot be neglected). The Gen-Z students would then have a new level of confidence when they go to their classes and interact with their teachers. However, without the right guidance to channel it properly, this surge of confidence can easily tip into an obdurate, impudent, and supercilious attitude, turning their outlook entirely quixotic. Therefore, the role of teachers, supervisors, universities, institutes, etc., would come into the picture, and they would have to face certain challenges. The challenges mentioned are not exhaustive; instead, they are suggestive.

The first challenge that universities/institutes (overall) and individual teachers as well would face is: Are the Gen-Z students going to listen (śravaṇa in Sanskrit—the first step of learning) to their teachers and universities? Are they going to follow the rules and regulations of the university/institute and maintain the decorum of the classes? Why I think this may be a challenge is because the Gen-Z students, with their creativity of language and presentation, have shut the mouths of many mainstream media channels and politicians, and have also astonished political scientists who never expected the occurrence of this nation-wide protest (if not in India, then at least not under the present government). These students have not been in the mood to listen to anything that has no bearing on the government’s accountability for the suicides of many NEET aspirants. This is understandable considering the seriousness of the issue. However, some videos have shown that students have hooted at the biased media channels, as they have been determined not to listen to anything from them.

The second challenge deals with humility and humbleness. Humility is an important aspect of learning. Learning results in humility (as said, vidyā dadāti vinayaṁ). Learning also results from humility—if I think that I am superior to others in terms of knowledge, how can I learn from others? I would then do whatever I think is fit according to ‘me’, even if that act disrespects someone. Are the Gen-Z students going to contemplate their continuous learning from life (manan in Sanskrit—the second step for learning), or would they feel supercilious? Are the Gen-Z students going to be in the disposition to learn from their teachers? Why I think this may be a challenge is because the Gen-Z students have already contemplated the inevitable consequences of the ruining of the country if the lacuna in education is not fixed. For this, they have raised their voice for their right to education, and thereby they have taught the world the peaceful management of crowds, connecting people, and leading a crowd. However, this same sense of achievement may let them feel that they know everything. It is also possible that they may not contemplate new learning, reflect deeply, or sharpen their arguments and creativity. Rather, they may take refuge in harsh and abusive language to assert their points, which has already been seen in the protests by some of the students. This aggression might block any novel and meaningful discoveries in their learning journey.

The third challenge is the continuity and culmination of the above two and deals with real-life experiences (nidhidhyāsana). The real-life experiences of unexpected events occur only when we listen to others and continuously contemplate them. Without that, we would continuously live in one set of habituated thinking caused by our external environments. But by continuously listening to others, like our well-wishers—teachers, parents, friends, etc.—and critics, we would be able to contemplate and improve our habituated practices. But without checks and balances …

title: Kurdish people renew pledge to carry on the struggle of the martyrs
content:
Mothers of the martyrs in Van (Wan) welcomed their loved ones with the words: “Our condolences to the Kurdish people and Abdullah Öcalan. We welcome our martyrs with pride. We will carry the banner they left us to victory and continue their struggle.” The scenes at the commemoration in Van once again reflected the reality of a people who resist and struggle. Through their stance, the Kurdish people created a scene that will remain etched in collective memory. The ululations of the mothers and the slogans of Van’s youth reverberated throughout the gathering. Pain, anger and hope for a free future were experienced simultaneously, with the intensity of the darkest days of war. Pride, a determination to uphold their legacy and a desire for retribution were present at the same time and in the same place. Through his 53-year struggle, Abdullah Öcalan built a people capable of resisting and of finding ways to continue their struggle even amid war. This spirit was visible throughout Van.


The Serhed region has endured countless tragedies and massacres over the past century. Yet it has never ceased to be a centre of resistance and popular uprisings; on the contrary, it has played a leading role throughout every period of the national struggle and remained an important arena of resistance. The emergence of the Kurdish Freedom Movement further strengthened this tradition through organisation. Even in the most difficult periods, the people of Van joined the struggle with a determination that became a source of strength for Kurds and the people of Kurdistan as a whole. The city of Van contributed thousands of courageous young people to the Kurdish people’s struggle. The commemorations held in the city reflected this legacy in every respect.


Kurdish youth entered the commemoration chanting “Şehîd namirin, Bijî Serok Apo (A.Öcalan)” (Martyrs never die, long live Apo) and pledged to uphold the legacy of those who had lost their lives. The stance of Van’s youth became a source of hope for the future of the Kurdish people. Abdullah Öcalan laid the foundations of this spirit of commitment 53 years ago, and today it has become a philosophy of life embraced throughout society.


At the commemoration for the martyrs in Van, mothers spoke of them in the following words:


“We are proud of them; they fought for freedom and dignity and fell courageously. There is no more honourable path or way of life than this. We will uphold their struggle. The entire Kurdish people must honour the sacrifices made by the martyrs.”


These words evoked a painful chapter in history: the Geliyê Zilan Massacre. During the massacre, when soldiers of the Turkish state beheaded Mother Gulnaz’s son and brought his head before her, she proudly lifted it, kissed it and said:


“I gave birth to this son for days such as these, and I am proud of his resistance. My son resisted you for the cause of his people.”


With these words, she faced the death of her son. Mother Gulnaz’s response left the Turkish soldiers astonished. They had expected her to mourn her son and be overwhelmed by grief, but her response instead embodied the resilience and defiance of Kurdish women.


The Kurdish people are now taking ownership of their future


The mothers of Kurdistan know what stance to take in the face of the occupying forces. The losses and deaths experienced in Kurdistan have also given rise to an ideological and political stance. History repeated itself once again through the mothers of Van (Wan). The commemoration held in Van represented a continuation of this stance and determination. Abdullah Öcalan has examined the history of the Kurdish people in all its dimensions and has built a Kurdish consciousness capable of changing the course of history.


Periods of mourning in Kurdistan have brought Kurdish society closer together and strengthened its attachment to the values it holds sacred. This coming together and sense of commitment have brought about fundamental changes in the sociology of Kurdish society. These changes are, of course, the result of Abdullah Öcalan’s 53 years of struggle and resistance. A people once struggling against the threat of annihilation have now broken the chains of subjugation and taken ownership of their own future.

author: Brian Hioe
title: Taitung Graft Probe Highlights Recurrent Issues of Rural Corruption
content:
ISSUES REGARDING local corruption are again in the news, with a number of pan-Blue Taitung city councilors questioned about the use of public funds to build a resort.

The resort, the Dongying International Resort, is linked to the family of Taitung County Council Speaker Wu Hsiu-hua. In May, independent city councillor Lin Tsan-tian raised during a county council meeting that public funds had been used to expand a road leading to the Dongying International Resort. Though the road was originally supposed to be three meters wide, it was expanded to nine meters wide. Reportedly, the road is also at least partly on state-owned land. For its part, Taitung authorities claimed the road was to benefit local farmers and prevent accidents, though no accidents had occurred on the road in the past decade.

What raised suspicion was that the discretionary funding of several city councilors was used on the road. Lin pointed to that while county councilors usually use discretionary funding to help repair roads or assist farmers to construct water tanks, they do not usually pool their discretionary funding on a road in this way.

In the wake of Lin’s questioning, a probe was launched. Seven city councilors have been questioned to date, six of whom are members of the KMT, and one of whom is a member of the People First Party. Wu was recently endorsed by Taichung mayor Lu Shiow-yen of the KMT in the upcoming elections.

Nevertheless, issues of corruption are far from unheard of in rural areas in Miaoli. Recently, KMT Legislative Caucus Leader Fu Kun-chi, who represents Hualien, came under scrutiny after former Financial Times journalist Kathrin Hille referenced widespread vote buying in Hualien during an interview on FTV.

Fu has long faced allegations of vote buying, not only in Hualien, but in the KMT Central Standing Committee election. Fu’s wife, Hsu Cheng-wei, is currently Hualien county magistrate, and she originally took up the post after Fu was arrested on corruption charges. Prior to his jailing, Fu divorced Hsu and named her deputy county commissioner to skirt nepotism laws, leading to a lawsuit against him over a fake divorce. Though Fu was previously kicked out of the KMT for his actions, he has since been welcomed back in because of his ability to win elections, and consequently risen to become KMT legislative caucus leader.

Other recent cases of high-profile corruption have also involved pan-Blue county magistrates. In January 2025, former Nantou county magistrate Lee Chao-ching, a former KMT member, was sentenced on charges totaling 656 years and four months in jail.

Charges facing Lee were mostly regarding kickbacks for reconstruction projects after Typhoon Morakot, which struck Taiwan in August 2009. Lee reportedly demanded 10% in kickbacks for reconstruction projects, which were passed to him in gift boxes of tea and fruit.

In December 2024, former Yilan county magistrate Lin Zi-miao was sentenced to 12.5 years in jail on charges of corruption. The charges against Lin date to 2022, when Lin came under scrutiny in connection to a development project on a 108-hectare plot of land in Luodong that was originally protected. However, the land was later rezoned for agricultural use in 2018, though residential building construction and public infrastructure development were allowed on the plot. The plot’s rezoning, as well as related land disputes, were seen as suggesting lawbreaking. This was quickly linked to Lin, seeing as the purchaser of the plot of land after its rezoning was Lin Shu-mei’s son. Lin Shu-mei, a former member of the National Assembly before its abolition, is Lin Zi-miao’s cousin and is a fellow member of the KMT.

Lin then came under scrutiny for checks worth over 100 million NT received by Lin or her family members from former KMT legislator Yang Chi-hsiung. Yang was known to have had a close relationship with Lin when he served as legislator, assisting Lin electorally. Likewise, several of Lin Zi-miao’s children worked in a mining company under Yang’s name.

Issues of local corruption continue to be commonplace in Taiwan, then. It is to be seen if charges stick in Taitung or, as with so many other cases, they simply bounce off.

author: groundxero
title: When the Mountain Broke: Inside Nepal’s Deadliest Himalayan Flood
content:
The disaster exposed the extreme fragility of high-altitude Himalayan ecosystems under a shifting climate.


 


By

Madhab Pant


 


At roughly 8:30 AM on 26 August 2026, a wall of water, mud, ice, and massive boulders roared down the Lhende Khola into the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river systems. The surge struck without local rainfall or warning sirens, catching border communities like Timure, mid-morning. Initial reports mistook the ground tremors for an earthquake, but satellite and seismic data later confirmed the real trigger: a high-altitude collapse of rock and ice near Langtang Lirung, on the Tibetan side, spanning nearly one square kilometer and generating a ground shock equivalent to a magnitude 5.2 quake. Plunging 1,200 vertical meters into the valley, the avalanche briefly dammed the Lhende River before rupturing, unleashing a debris-laden slurry that tore through Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha, Tanahun, and Chitwan.


 


Environmental Drivers and Hydrological Cascade


 


The disaster exposed the extreme fragility of high-altitude Himalayan ecosystems under a shifting climate. Rising temperatures and accelerating freeze-thaw cycles are steadily degrading permafrost and the cryogenic bonds that hold mountain bedrock together, priming slopes for collapse. This was not an isolated event: smaller glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) incidents in July 2025 had already weakened local topsoil and riverbank integrity.


 


The catastrophe unfolded in two stages. First, the avalanche formed a short-lived debris dam across the narrow Lhende Khola. Hydrostatic pressure built rapidly behind the ice-and-rock wall as glacial meltwater and river discharge backed up, until the barrier gave way. Second, the released surge raced downstream at speeds exceeding 75 km/h, scouring up topsoil, riverbed gravel, and boulders as it went and turning into a hyper-abrasive slurry that gouged riverbeds, stripped valley walls, and undercut mountain foundations across the Bhotekoshi, Trishuli, and Narayani corridors. Secondary barrier lakes are still forming along blocked upper tributaries, prompting fresh flood warnings downstream.


 


Human Toll and Structural Damage


 


According to Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) and the Nepal Police, the toll on life and infrastructure has been devastating. Confirmed deaths have surpassed 669, with victims swept as far as Chitwan (248), Nawalparasi East (158), and Paschim Nawalparasi (75); some remains were recovered up to 240 kilometres away in India’s Uttar Pradesh. Between 1,000 and 2,426 people remain missing, including 933 hydropower workers, dozens of security personnel from the Nepal Army, Police, and Armed Police Force, customs officers, residents, and over 500 foreign nationals mostly trekkers and Kailash Mansarovar pilgrims from more than 30 countries.


 


On the recovery front, between 3,700 and 4,400 survivors have been treated or evacuated, including nearly 200 workers pulled from flooded underground hydropower tunnels. Damages are now estimated to exceed NRs 200 billion. The flood destroyed more than 80 bridges (35+ motorable, 45+ suspension) and washed out 40 kilometers of the vital Betrawati–Rasuwagadhi trade corridor, halting overland commerce with China. Thirteen run-of-the-river hydropower plants including the 111 MW Rasuwagadhi and 60 MW Upper Trishuli 3A sustained direct structural damage, knocking hundreds of megawatts off the national grid.


 


Ecological Disruption and Human-Made Risk


 


Beyond the human and economic cost, the scouring wiped out aquatic habitats and macroinvertebrate populations across Langtang National Park and its buffer zones. Millions of tons of topsoil were stripped from mountain slopes, while heavy silt deposits degraded farmland further downstream. Environmental assessments warn that unstable debris left in the upper tributaries could form new barrier lakes, raising the risk of further outburst floods when the rains return.


 


Human activity in these narrow corridors amplified the destruction. Encroaching highway construction, constricted floodplains, and loose excavation muck from active building sites added extra material to the flood’s path. Once the surge hit, this debris and the narrowed riverbeds turned built infrastructure into secondary hazards that intensified the wave’s force.
