author: rti_admin
title: India’s Unfinished Independence
content:
Every August 15, the flag goes up over the Red Fort, the anthem plays in every school and University for a day to celebrate being free. We call it Independence Day — the day India stopped being ruled by the British after two hundred years. And I celebrate it too. But every year, sitting with it a little longer than a headline or a holiday usually gets, one question won’t leave me. Free from what, exactly, and free for whom? The British extracted our wealth, silenced us, and treated us like subjects and inhumane instead of people. They eventually left. But did the thing they left behind actually go with them? Seventy-five-plus years later, many people are still living under a kind of threat, inhuman, and subject to no major change, and the political power is transferred from one hand to another. That time, foreign rule, and the present time, the elite and the oppressed class. caste, patriarchy, or social hierarchy systems- nobody ever really dismantled them, just handed them down like inheritance. The face in charge changed. For too many people, the situation underneath it didn’t. None of this is me rejecting the freedom we won or the people who died for it. It’s me refusing to let “freedom” become something we wave on a flagpole once a year without looking at who still doesn’t have it. After independence, many have hope for major change. We are ruling ourselves at least; nobody discriminates against us, but it is only theoretical, not practical.

We, the people of India, aren’t one religion. We’re not just Hindu, or just Muslim, or Christian, or Sikh — and the Constitution doesn’t lean on any of that in its opening line. It says: “India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.” That’s a bigger sentence than it looks. India was never built to belong to one group. Many people are sacrificing their lives, their homes, their hope, their relatives, etc., every family, every tongue, every tradition, without asking anyone to give up who they are to be let in. The Constitution doesn’t just govern us. It protects the different ways we live, our culture, tradition, and language. But that raises a fair question: why does a free people need a document telling them how to live? If human beings are born free, shouldn’t that be enough on its own? For most of history, freedom on paper and freedom in real life were two completely different things. Before the Constitution, millions of people on this land weren’t fully recognized as human, and they were denied all human rights. No education, no right to object to injustice out loud, no fundamental rights. treated as animals; they were not counted as citizens. Two hundred years of British rule made all of that worse, and many people gave everything to end it. Even now, it’s worth asking: is that independence something everyone actually gets to feel, or is it still a promise some people are still waiting on? The Ambedkar Constitution is not just a rulebook. They wrote down a vision; it is a way of life, what Ambedkar called Prabuddha Bharat, an “Enlightened India” where every person could live with dignity and respect, no exceptions. A constitution isn’t a book or a scripture. It’s that imagination of a glorious society, made enforceable.

When Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and the others wrote the Constitution, they weren’t just setting up a government. They were imagining a civilization. Ambedkar called it Prabuddha Bharat — an Enlightened India — where a person’s caste, gender, religion, or birth wouldn’t determine how freely they could move, speak, or live. Liberty, equality, and fraternity weren’t supposed to just sit in the preamble looking nice. They were supposed to be alive. On the eve of the Constitution’s adoption, Ambedkar warned that India was walking into a life full of contradictions — political equality on paper, and deep social and economic inequality in daily life. He said if that contradiction were allowed to go unaddressed, the people suffering under it would eventually blow up the whole structure of political democracy. That warning is still hanging over us, mostly ignored. Caste wasn’t invented by the British — it existed long before them, and it outlived them too. Dalits and Adivasis still face discrimination in villages, in workplaces, in schools, and even in death — separate cremation grounds, separate wells, and separate seating still exist in parts of this country. People still get attacked over things as small as riding a horse to their own wedding, wearing certain …

author: Alma Torlakovic
title: ‘Working 9 to 5, should be able to make a living’—Sydney Uni staff shut down campus over pay, conditions
content:
The first strike of Sydney University staff in our new enterprise agreement campaign was a banger. The campus was a ghost town, with very few people even attempting to enter. Services were disrupted all over because significant numbers of staff were on strike or “absent” in solidarity. All the libraries closed for the day, and classes were cancelled or rescheduled.

The picket line was well-attended, jubilant and colourful. About 600 staff and students set up pickets around campus entrances from 7am. Between chanting classic union slogans, talking to passersby and arguing with people to turn around and not work today, we found time to sing and dance.

By far the most popular song of the day was “9 to 5”, by Dolly Parton. It’s just what a striking worker wants to hear, and you gotta admit, it’s contagious:

Working 9 to 5, what a way to make a living

Barely getting by, it’s all taking and no giving

They just use your mind, and they never give you credit

It’s enough to drive you crazy if you let it (but you won’t let it)

Parton’s song sums up exactly how we’re feeling at the moment, barely able to keep up with rent, mortgages and bills. With all the added mental and physical stress of counting every dime to make ends meet, we’re somehow still expected to perform our jobs to a high standard. And accept that management doesn’t really care for our lives or opinions.

The collective solidarity at the pickets was a natural antidote to the everyday experience of being at work. You look around the campus and see that nothing is moving without us, and suddenly, we don’t feel so disposable.

Staff brought their own placards, and food to share. We spent the day sharing stories and reasons for why we’re on strike. At the Parramatta Road main gate picket, we played a fun guessing game we dubbed “The Price is Outrageous!” to highlight the cost-of-living crisis.

An all-in rally culminated outside the vice-chancellor’s administration building with more chanting and speeches.

The strike was for 24 hours, and we will need many more if we are to win. NTEU Fightback, a rank-and-file group within the National Tertiary Education Union, argues that regular and well-planned strikes are the only effective tool our side has.

Management has a suite of proposed attacks on our conditions. They want to make it easier to push through redundancies. They want to deploy AI, threatening job security, the quality of our jobs, and the education and services we provide. And they want us to trust that they’ll do so on an ethical basis with staff rights at heart.

They won’t commit to serious action on de-casualisation, instead proposing to introduce more teaching-focused roles that break the teaching-research nexus.

The union has a lot to win as well. We are seeking a 20 percent pay rise (notably, we initially voted for 25 percent, but this was quashed by our own national office). We want recognition that staff wages have gone backwards by tens of thousands since 2021 due to sub-inflation pay rises. We are still pressuring management to commit to enforceable targets for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander employment, improved disability rights, an academic workload allocation policy based on how much time the work actually takes, intellectual freedom, and an increase in severance pay for professional staff.

Alma Torlakovic is a member of the NTEU branch committee, the NTEU national council and is the NSW Socialists candidate for Granville in the March 2027 state election.

title: “There’s this sketchy Dutch black metal band touring Australia …”
content:
I was contacted a little while ago by somebody raising concerns about a couple of upcoming black metal gigs. Below is the text they sent.

There’s this sketchy Dutch black metal band, Helleruin, playing in Melbourne at the Northcote Social Club on September 11 and in Sydney at Crowbar on September 12.

Most of Helleruin’s records have been released on New Era Productions, which has put out a number of releases by fash black metal bands and which is run by Jasper Velzel, a NSBM and RAC musician. In addition, another project of Helleruin’s Carchost — Orewoet — is on the label Heidens Hart, which — along with releasing some far-right stuff — is owned by a former live guitarist of prominent fash band Graveland.

Moreover, a number of the local supporting acts have sketchy connections.

Order of Orias, one of two supports in Melbourne along with Petrol (see below), are on World Terror Committee, which releases fashy stuff and is owned by Sven Zimper, a member of prominent NSBM group Absurd.

Of the bands playing Sydney with Helleruin (Krvna, Pestilential Shadows, Destruktor, Vicissitude, Gravgöt, Grotesque Bliss, Petrol, Blasfemancia and Akhoth) at the ‘Call from the Grave’ festival:

Pestilential Shadows have released music on the Chinese label, GoatowaRex, who are very friendly to NSBM acts. Additionally, PS is part of a collective called Ordo Ater Anguis/Order of the Black Serpent, which includes numerous far right acts. Michael W Ford of Black Funeral appears to be a former Order of Nine Angles (09A) member in the United States who — after distancing himself from O9A — attempted to formulate a social Darwinist version of the Satanic Temple (lol), which coalesce around the Australian fash-friendly label, Dark Adversary. Indeed, one of the members of PS is also a member of Varw, a band on Dark Adversary. Further, Akhoth released a demo, ‘Storm of Pagan Fury’, on CD on Dark Adversary this year.

Grotesque Bliss are on Iron Bonehead which, along with the suspect name, appears to be run by a (if only barely) crypto-fascist.

Destruktor is on a label, Hells Headbangers, which has previously released and re-released stuff by Satanic Warmaster and Deströyer 666, including re-releasing Deströyer 666’s debut album, ‘Unchain the Wolves’, on a few different mediums over the last few years. Additionally, Inquisition had a few releases on Hells Headbangers after their lead singer (who is also a Satanist pedo) released openly fash music on fash label Satanic Skinhead Propaganda (a label which the Iron Bonehead guy sold in his old fash-friendly record store).

The most recent (2024) EP of Krvna, formally of PS, was released on Zazen Sounds, run by Greek nazi black metaller Acherontass of Αχέροντας (Krvna played guest guitar on their most recent album). For what it’s also worth, Third Eye Temple — the Polish label on which Krvna’s 2022 album was released — have released one split and re-issued an EP by Voidhanger, a side project of Polish far right black metallers, Infernal War.

Finally, Petrol were previously on a cancelled bill with Gurn. They also played a gig with Japanese band Abigail, who are signed to Nuclear Now Productions, a fash-friendly label linked to Iron Bonehead (similarly exposed by the nsbmboneheads blog linked above). In addition, Petrol played at Crowbar Sydney last year with Bolzer (see nsbmboneheads blog), who released all but their last record on Iron Bonehead. The other headliner was Portal, who have released lots of records on Hells Headbangers including, recently, a split with Blood of Kingu — a side-project of the Ukrainian ultra-nationalists from Drudkh — on the label in 2014.

author: Isaac Nellist
title: Lessons from One Nation’s Secret Harbour by-election win
content:
It wasn’t even close. Pauline Hanson’s One Nation won the August 29 Secret Harbour by-election in Western Australia with 38.9% of the primary vote, up from 8.43% in the March 2025 state election.

With preferences, it secured 57% of the two-party preferred vote. Labor's primary vote slumped to 24.3%, down from 46.5%. The Liberals came in third with 17%.

The Greens ran a strong campaign, targeting the cost of living and AUKUS, but their vote dipped slightly from 8.82% to 7.64%.

The hope of some Labor party strategists after the South Australian state election that the nationwide surge in support for One Nation would mostly eat away Liberal or National Party votes was smashed.

Labor's candidate was Georgia Tree, a former lobbyist for oil and gas giant Woodside who no longer lived in the electorate. This did not help her credibility but the size of the swing indicates that this was a secondary factor.

There was as much dirt swirling around the One Nation candidate, whose party is even more explicit in its support for the fossil fuel industry.

There has been a four-decade decline in the primary vote for both Labor and Coalition. The thumping wins by WA Labor between 2017 and 2025 temporarily disguised this reality.

While Labor’s parliamentary majorities are real, they were and did not represent a new generation of “rusted on” loyal voters. That no longer exists like it did in the past.

Instability is the new normal in Australian politics.

In this turmoil One Nation’s bubble could also pop. However, neither the volatility nor the surge in toxic racist, sexist and anti-LGBTIQ scapegoating will go away by themselves.

This ugly reality grows out of three interrelated phenomena. They need to be understood separately and in combination because they all contribute to explaining why so many have turned to One Nation, but they each vary in importance depending on the individual.

The first is four decades of neoliberalism implemented by Liberal and Labor. This means policies that favour the rich at the expense of working people such as privatisation, deregulation, contracting out, corporate tax cuts and subsidies to landlords.

Together these policies have led to the wages share of national income falling to record lows — even though Australian workers are more productive than ever — a loss in job security and now the ferocious damage done by the housing affordability crisis.

The statistics bear out the feeling that many Australians have that the system, the economy and politics, no longer works for them.

Second is the fact that implementing neo-liberalism depended on reducing the militancy and organisation of Australian workers.

In the US and Britain this was achieved by conservative governments unleashing full-frontal attacks on the unions in an attempt to smash them.

In Australia it was done by Labor but more drawn out, slowly strangling the traditions of self-organisation and industrial action by taming unions through the infamous Prices and Incomes Accord.

In the 1970s the majority of the Australian workforce had some experience of going on strike, of taking collective action with their workmates to make their own lives and the lives of others better.

Unless they’ve been lucky enough to connect with a vibrant community or social movement campaign, or been part of the recent upsurge in activism against the genocide in Gaza, most Australian workers have never been part of such collective action.

The vacuum is quickly filled by despair, individualism, scapegoating and “culture wars”; all of which erode social solidarity.

Third is the unrelenting campaign by the pro-capitalist parties and media over the last decades to deflect people’s anger and anxiety at refugees, Muslims and migrants in general.

The Labor Party has gone along with this, and most of the union movement acquiesced, doing terrible damage to working-class consciousness.

Labor is powerless to kill the monster it helped create, and does not have the will to do so. It’s determination to squash the Palestine solidarity movement is proof of that.

Of course racism in Australia didn’t begin with the assault on refugee rights or the ramblings of Pauline Hanson.

It has its origins in a colonial settler state based on the violent dispossession of Indigenous people and serving as a fortress for the British Empire, and now the US, in the Asia Pacific.

The world economy divides humanity into rich and poor. This system is both violent and requires …

author: Alexis Vassiley
title: Labor’s Secret Harbour by-election loss is ominous
content:
Less than eighteen months ago, Western Australian Corrective Services Minister Paul Papalia comfortably held the seat of Secret Harbour, in Perth’s southern suburbs, with a two-party preferred vote of 61.5 percent in the state election. The by-election on Saturday wasn’t even close. One Nation currently leads 57-43 on a two-party preferred basis with 75 percent of the vote counted.

ON candidate Luke Herdegen’s 39 percent primary vote represents a swing of more than 30 percent to the party since last year. Labor’s primary vote plummeted to less than 25 percent, for a negative swing of 22 percent.

Labor’s campaign was utterly tone deaf. Papalia, who retired last month, triggering the by-election, told the

West Australian

days before the election: ‘‘We live in the best state in the best country on planet Earth, and part of the reason for that is good, solid, responsible government”. Anthony Albanese flew to Perth, not to campaign in the election, but for a $10,000-a-head fundraising dinner in a mansion on a street nicknamed “millionaire’s row”.

The party’s candidate selection was no better. Georgia Tree, a government relations advisor to Woodside Energy, was parachuted into what was considered “safe” territory. She previously worked for Federal Resources Minister Madeline King. Tree tried to leverage her working-class roots, saying how important Medicare and TAFE were to her parents. But all she could muster was a pathetic $100 fuel payment for motorists as her answer to the cost-of-living crisis.

Labor threw its all at the campaign, spending more than $400,000 (of which $14,850 came from Woodside). The premier seemingly never left the candidate’s side, while government MPs from all across Perth doorknocked. Labor also spent millions on a pork-barrelling spree and promised to finally start work on a train station they first promised ten years ago. But it was to no avail.

Despite what WA Labour tells itself, voters are not happy. A Demos poll in late August asked respondents if the state government was doing a good or bad job managing particular issues. Its

best

 result was 0 percent for “net good job” (i.e. the same percentage thought it was doing a good and bad job) for education and schools. On the cost-of-living, net good job was negative 56 percent; for housing it was negative 57 percent.

Indeed, the health and education systems are in crisis. The housing situation is thrown into stark relief on Memorial Drive, in the neighbouring Rockingham electorate, where hundreds of homeless people sleep in tents and caravans. Yet funding can be found to build housing for 1,200 defence personnel from the US and UK. In fact, Labor governments are spending billions of dollars on nearby military facilities at HMAS Stirling and the Henderson industrial precinct.

Secret Harbour is one of the least diverse seats in the state. There are fewer immigrants than the state average; those there hail largely from the UK, New Zealand and South Africa. Largely working class, more people have vocational qualifications than university degrees.

Gym owner Herdegen’s pitch centred on infrastructure, the cost of living, crime, immigration and housing. He told voters that Labor had neglected the area for too long, and this was an opportunity to send a message. Herdegen’s campaign did not shy away from far-right talking points. One social media video, for instance, talked about “saving the family suburb”, blaming a “population explosion” for ruining the “suburban Australian dream”, featuring white faces and nostalgic music. The One Nation campaign also spent a huge amount.

The Liberals did badly, coming third with around 17 percent of the primary vote (a negative swing of nearly 8 percent. State Liberal leader Basil Zempilas provoked a stoush with the Liberal federal MP for Canning, Andrew Hastie (whose seat overlaps with Secret Harbour), by claiming that a One Nation win would actually be a Liberal “victory”.

The Greens vote held mostly steady at 7.5 percent. The party campaigned on Labor’s neglect of the area, the cost of living, housing and against the AUKUS security pact.

So this was a good night for the racist far-right bigots of One Nation. The orange wave is real. Prior to Secret Harbour, it remained to be seen if One Nation could actually win seats off Labor. They can, and “safe” ones at that. Labor had held Secret Harbour and its previous incarnations since 1989. Only in 2008 and 2025 did Labor candidate need preferences to …

author: Susan Price
title: Climate emergency: Nepal disaster is ‘showing us the future’
content:
While the whole world is shocked and horrified at the scenes of the catastrophic glacial floods and landslides in Nepal and Tibet, this should be an international wakeup call, said Indra Raj Bhattarai, a social justice and human rights advocate, conservation educator and researcher from Nepal.

Speaking from Nepal’s capital, Kathmandu, Bhattarai told Green Left that despite several climate summits the international community has fallen far short of its targets for funding climate change frontline states such as Nepal.

“This is not only an issue of Nepal,” he said. “Nepal adds very little to the global greenhouse gas emissions and 46% of Nepal is forest.

“And it is not just Nepal that is affected. It goes to other countries also, because the river flows all the way to the ocean, past the boundaries of landlocked Nepal.”

Melting glaciers across the whole Hindu Kush Himalaya mountain system directly affect China, India, Myanmar, Bangladesh, Bhutan and Pakistan, Bhattarai explained.

“It affects these countries’ agriculture, the ecosystem and the economy of the whole region.

“Eventually the water from melting glaciers will raise the sea level and affect even more countries.

“We’ve talked about this problem for at least the past two decades in lots of international meetings. Day by day, our extreme weather patterns send us reminders.

“The devastating consequences are seen. The biodiversity is in decline, new diseases are emerging and lots of devastating effects remind us that this is the problem of the whole world.”

Bhattarai said that the international climate talks have focused on the “polluter pays” principle (PPP) which means that those responsible for environmental damage and greenhouse gas emissions should pay the cost of preventing, controlling and remedying impacts.

“What happened to PPP? Nepal actually increased its forested area by 10% in the last decade and a half, but we are facing the challenges arising from increased greenhouse emissions and forest clearing in other parts of the world…

“There’s a fund called the Green Climate Fund [which approved $36.1 million for Nepal in 2025] to reduce the risk of glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) and United Nations agencies are working on that, but Nepal still has no early warning system.

“That should be the first thing the fund is used for. If we had an early warning system, thousands of lives would have been saved.

“We still don’t know exactly how many people lost their lives but we can say that between 15,000 and 20,000 people have been directly affected.”

The Nepali government is struggling to deal with this catastrophe and the problem is made worse because there is not enough cooperation with China, Bhattarai told GL.

“We need real-time information sharing mechanisms between these two countries to deal with this disaster.

“One week after this flood swept through the Rasuwa and other valleys, there are some remote areas where they have not seen any government representatives or aid.

“While the Nepali and Chinese governments are doing their best to rescue the people buried in the hydroelectric dam tunnels, many other people in remote areas are still not getting emergency assistance, nor have there been efforts to rescue them.

“They urgently need food, medical help and temporary shelters. They need solar lights, communication equipment or mobile connections.”

Those who survived the flood but lost family members also face a very challenging time, Bhattarai said.

“They are moving from one place to another trying to identify their families among the dead bodies, and as a result suffer serious mental health problems, which are not addressed.”

There have been complaints about the emergency response by the new Nepali government, under Prime Minister Balendra Shah. However, Bhattari said that the PM was correct to call an all-party meeting to deal with the crisis.

“While all the party leaders agreed to cooperate, until now there is little cooperation between the federal, provincial and local governments.

“The provincial and local governments are in a better situation to understand the real problems in the field but they are controlled by the parties in opposition at the federal level. The federal ministers have little local connections.”

Bhattarai said the federal government should be distributing more of the international funds to the provincial and local governments.

“Our political leaders should realise that they need to put the people’s interest …

author: Jerome Small
title: Vic premier’s attack on independent unions is an attack on decent unionism
content:
Organisations that offer workers some choice over who represents their industrial interests should be in the same legal category as violent fascist gangs and listed terrorist organisations. This is the intended effect of

amendments

 to laws governing incorporated associations, introduced into the Victorian parliament in mid-August by new Premier Ben Carroll’s Labor government. 

The law threatens to wipe out the Retail and Fast Food Workers Union (RAFFWU), which is a challenger to Labor’s largest affiliated union—the notoriously right-wing Shop, Distributive and Allied Employees Association (SDA). Much of the media coverage has presented Carroll’s appalling attack on RAFFWU as a straightforward factional payback, after the SDA-aligned faction within the Labor caucus supported Carroll when he rolled Jacinta Allen as premier of Victoria last month. 

Factional favours may well be a factor, but there’s more to it than that. 

As well as being a gift to the SDA leadership, Carroll’s move is part of a nationwide trend for Labor to crack down on any idea that workers should be entitled to seek representation from a union body not currently licensed by the state through the Fair Work Commission. 

Similar legislation

 to the current Victorian bill was passed in Queensland in 2022 under the Labor government of Annastacia Palaszczuk. And the

Australian Financial Review


reported

 in mid-August that Workplace Relations Minister Amanda Rishworth, a former SDA organiser, moved amendments to the national Labor platform at July’s national ALP conference “to bind the party to target ‘sham unions’”. According to the

AFR

: “The amendments say Labor will legislate to limit unregistered unions’ participation in industrial matters, including acting as bargaining representatives”.

Labor figures say that the main target of these moves are the so-called “Red” unions set up in recent years. These “Red” unions are indeed a crime against decent, principled unionism. Their main instigator is Graeme Haycroft, who has a long history in the Liberal National Party in Queensland and was a long-time, prominent member of the notorious 1980s union-busting think tank the

HR Nicholls Society

.

But the best remedy against right-wing unions preying on workers is political exposure, along with established unions demonstrating their superiority through organising strikes and industrial action that improve workers’ lives. This is clearly too much work to contemplate for most of today’s union leaders, and would run totally counter to their politics, which emphasises class collaboration rather than class combat. Much easier to just rely on Labor to wipe out any competitors through legal and bureaucratic methods.

It’s not just RAFFWU and the “Red” unions that are affected by Labor’s attacks. For a decade from 2015, the farm workers’ organising team of the United Workers Union conducted a series of effective—in fact,

outstanding

—organising drives among migrant workers on farms. These workers sometimes made use of the provisions in the Fair Work Act that allow workers to nominate independent bargaining agents to represent them at enterprise agreement negotiations. 

This enabled workers to get around the dictates of the Fair Work Commission, which enforces a legal monopoly on union coverage for most industries in Australia. In the case of farms, this state-sanctioned monopoly belonged to the Australian Workers Union, which had done zero organising on farms for decades and was utterly opposed to any other union doing this organising either. 

Removing the ability of workers to appoint an independent bargaining agent in these circumstances, which seems to be the intention of Rishworth’s proposed changes to national industrial laws, would pose a significant problem for workers in situations like this. Migrant farm workers would be able to secure decent representation only by overthrowing the entire national leadership of the AWU, one of the oldest and strongest bureaucratic machines within Australia’s union movement. 

There’s also the case of the

Independent Transport Union

, a breakaway from the Rail, Tram and Bus Union in Victoria. Unlike RAFFWU, the ITU didn’t start as a project of the left, but rather as a sectional breakaway representing train drivers. But regardless of its origins, the ITU has become an effective industrial force within V/Line, Victoria’s regional rail network. The ITU’s existence as an incorporated association is clearly …

author: Alex Bainbridge
title: Activists protest Murray Watt on Beetaloo gas
content:
Yesterday, fracked gas from the Beetaloo Basin was pumped into the NT electricity grid for the first time. The NT is also planning a big expansion of data centres which will be run in part on Beetaloo gas.

Around the country today, people took action to oppose the opening of Beetaloo and to highlight the disaster that ongoing fossil fuel extraction will be. This action was in Magan-djin/Brisbane outside federal environment minister Murray Watt's office.

Activists intended to present Watt with fracking fluid to show how dangerous it is, but he declined to meet with protesters.

author: Cecilia Judge
title: Victory for rank-and-file ticket in Victorian health union election
content:
A group of rank-and-file unionists have ousted the leadership of the Victorian Allied Health Professionals Association (VAHPA) in a landslide election. The VAHPA Pulse ticket, made up of rank-and-file union activists, gained almost twice the vote of the incumbents, VAHPA Unity, and won all the positions.

The VAHPA Unity team has controlled the union for fourteen years and was backed by significant anonymous donations. By contrast, VAHPA Pulse, which I am part of, relied for our support on conviction and our reputations as experienced and uncompromising delegates and activists. Our victory is the culmination of many years of hard work and solid rank-and-file union activity.

The outgoing leadership took control of VAHPA with the ticket name “Clean Sweep”. Clean Sweep faced off against cronies of former national secretary Kathy Jackson, who was responsible for disgraceful corruption and whose actions gave bosses and anti-unionists ammunition to attack unions. Defeating them was an important victory.

However, after the new leadership stemmed the haemorrhaging of members and rebranded the union from HSU Branch 3 to the Victorian Allied Health Professionals Association to signal the beginning of a new era, there has been little in terms of concrete improvements for allied health workers.

I started working in public health just a few months after Clean Sweep came into office. Coming from the community sector, I was excited at the prospect of better pay and conditions in the health system. Today, members are leaving public health for the community sector for the same reason.

However, it’s not just our pay and conditions that have gone backwards under Clean Sweep. Members have also become increasingly frustrated and angry with the lack of communication and transparency on the part of the leadership, as well as its hostility to rank-and-file activity.

After working on the front lines throughout the pandemic, allied health workers had an enterprise agreement pushed on us in 2022 that contained a pathetic 2 percent pay “rise”. As the cost-of-living crisis intensifies and the workload increases in quantity and complexity, VAHPA members increasingly find themselves unable to remain in the sector, whether for financial reasons or their own mental health, often both.

At the 2023 delegates conference there was hope that the situation facing allied health workers might start to turn around. A new public sector organising team presented its three-year plan to rebuild delegate structures and networks in the lead-up to our next round of bargaining. There seemed to be a willingness to involve members and an understanding of the central role delegates play in not only recruiting members but also helping them become active unionists.

We all left excited. Delegates formed new working groups. In particular, professional reference groups were established to provide a mechanism for different occupational groups within VAHPA to raise their particular issues within the union.  Given VAHPA represents around 50 different professions within the complex health system, this work was vital not only to assist the union organisers to understand the issues on the floor, but also to strengthen our identity and ultimately our industrial confidence. All this work was to help inform our strategy before negotiations began on our next agreement.

These exciting developments were unfortunately short lived. We were told by the union leadership, and directly by the secretary, that this work was undermining and divisive to the union as a whole. Radiation therapists, arguably our most organised profession within the union, had been taking initiative in organising across the state and reaching out to their interstate counterparts to learn from their industrial victories. This was attacked by the leadership, which accused these workers of leaving other professions behind.

The message was clear: the leadership calls the shots.

The 2025 delegate conference was very different. Even friendly attempts by members to connect with each other were responded to aggressively by the leadership. I was rudely shouted at by the secretary on the conference floor after I asked for clarification about staffing. Later, I was attacked by an organiser and a delegate (who ran for assistant secretary on the VAHPA Unity ticket) in front of other delegates when I, on behalf of a core group of rank-and-file delegates, offered to start up a rank-and-file WhatsApp chat to increase …

author: Unknown
title: İHD 2025 Yılı Hak İhlalleri Raporu: Sandığa darbe, sokağa yumruk
content:
Eylem Nazlıer [email protected]

İnsan Hakları Derneği’nin (İHD) basından ve açık kaynaklardan derlediği bilgilerle hazırladığı 2025 Yılı Hak İhlalleri Raporu, Kürt sorununda çatışmalı süreç geride kalsa da birçok temel alanda insan hakları ihlallerinin tüm ağırlıyla varlığını sürdürdüğünü ortaya koydu. Raporda, “barış ortamını besleyip güçlendirecek yeterli demokratik adımların atılmaması, üstelik her türlü toplumsal tepkiyi yargı kılıcı ve kolluk sopasıyla bastırmayı düstur edinen yönetim anlayışının devam etmesi yine pek çok temel hakkın ihlaline yol açtı” tespitinde bulunuldu.

Rapora göre, 2025 yılında en çok hak ihlali tespit edilen iller sırasıyla İstanbul, Ankara, İzmir, Bursa, Van, Antalya, Diyarbakır, Mersin, Kocaeli ve Şırnak oldu. Nüfusa oranla en sık hak ihlali tespit edilen illerin başını ise Tunceli (Dersim) çekti. Onu sırasıyla Erzincan, Bolu, Kırşehir, Şırnak, Van, Ankara, İstanbul, Elazığ ve Iğdır takip etti.

Rapora göre, yaşam hakkına yönelik ihlaller sonucu en az 2.749 kişi hayatını kaybetti, en az 1.112 kişi yaralandı. Yaşam hakkı ihlallerinde başı iş cinayetleri çekti. 2025 yılında en az 2.105 kişi iş cinayetleri sonucu yaşamını yitirdi. Böylece 2016-2015 yılları arasında, 10 yılda iş cinayetleri sonucu ölen kişi sayısı 20.009 kişiye ulaştı. 2025’in ekonomik kriz ve MESEM vb. uygulamalarla çocuk işçiliğinde yaşanan kitleselleşmenin sonuçlarına da dikkat çekilen raporda, 26’sı 14 yaş ve altı, en az 94 çocuğun iş cinayetlerinde hayatını kaybettiği aktarıldı.

Rapora göre, Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan’ın “Aile Yılı” ilan ettiği 2025 yılında, kadınlar ve çocuklar yine erkek şiddetinin hedefi oldular. Her gün en az bir kadın ya da çocuk erkek şiddeti sonucu yaşamını yitirdi. Kadınlar en çok iktidarca konumlandırıldıkları “evde” şiddete maruz kalırken, bu şiddetin faili de yine eski/yeni eşler, partnerler ile baba, kardeş, damat gibi erkek aile fertleriydi.

Raporda, İHD’nin 1991 yılından bu yana yaptığı çalışmalara dayanılarak, Kürt sorununda çatışmalı süreç nedeniyle en az 36.479 kişinin yaşamını yitirdiği aktarıldı. İHD’nin verilerine göre, 25 yıllık bu süreçte 27.025 kişinin doğrudan operasyon ve çatışmalarda, 9.454 kişinin ise çatışmalı süreçle bağlantılı diğer saldırı ve yaşam hakkı ihlalleri sonucu hayatını kaybetti.

Rapora 2025 yılında, en az 159 kişi resmi ihmal ve denetimsizlik sonucu hayatını kaybetti. Deprem, sel vb. doğa olayları sonucu en az 1 kişi öldü, en az 180 kişi yaralandı. Bolu’da otel yangınında 34’ü çocuk, toplam 78 kişi yaşamını yitirdi. Orman yangınlarında 10 kişi yaşamını yitirdi. Kolluk güçlerine ait araçların karıştığı kazalar sonucu 20’si asker, 7’si mülteci, 1’i çocuk en az 29 kişi yaşamını yitirdi.

Ayrıca, kolluk güçlerinin silah kullanma yetkisini ihlal etmesi sonucu en az 3 kişi yaşamını yitirdi, en az 5 kişi yaralandı.

2025 yılında politik nedenler ya da ırkçı, ayrımcı, fobik saiklerle gerçekleştirilen en az 43 fiziksel ya da silahlı saldırı basına yansıdı. Bu saldırılarla en az 148 kişi doğrudan hedef alınırken, bu saldırılarda en az 15 kişi yaşamını yitirdi, en az 52 kişi yaralandı.

En az 9 gazeteci saldırıya uğradı. Hakan Tosun hayatını kaybetti. Dönemin CHP Genel Bşk. Özgür Özel fiziksel saldırıya uğradı. IŞİD ile ilişkili 2 saldırıda, en az 6 polis ve 6 silahlı örgüt militanı yaşamını yitirdi. En az 5 fobik saldırı tespit edildi. 1 trans kadın öldürüldü. 8 ırkçı saldırıda en az 14 kişi yaralandı. 12 yaşındaki mülteci çocuk evinde uğradığı saldırı sonucu öldürüldü. Fındıklı Belediye Başkanı saldırıya uğradı.

2025 yılında en az 1842 kişi işkence ve diğer kötü muamele niteliğindeki uygulamalara maruz kaldı.

Ankara’da gözaltında işkence gördüğü iddia edilen Musa Nargüner, tedavi gördüğü hastanede yaşamını yitirdi. 1’i geri gönderme merkezlerinde en az 90 kişi resmi gözaltı yerlerinde işkence ve kötü muameleye maruz kaldı. 1493’ü toplantı ve gösterilere yönelik kolluk müdahalelerinde olmak üzere, en az 1592 kişi resmi gözaltı yerleri dışında işkence ve kötü muameleye maruz kaldı. En az 185 mahpus hapishanelerde işkence ve kötü muameleye maruz bırakıldı.

2024 yerel seçimlerinden 2025 yılı sonuna kadar 27 belediye başkanı görevden uzaklaştırıldı, 13 belediyeye kayyum atandı. 16 belediye başkanı tutuklandı.

author: Victoria Valenzuela
title: US communities are organizing to end complicity with genocide in their backyards
content:
This article

US communities are organizing to end complicity with genocide in their backyards

 was originally published by

Waging Nonviolence

.


Dwight Hua’s roommate knocked on his door at 5:30 a.m. on May 22, saying there was a notice for

nearly 50,000 people in their city of Garden Grove

, California, to evacuate due to the danger of a deadly chemical explosion at a nearby GKN Aerospace plant. Hua quickly left for a shelter in a neighboring city. But he had a lot of questions. 


As the evacuation stretched over five days, advocacy groups VietRISE — where Hua is a youth programs coordinator — the Harbor Institute for Immigrant and Economic Justice, the Palestinian Youth Movement, and Orange County Justice for Palestine formed a coalition to demand “transparency about why a facility tied to global hazardous weapons manufacturing is operating in the middle of working-class immigrant neighborhoods.” Research led by the local chapter of the Palestinian Youth Movement, or PYM, found that the company manufactured parts for military vehicles, including F-35 fighter jets, which are used in Israel’s

ongoing genocide

 of Palestinians.


“No one really knew that this was what we were living close to,” Hua said. “A company that makes money off of violence abroad is not the character of Garden Grove and its residents.”


Many residents who, like Hua, live just blocks away from the facility felt enraged when they found out. The coalition joined the

People’s Embargo for Palestine

, an international movement to establish an arms embargo on Israel, and began organizing actions to push the city to shut down GKN Aerospace and place a moratorium on military manufacturing in Garden Grove. They have been canvassing, showing up to city council meetings and circulating a

petition that has drawn more than 11,000

 signatures. Addressed to the mayor and city council, the petition demands “an immediate end to the use of our tax dollars, public land and public infrastructure to manufacture, store or transport the weapons that make this genocide possible.” 


While the Garden Grove City Council has canceled meetings and omitted GKN Aerospace from meeting agendas in the months since the evacuation, Hua said, the coalition has kept on growing in size and influence. Members continue to show up to city council meetings, canvass and meet with city officials, some of whom have shown support for the embargo.


The campaign for a weapons embargo is part of a larger international movement to stop global manufacturing and shipment of weapons to Israel. From Türkiye to Italy to the U.S., localized campaigns targeted at Israeli weapons suppliers have emerged, led by community groups and unions, and often supported by PYM chapters. Their goal is to end local complicity in the genocide — and ensure worker and community safety — through bans on weapons shipments through local airports and seaports, as well as shutdowns and moratoriums on weapons manufacturing facilities in residential areas.


Putting communities at risk for Israel


A coalition of community groups is leading an embargo campaign in New York City’s John F. Kennedy Airport, where dangerous

explosives

 and F-35 bomber components bound for Israel have passed through the same runways as passenger flights. The campaign is calling on the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey to end arms shipments through public infrastructure. Most of the coalition’s efforts have been geared toward organizing and educating workers, especially unionized workers in warehouses and on planes. 


Sign Up for our Newsletter


We’ll send you a weekly email with the latest articles.


Abdullah Shehadeh, communications co-chair of Break the Chain, the coalition leading the campaign, said that workers were unaware they were handling explosives bound for Israel because they were mislabeled. 


“Workers feel very scared about what they’re doing in their day to day, not knowing that complicity like this is even possible for them,” Shehadeh said. “They didn’t sign up to be part of a supply chain of genocide.”


In outreach to workers, volunteers with the coalition also point out the dangers of handling explosives, noting that a

munitions plant in Tennessee

 which manufactured the same explosives experienced a blast last year that destroyed an entire building and killed 16 people. 


Organized by New York City’s Democratic Socialists of America chapter, Break the Chain was founded in 2025 by Palestinian …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Hospital Garrahan: persecución del gobierno contra Norma Lezana
content:
El ministro de Salud de la Nación, Mario Lugones, lanzó una campaña contra la Secretaria General de la Asociación de Profesionales y Técnicos (APyT) difundiendo que la misma habría sido despedida, lo cual nunca ocurrió. “Me quieren usar como cortina de humo para tapar los negociados turbios que estamos descubriendo”, declaró Lezana, refiriéndose al reciente informe que reveló que la cartera de Lugones desvió casi 60 mil millones de pesos del hospital Garrahan a inversiones financieras.


Norma Lezana. Foto: Maia Pauro


Con información de APyT, FM En Tránsito, Agencia FARCO y Periodismo de Izquierda.


En un acto en la puerta del Garrahan, tanto la propia Norma como su gremio aclararon que no recibió ninguna notificación formal de cese, que continúa ingresando a trabajar con normalidad y cuenta con la protección de sus fueros gremiales.


“Sin que haya mediado ninguna notificación formal a la licenciada Lezana, el ministro Mario Lugones en su cuenta de X, la página del Hospital Garrahan y en el medio A24 el periodista Eduardo Feinmann al aire, informaron y “festejaron” el “presunto despido de la emblemática profesional del hospital”, explicaron desde el sindicato, mediante un comunicado, en tanto que la misma Lezana lo desmintió también.


Lezana denunció que “es mentira que esté despedida. Primero, porque no fui notificada (y Lugones, Feinmann y la intervención lo anuncian como una “primicia”) y luego porque soy Secretaria General electa del sindicato que representa 24 profesiones del hospital y al conjunto de técnicos y trabajadores, y tengo protección gremial que sigue vigente, aunque Lugones y sus acólitos en el Garrahan crean que esto es una dictadura. No puede decidir ninguna cesantía, a pesar de no soportar que sea la única Secretaria General mujer, independiente y que no calla ante ninguna gestión”.


Foto: Maia Pauro


Lezana aseguró que “es evidente que están montando una cortina de humo atacándome a mí, para que no se sepa lo que estamos denunciando y empezamos a descubrir: contrataciones directas sin concurso, licitaciones millonarias sin rendición de cuentas de una empresa privada de seguridad o el uso de fondos por casi 60 mil millones de pesos del Garrahan en especulación financiera, mientras niegan la compra de prótesis y medicamentos para nuestros pacientes. No nos vamos a callar. No les tenemos miedo. Ninguna intervención autoritaria me va a sacar del Hospital”.


En este contexto, se realizó un acto este miércoles en la puerta del nosocomio, en defensa de Norma y del Hospital Garrahan.


Foto: Julieta Luna


Este ataque contra Lezana persigue un claro doble objetivo, plantearon desde el gremio. Por un lado, responde a una política de revanchismo del gobierno, que busca castigar a una de las referentes del histórico conflicto que el año pasado logró quebrar la pauta salarial oficial.


Al mismo tiempo, los trabajadores denunciaron que esta persecución, avalada por la dirección designada por Lugones, funciona como una cortina de humo para tapar graves irregularidades: contrataciones directas millonarias en seguridad privada y el desvío de casi 60 mil millones de pesos del presupuesto hacia la especulación financiera, todo mientras se niega la provisión de prótesis y medicamentos básicos para los pacientes.


Foto: Maia Pauro


Aquella lucha en el Garrahan demostró que es posible frenar las políticas de ajuste de Javier Milei mediante la más amplia unidad en la diversidad, la participación directa de las bases y la independencia política de todas las gestiones.


La plata de la salud de las infancias desviada a la bicicleta financiera


Un informe basado en documentos oficiales reveló que el Hospital Garrahan acumulaba más de 58 mil millones de pesos en inversiones financieras.


Escuchá el reporte de Sergio Lucarini, de Fm En Tránsito.


La Asociación de Profesionales y Técnicos del Hospital Garrahan (APyT) criticó al Ejecutivo por destinar fondos a la bicicleta financiera en lugar de volcar los recursos de forma directa a las necesidades urgentes y salarios del personal.


Voceros y cuentas oficiales del Gobierno intentaron desmentir la información, calificaron la noticia como falsa y aseguraron que se tergiversó la información contable y el desglose de los rubros del hospital.


Alejandro Lipovich, trabajador del Hospital Garrahan y secretario general de la Junta Interna de ATE, explicó en diálogo con

FM En Tránsito

: “Es algo similar a lo que sucedió el año pasado, a partir de distintos pedidos …

6μμ Άγαλμα Βενιζέλου


Στις 4 και τις 5 Σεπτέµβρη όλοι οι δρόµοι οδηγούν στην Θεσσαλονίκη στο αγωνιστικό διήµερο στα εγκαίνια της ∆ΕΘ. Στις 4 Σεπτέµβρη απεργούν και διαδηλώνουν τα νοσοκοµεία στις 8.30πµ στο Ιπποκράτειο Νοσοκοµείο της Θεσσαλονίκης και την επόµενη µέρα στις 5 Σεπτέµβρη, όλες και όλοι οι εργαζόµενοι συµµετέχουµε στο πανεργατικό συλλαλητήριο. Οι πυροσβέστες άνοιξαν το κύκλο καλώντας συλλαλητήριο στις 31 Αυγούστου και την ίδια μέρα η ΑΔΕΔΥ με τη στάση εργασίας.


΄Ωρα να βάλουμε την δική µας εργατική σφραγίδα στην πτώση του Μητσοτάκη, για να τελειώνουµε µε την κυβέρνηση των δολοφόνων, την κυβέρνηση του πολέµου και της καταστροφής: Νεκροί πυροσβέστες στο Ρέθυμνο, σύγκρουση ελικόπτερων και ολική καταστροφή στο Πόρτο Γερμενό, πανικός στη Χαλκιδική, νεκροί δυο ηλικιωμένοι στη Σαλαμίνα… Και δίπλα σε όλα αυτά είναι η ακρίβεια και η φτώχεια που θερίζει τα εργατικά νοικοκυριά, η διάλυση και η ιδιωτικοποίηση των δηµόσιων νοσοκοµείων, οι πάνω από 2.000 διώξεις εκπαιδευτικών που αντιστέκονται στην διάλυση του δηµόσιου σχολείου.


Χρειάζεται να οργανώσουμε αυτή τη μάχη σε κάθε χώρο εργασίας και γειτονιά για να ανέβουμε μαζικά με πούλμαν, να γίνει σταθμός για την ανατροπή της κυβέρνησης.


Να δώσουμε συνέχεια στην αντικυβερνητική οργή που ενώθηκε με την αλληλεγγύη στην Παλαιστίνη στις 9 Αυγούστου. Οι καταστροφές από τις πυρκαγιές εδώ ήταν η επιβεβαίωση για το πόσο κοστίζει ο «άξονας» του Μητσοτάκη με τον Νετανιάχου. Λεφτά υπάρχουν για το «θόλο» του Δένδια με το Ισραήλ, αλλά όχι για τη δασοπυρόσβεση. Δεν φταίει το κλίμα, φταίει το κέρδος. Οι ιδιωτικοποιήσεις σκοτώνουν από τα τρένα μέχρι τα δάση, αλλά ο Μητσοτάκης και οι υπουργοί του τρέχουν να ιδιωτικοποιήσουν τα Νοσοκομεία, την Παιδεία, το Νερό.


Όλο το προηγούμενο διάστημα έχουμε ξεκινημένους αγώνες στους χώρους: απεργία της ΑΔΕΔΥ κατά της πραξικοπηματικής “συνταγματικής αναθώρησης”, απεργίες στον Ασπρόπυργο και το Ελληνικό κατά των εργοδοτικών ατυχημάτων-εγκλημάτων για τα κέρδη των εταιριών, απεργία των ντελιβεράδων στην efood και την Wolt, στον επισιτισμό τουρισμό. Το Συνέδριο της ΔΟΕ αποφάσισε για απεργία μέσα στον Σεπτέμβρη. Και στα πανεπιστήμια φουντώνει η οργή για την ιδιωτικοποίηση.


Αυτή είναι η δύναµη της τάξης µας και αυτήν την δύναµη χρειάζεται να βάλουµε µπροστά στην ∆ΕΘ για να σιγουρέψουµε ότι η ανατροπή της Ν∆ θα ανοίξει δρόµους για το εργατικό κίνηµα. Για να κλιµακώσουµε απεργιακά και να κερδίσουµε όλα τα αιτήµατα για τα οποία παλεύουµε.


Ώρα να ενώσουμε τα ποτάμια της οργής και της αντίστασης στους χώρους δουλειάς. Να βρεθούμε μαζί εργαζόμενοι από τους “ήρωες των πυρκαγιών”, από τα νοσοκομεία, τα σχολεία, τους Δήμους, τα υπουργεία και τις υπηρεσίες, τον επισιτισμό, τις οικοδομές, τα εργοστάσια. Μαζί με τα ταξικά µας αδέρφια τους µετανάστες, µαζί με το κίνηµα αλληλεγγύης στην Παλαιστίνη.


Ελάτε να οργανώσουμε ένα μαζικό καραβάνι με πούλμαν για συμμετοχή στο εργατικό συλλαλητήριο στη ΔΕΘ το Σάββατο 5 Σεπτέμβρη στο Αγ. Βενιζέλου στις 6μμ όπου καλούν η ΑΔΕΔΥ και τα συνδικάτα. Μαζικά, ενωτικά έτσι ώστε η ανατροπή της κυβέρνησης να ανοίξει τον δρόµο για την εργατική προοπτική.


Αυτήν την προσπάθεια κάνει ο Συντονισµός Εργατικής Αντίστασης και σε καλεί να παλέψουµε µαζί.

title: KESK women to set new roadmap for struggle at congress
content:
The Confederation of Public Employees’ Trade Unions (KESK) will hold its 3rd KESK Women’s Congress from 4 to 6 September under the slogan “Resistance is our legacy, struggle is our promise.” KESK Women’s Secretary Döne Gevher read out the statement at the headquarters of the Agriculture and Forestry Public Employees’ Union (TARIM ORKAM-SEN). Gevher recalled that 150 women were killed as a result of male violence in the first six months of 2026, while 151 women died under suspicious circumstances. She pointed out that 61 percent of the women who were killed lost their lives in their own homes and said: “Women are being killed in the very homes where the government’s policies seek to confine us. Only eight of these women were under protection pursuant to Law No. 6284 at the time they were killed.”


Gevher also criticised the decision to withdraw from the Istanbul Convention and said: “Despite all this, the Justice and Development Party (AKP) government unlawfully withdrew from the Istanbul Convention. This unlawful situation has remained unaddressed for four years. Following the withdrawal from the Istanbul Convention, the number of femicides recorded in the first half of the year rose from 131 in 2021 to 150 in 2026.”


Women are being excluded from employment


Citing the “Women in Turkey with Statistics” report by the Turkish Statistical Institute (TUIK) and the United Nations Office in Turkey, Döne Gevher said that 64 percent of the country’s 33 million working-age women were outside the labour force. She said, “Although 21 million 548 thousand women want to work, they are unable to participate in the labour force because of care responsibilities and structural barriers. Three out of every ten employed women are also forced into informal employment.”


We will draw up a roadmap for our struggle


Gevher called on women to participate in the Women’s Congress and said they had been discussing the discrimination women face in areas ranging from education and healthcare to local government and the workplace, as well as the invisible burden of care work. She said war, authoritarianism and attacks on secularism were also among the issues being addressed. Gevher said, “We are now bringing this accumulated experience to Ankara. Starting on 4 September, we will spend three days sharing our experiences in a total of 15 workshops under five main themes. Through this congress, we will draw up a roadmap for our future struggle.”


Gevher said the Women’s Congress would bring together around 300 women delegates from trade unions affiliated with KESK and would address women’s labour, patriarchy and conservatism, violence, war, refugees and migration, as well as trade union struggle and organising. Gevher listed their demands as follows:


- The Istanbul Convention and Law No. 6284 must be fully and effectively implemented.


- Turkey must ratify the International Labour Organization (ILO) Violence and Harassment Convention No. 190. Women’s employment must be secure and full-time.


- Equal pay for equal work must not remain merely a slogan but must be put into practice.


- Public care services must be expanded.


- Women must be represented in decision-making bodies and at collective bargaining tables.


- De facto and legal barriers to trade union organising and the right to collective bargaining must be removed.


- Women’s right to organise freely must be guaranteed.

title: Quelques tags pour Gino, Zaid, Maja et les autres
content:
Soutien à Gino, Zaid, Maja, aux inculpé-es de Lyon et à toustes les autres.


Suite à l'annonce du verdict de la Cour d'Appel confirmant l'extradition de Gino vers l'Allemagne et à l'appel aux actions de soutien en sa faveur, un groupe organisé à décider de participer à la visibilisation de la répression des camarades pourchassé-es et enfermé-es pour leurs actions et leurs convictions politiques.


Parmi les plus médiatisés, le procès Antifa Ost continue en Allemagne, des camarades de l'affaire Budapest sont poursuivi-es en Allemagne et en Hongrie et les inculpé-es de Lyon sont enfermé-es en attendant leur jugement dans l'affaire Quentin. Un point commun : des personnes qui ont décidé de s'organiser pour se défendre face à la vermine fasciste la plus active en s'en prenant à leurs membres physiquement pour les empêcher d'agir.


Le fascisme n'est qu'un stade du capitalisme et le spectre de l'extrême droite ne doit pas nous faire oublier que ceux qui permettent leur ascension inquiétante en France et en Allemagne sont la classe politique institutionnelle allant des Verts/du

PS

 à la droite dite «

 

républicaine

 

». Nous sommes solidaires de toute action visant à freiner cette progression, qu'il s'agisse de brûler un local

PS

 ou de tabasser un nazi dans la rue. Il est plus que nécessaire aujourd'hui, à moins d'un an du cirque électoral habituel, de mettre en place des formes d'organisation collectives et autonomes : groupes d'autodéfense, comités de quartiers, assemblées locales mais aussi l'acquisition, par quelque moyen qui soi, de lieux et de moyens matériels. Face à ces formes d'organisation, la répression policière et judiciaire a rarement frappé aussi fort. Soyons solidaires de celleux qui s'y retrouvent confronté-es car iels n'ont pas leur place dans la logique capitaliste : sans-papier, fraudeur-se, voleur-se à l'étalage, cambrioleur-se et/ou tabasseur-se de faf etc. (quelques exemples)


Devant l'ampleur de la tâche à réaliser, quelques tags dans un quartier peuvent sembler dérisoire. Mais, nous y voyons 2 utilités. Premièrement, la présence à répétition sur plusieurs lieux de passages fréquentés peut interpeller les passant-es et pousser quelques personnes à s'informer sur ce sujet et ces affaires autrement que par les médias dominants. Deuxièmement, ce type d'opération peut être une première étape, un entraînement, une manière de gagner en confiance et en compétences en vue de réaliser d'autres actions plus ambitieuses : sabotage, attaques diverses etc.


En tout cas, nous pensons que c'est à la portée de beaucoup de personnes (attention aux caméras et aux voitures banalisées de flic la nuit) et nous préférerons toujours montrer notre solidarité ainsi plutôt qu'en repostant une story instagram avant de retourner à un train-train quotidien confortable.


Espérons que cette action puisse participer à soutenir Gino, Zaïd, Maja, Lina, les lyonnais-es et les autres. Des camarades.

author: By Sean Summers, Unicorn Riot
title: The US Brought the G20 to NC to Highlight the Region’s Hurricane Recovery. Locals Say the Government Wasn’t Who Made it Possible.
content:
Asheville, NC — Last weekend, the G20 finance ministers and central bank governors met in Asheville at the behest of the U.S. federal government. Billed as an opportunity to showcase the region’s recovery after Hurricane Helene laid waste to western North Carolina in 2024, locals took issue with their suffering and hard work being co-opted by representatives of the world’s richest countries.


After the Department of Treasury

announced

 in February that the meeting would take place in the Appalachian town, locals began organizing.


In the weeks before the meeting, organizers hosted a series of events and worked to spread the word about the finance ministers who had set their sites on Asheville’s Omni Grove Park Inn as their venue.


By the time delegates arrived on Saturday, August 29, a slew of organizations and unaffiliated locals had prepared a weekend of events to highlight that the often-overlooked meeting was taking place and emphasize that they, not the government or economists, were the ones who did the work of rebuilding the area after the storm.


Starting on Friday, groups of protesters took space on bridges spanning the interstate that runs by downtown Asheville. Holding banners, locals decried the presence of the finance ministers who arrived in their town that day. On at least three bridges, organizers draped banners with messages including “Asheville rejects technofascism” and “workers over billionaires.”


“We think they’re more focused on corporate interests and the interests of the wealthy over the interests of everyday people and working people,” Rachel Cohen, local policy lead of Sunrise Movement Western North Carolina, told Unicorn Riot.


Cohen’s suspicion is supported by the group’s history. The G20, or

Group of 20

, is a coalition of the world’s 20 largest economies made up of 19 member countries, the European Union and the African Union. The finance track, which meets four times a year leading up to the annual global summit, sets policy and determines the focus of the broader group.


Among the forum’s stated goals is to ensure economic stability and cooperation, but historically the body has worked to prop up capitalism in moments of crisis.


The G20 was formed in 1999 following the

Asian market collapse

 brought on by

financial manipulation

 from foreign investors who saw vulnerabilities in booming southeast Asian economies. After Thailand’s baht collapsed, the International Monetary Fund loaned Thailand and other countries caught in the turmoil billions of dollars to be repaid with interest, prompting a steep rise in unemployment, poverty and a decrease in social welfare spending.


In 2008, after the U.S. housing bubble burst and sent the economy into a tailspin, the G20 held its first global summit to respond to the crisis facing U.S. markets and capitalism’s legitimacy. Called by President George W. Bush to address a problem bigger than any one government could resolve,

the G20 assembled

 to develop solutions to the collapsing economy and ensure continued, perpetual growth.


Every year since, a member country has hosted the annual G20 summit as well as a series of satellite meetings that direct the group’s policies and mission. This year, the U.S. is hosting the G20, and last weekend’s gathering represented one of the finance track’s series of meetings leading up to the global summit to be hosted this December in Miami.


As vehicles honked in support during last Friday’s banner display, residents told Unicorn Riot that the G20 meeting in their town specifically to highlight the recovery post-Helene glossed over the reality of the situation.


Locals, like those waving banners from the bridges that afternoon, and nearby supporters responded to the crisis and are continuing the ongoing work of rebuilding the area, not the G20 or the entities they represent, Cohen said to UR.


The following morning, approximately 150 protesters spread out along Merrimon Avenue just north of downtown Asheville to oppose the meeting and continue to spread their message. There, along the busy thoroughfare, protesters waved signs and recalled who was present in the aftermath of the hurricane nearly two years earlier.


Lola Lafey, a local who lived through the storm, told Unicorn Riot that the first responders she saw were locals and neighbors, and that the federal government didn’t play as big a role as they needed to in the days after Helene.

title: Neuer Angriff auf die VVN-BdA und die Gemeinnützigkeit
content:
Neuer Angriff auf die VVN-BdA und die Gemeinnützigkeit


Die Bundesorganisation der Vereinigung der Verfolgten des Naziregimes – Bund der Antifaschistinnen und Antifaschisten (

VVN

-BdA) sieht sich einem Angriff auf ihre Gemeinnützigkeit gegenüber: Das Finanzamt Berlin hat eine außerordentliche Prüfung eingeleitet, weil es die antifaschistische Arbeit der Organisation als „unzulässige politische Betätigung“ einstuft. Ganz konkret verweist die Behörde auf die Bündniskampagnen gegen die AfD, an denen sich die Vereinigung beteiligt. Die

VVN

-BdA war nach der Befreiung vom

NS

-Faschismus von Überlebenden des

NS

-Terrors gegründet worden und engagiert sich bis heute gegen rechte Hetze und Krieg.

Bereits am 17. Juli 2026 schickte das Finanzamt für Körperschaften I Berlin der Bundesorganisation der

VVN

-BdA die Aufforderung, bis November vorzeitige Steuererklärungen der vergangenen drei Jahre einzureichen, da Zweifel an der Gemeinnützigkeit bestünden. Explizit benennt das Schreiben die von einem breiten Bündnis getragene Kampagne „Menschenwürde verteidigen – AfD-Verbot jetzt“. Die

VVN

-BdA fungiert als rechtlicher Träger des Gemeinschaftsprojekts und stellt auch das Spendenkonto zur Verfügung. Dass staatliches und gerichtliches Vorgehen gegen die faschistischen Umtriebe eingefordert wird, widerspricht dem Verständnis des Finanzamts von Gemeinnützigkeit. 

Ebenfalls ein Dorn im Auge der Behörden und der Rechtsaußen-Partei ist die Kampagne „Widersetzen“, die sich gegen Parteitage und andere Großveranstaltungen der AfD richtet. Durch massenhaften zivilen Ungehorsam und Blockaden konnten die rechten Versammlungen jeweils nur mit starker Verspätung und unter extremen Beeinträchtigungen stattfinden. Bereits kurz vor der vergangenen Großaktion von Widersetzen am 4. Juli 2026 in Erfurt hatten AfD-nahe Akteure gefordert, der

VVN

-BdA die Gemeinnützigkeit abzuerkennen, was in den Folgetagen von verschiedenen Medien aufgegriffen wurde und sich zu einer wahren Hetzkampagne entwickelte.

Mit dem Schreiben vom 17. Juli 2026 setzte das Finanzamt diese Forderung bereitwillig um und bedroht damit die älteste antifaschistische Organisation in ihrer finanziellen Handlungsfähigkeit. Das passiert nicht zum ersten Mal: Bereits 2019 hatte die Berliner Behörde der

VVN

-BdA die Gemeinnützigkeit aberkannt, musste dann aber wegen des breiten politischen Drucks und sogar internationaler Proteste einlenken. Nach der damaligen Schlappe hofft das Finanzamt wohl, sich beim aktuellen Vorstoß durchsetzen zu können.

„Es ist empörend, dass die staatlichen Behörden versuchen, über den Angriff auf die Gemeinnützigkeit antifaschistische Arbeit und zivilgesellschaftliches Engagement gegen rechte Hetze zu unterbinden oder zumindest kleinzuhalten. Ganz offensichtlich soll an der

VVN

-BdA ein abschreckendes Exempel statuiert werden, um auch andere oppositionelle Vereine und Organisationen mundtot zu machen“, erklärte Hartmut Brückner vom Bundesvorstand der Roten Hilfe e. V. „Umso notwendiger ist es, gegen diesen Repressionsschlag mit breiter Solidarität und Massenprotesten vorzugehen. Wir stehen an der Seite der

VVN

-BdA. Antifaschismus muss gemeinnützig bleiben – Wir sind alle Antifa!“

Pressemitteilung


Die

VVN

-BdA steht erneut im Visier des Berliner Finanzamts. Weil sie sich an Bündnissen und Protesten gegen die AfD beteiligt, droht der antifaschistischen Organisation der Verlust ihrer Gemeinnützigkeit.

title: World’s Largest Far Right Paramilitary Rallied in NYC. It Should Alarm Everyone.
content:
Five thousand people attended a rally in New York City led by the right-wing Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

On February 20, 1939, the Madison Square Garden arena in New York City hosted a chilling spectacle. A portrait of George Washington hung at the center of the arena, flanked by U.S. flags and swastikas. Over 20,000 people packed the stands to hear Fritz Kuhn, leader of the German American Bund — one of the most prominent U.S.-based organizations aligned with the Third Reich — project his vision of a “white, Gentile-ruled United States.” Outside, 100,000 anti-Nazi protesters clashed with police on Eighth Avenue, determined to stop the legitimization of European fascism on U.S. soil.

Eighty-seven years later, global leaders in ethno-fascism and their sympathizers returned to Madison Square Garden.

On August 29, 2026, 5,000 people gathered at Madison Square Garden to hear Mohan Bhagwat, the sarsanghchalak (Supreme Leader) of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS). As the ideological parent of India’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the RSS is the world’s largest far right paramilitary organization, with an estimated 4 million members spread over 73,117 branches across India. Just as the Bund attempted to leverage the image of George Washington to legitimize Nazism in their rally of 1939, the RSS used this invite-only event — apparently attended by 180 religious leaders from 30 countries — to sanitize a century-old project of Hindu fascism. Obscuring its extremist agenda, the RSS cloaked the gathering in the rhetoric of liberal multiculturalism, branding it with the theme “Universal Oneness.”

In his 42-minute keynote, the septuagenarian Bhagwat played the part of a playful but discerning uncle, dispensing meandering aphorisms about an “innate, eternal oneness” that connects humanity and nature. Rooting these concepts in the Atman (soul) and India’s civilizational values, Bhagwat painted a picture of a nation that champions “unity in diversity.” In a jarring contrast to his movement’s actual record, he claimed that India chooses to tolerate its enemies rather than subjugate them — elevating the country as a global exemplar of enlightened governance.

While Bhagwat spoke inside, an interfaith and anti-caste coalition protested outside. It consisted of groups like SALAM (South Asian Left), Hindus for Human Rights, and the Indian American Muslim Council, along with members of some of the 66 organizations that signed on to a statement earlier this week condemning Bhagwat’s visit. Their speeches exposed the hypocrisy of Bhagwat’s claim to “unity in diversity,” demonstrating how the RSS and its massive network of Hindu supremacist partners — including nearly a thousand nonprofit organizations, cultural organizations, paramilitary groups, unions, and political parties, collectively known as the Sangh Parivar (or the Family of the Sangh) — routinely practice the exact opposite of what Bhagwat preaches.

Speakers pointed out how the RSS’s notion of unity is, in fact, exclusively reserved for Hindus — and only for those who are wealthy and upper-caste. Shree Baphna from SALAM talked about how Hindutva (or the Hindu supremacist movement) attempts to divert mass anger “away from those in power and towards those communities who are exploited and oppressed.”

When a Dalit [lower caste person] demands land, dignity and the annihilation of caste, Hindutva says, ‘forget caste – you are Hindu. When an Adivasi [Indigenous person] defends jal, jungle, zameen [water, forests and land] against mines, dams and corporations – Hindutva says, ‘forget your history – you are a vanvasi – a child of the Hindu nation.’ Shame!

Ritu Gupta from the nonprofit Hindus for Human Rights, noted that Mohan Bhagwat is here “pretending to spread the message of oneness.” But this is not the message Bhagwat’s supporters spread in India, Gupta retorted. “In India they say, ‘Hindus only – everybody else, get out!’ These Hindus who support the message of purging India of its minorities do not represent all Hindus. There could be no bigger hypocrisy than this!”

title: Памяти "Сократа"
content:
Сегодня мы вспоминаем нашего товарища Алексея "Сократа" Сутугу, он умер ровно 6 лет назад. Сократ был настоящим антифашистом, идейным бойцом. Его яркая харизма, желание всем помочь, всех защитить сделали его очень заметной фигурой в анархистском и антифашистском движении. За это его ненавидели власти и немало времени ему пришлось провести в неволе. Но даже этот опыт он сделал оружием в борьбе с властями. Канал "Antifascist Post Every Day" напоминает слова Сократа из его книги "Диалоги о тюрьме":

"Есть отработанная тема: если ты слышишь, что пытают зека и ты точно знаешь, что это не провокация мусорская, ты должен заступиться за этого зека, потому что, если мы будем друг за друга заступаться, будет нормально все у зеков, мусора не будут так жестить, а если мы будем попустительством заниматься, начнут всех пиздить, вымогать деньги. Это общее людское понятие, ты должен заступиться вплоть до того, чтобы вскрыться, вскрыть вены, чтобы остановить насилие. Если ты этого не сделаешь, и об этом узнает братва, другие зеки, тебе скажут, ты что охуел так поступать, ты поступил как непорядочный, каждый порядочный должен заступиться за другого зека"

При всей своей известности в антифашистских кругах, у Алексея не было звёздной болезни. Он всегда оставался надёжным товарищем. Жизнь "Сократа" была такой яркой, что продолжает светить и новому поколению антифашистов.

Как сотрудничать с Автономным Действием

author: Wolfgang
title: Verfassungsschutz-Klausel gefährdet gemeinnützige Organisationen
content:
Dossier


Es begann mit einer

grundsätzlichen Sache

: 36 NGOs kritisieren geplantes Steuergesetz 2013 / Offener Brief an Bundestagsabgeordnete

:

„

Zivilgesellschaftliche Organisationen haben sich gegen ein Gesetzesvorhaben gewandt, das dem Verfassungsschutz ermöglichen würde, de facto über den Fortbestand gemeinnütziger Organisationen zu entscheiden. Sie forderten die Bundestagsabgeordneten jetzt in einem offenen Brief auf, dem Steuergesetz 2013, das morgen in erster Lesung im Parlament debattiert wird, ihre Zustimmung zu verweigern. Mit dem vorgelegten Gesetz will die Bundesregierung die Abgabenordnung (AO) so ändern, dass Organisationen, die in einem Verfassungsschutzbericht im Zusammenhang mit Extremismus genannt werden, die Gemeinnützigkeit ohne Prüfung entzogen wird (§ 51, Absatz 3, AO)

…“ (Presseerklärung vom 27.6.2012). Leider kamen schnell konkrete Fälle hinzu: dem Frauenverband

Courage e.V.

  und später auch

attac

 sowie

Doña Carmen e. V.

 wurde durch die jeweiligen Finanzämte die Gemeinnützigkeit abgesprochen, nun droht dies auch

VVN-BdA


 und

Campact,

  

DemoZ

  und

Change.org

 sowie

NachDenkSeiten

 und

innn.it e.V.

  und nun

Volksverpetzer

 – wir dokumentieren alle Aspekte der Problematik:


Grundsätzliches zur Gemeinnützigkeit


NRW-Landesregierung bekräftigt Recht auf politische Teilhabe gemeinnütziger Organisationen


„

Im April dieses Jahres stellte die AfD-Fraktion im nordrhein-westfälischen Landtag eine Große Anfrage zur „politischen Neutralität staatlich geförderter Organisationen“ (Drucksache MMD18-13444). Ziel war offensichtlich, gemeinnützige Organisationen – insbesondere solche, die sich für Vielfalt und gegen Rechtsextremismus einsetzen – durch das Infragestellen ihrer Gemeinnützigkeit politisch unter Druck zu setzen. In der Anfrage wurden konkrete Demonstrationen und teilnehmende Organisationen namentlich aufgeführt.


Die nun vorliegende Antwort des nordrhein-westfälischen Finanzministers (Drucksache 18-14721) ist eindeutig und unmissverständlich: Die Landesregierung teilt die Auffassung der AfD ausdrücklich nicht.

Stattdessen bekräftigt sie: Es gibt kein generelles Gebot politischer Neutralität für zivilgesellschaftliche, staatlich geförderte Organisationen – solange deren Aktivitäten im Rahmen ihrer satzungsgemäßen und gemeinnützigen Zwecke erfolgen. Gemeinnützige Organisationen dürfen sich politisch äußern, an Demonstrationen teilnehmen und aktiv an gesellschaftlichen Debatten mitwirken, sofern sie nicht parteipolitisch agieren.


Besonders deutlich wird dies in der Stellungnahme der Landesregierung:


– „Zivilgesellschaftliches Engagement im Zusammenschluss engagierter Bürgerinnen und Bürger, für ein friedliches, vielfältiges und respektvolles Zusammenleben, das auch menschen- und demokratiefeindliche Phänomene benennt und Extremismus sowie Radikalisierung entgegentritt, ist damit ein integraler Bestandteil der freiheitlichen demokratischen Grundordnung, der die Landesregierung uneingeschränkt verpflichtet ist.“ (S. 16)


–

„Während somit der Staat als Zuwendungsgeber selbstverständlich zur Neutralität verpflichtet ist, wäre es ein grundlegendes Missverständnis des freiheitlichen demokratischen Gemeinwesens anzunehmen, die der Sphäre der Zivilgesellschaft zuzuordnenden Zuwendungsempfängerinnen und -empfänger seien im Rahmen der Ausübung ihrer grundrechtlich geschützten Freiheiten ebenfalls zu politischer Neutralität verpflichtet.“ (S. 17)


Zudem stellt die Landesregierung klar, dass sie keine politischen Bewertungen zivilgesellschaftlicher Organisationen vornimmt und keine Informationen über deren politische Aktivitäten oder Ausrichtungen erhebt – weder im Rahmen von Förderentscheidungen noch darüber hinaus.


Antwort der Landesregierung: Drucksache 18-14721

 


Kurzbemerkung:


Eine erfreulich klare, überfällige und notwendige Antwort der NRW-Landesregierung: Es gibt kein Gebot politischer Neutralität für zivilgesellschaftliche Organisationen. Diese Position sollten sich auch AfD, CDU/CSU – insbesondere Politiker wie Merz, Linnemann und Söder – endlich zu eigen machen. Denn es war nicht nur die AfD, die nach der Bundestagswahl 2021 mit einer Kleinen Anfrage (551 Fragen!) versuchte, zivilgesellschaftliche Akteure wie CORRECTIV, BUND oder Greenpeace ins Visier zu nehmen.


– Hintergrundbericht bei Legal Tribune Online (LTO):

https://t1p.de/kdzgw

 


 – Handreichung des Paritätischen Gesamtverbands zur politischen Betätigung gemeinnütziger Organisationen …
