title: Der Server namens Paranoia: Verteidigt Autistici/Inventati vor dem 25.9.
content:
Seit fünfundzwanzig Jahren baut ein italienisches Hackerkollektiv eine Kommunikationsinfrastruktur auf, die Zensur, Überwachung und Polizeirazzien überstehen soll. Am 26. August stuften es die Vereinigten Staaten als terroristische Organisation ein. Am 25. September endet die Frist der Abwicklung.


Dieser Text ist eine Übersetzung von

«The Server Called Paranoia: Defend Autistici/Inventati Before September 25»

, vom 27. August 2026, von Sabot Media. Mit kurzem Kommentar und weiterführenden Ressourcen.


Es hätte eine dunkle und stürmische Nacht in einem italienischen Hacklab sein sollen.


Es war, ärgerlicherweise, ein schöner sonniger Sonntag.


Am 3. März 2001 versammelten sich rund zehn Personen im LOA Hacklab in Mailand um einen Computer, der aus ausrangierten Teilen zusammengebaut war. Eine Bank hatte ihnen einen alten Server zum symbolischen Preis von 15.000 Lire, etwa acht Dollar, verkauft. Sie bauten ihn mit ausgeschlachteten Komponenten, auch mit einer Festplatte von einem Heimcomputer, weiter aus. Niemand kam mit einem fertigen Bauplan. Softwarepakete wurden einzeln in Betracht gezogen. Jede Entscheidung wurde besprochen, bis alle einverstanden waren. Sie setzten bewusst die technisch am wenigsten erfahrene Person an die Tastatur. Der Prozess dauerte viel länger als nötig, weil Effizienz nicht das einzige Ziel war. Alle sollten verstehen, was sie bauten. An diesem Tag, erinnerte sich eine teilnehmende Person später, stellten sie fest: «A/I existiert jetzt.»


Sie nannten den Computer

Paranoia

. Im darauffolgenden Monat ging er online. Mit zwei Domains und zwei miteinander verflochtenen Geschichten: Autistici.org und Inventati.org. Fünfundzwanzig Jahre später, am 26. August 2026, stuften die Vereinigten Staaten Autistici/Inventati als Specially Designated Global Terrorist (ausgewiesene globale Terroreinheit) ein und setzten sie auf die Liste der Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (mit dieser SDN-Liste setzt die USA Sanktionen durch. Sie landet global in automatischen Screening-Listen und blockiert und erschwert Geschäfte).


Die Strecke zwischen diesen beiden Ereignissen – von einem recycelten Computer in einem Mailänder Hacklab zu den Mühlen des amerikanischen Sicherheitsstaates – ist die Geschichte eines Kollektivs, das ein Vierteljahrhundert damit verbrachte, auf einem gefährlichen Unterfangen zu beharren:


Personen sollten kommunizieren können, ohne sich zuvor Konzernen oder Regierungen zu unterwerfen.


Die unmittelbare Bedrohung hat jetzt ein Datum. Am 25. September läuft die Frist des US-Befehls aus. Institutionen müssen ihre Beziehungen zu A/I bis dann herunterfahren. Banken, Technologieunternehmen, Hosting-Anbieter und andere Institutionen werden angewiesen, verbleibende Beziehungen zu kappen. A/I baute seine Infrastruktur so, damit sie das Verschwinden eines Servers überlebt. Die Vereinigten Staaten versuchen nun, das Kollektiv wirtschaftlich und technologisch unberührbar zu machen.


Bleib dabei: Wir vertiefen, was A/I ist, zeichnen die Geschichte des autonomen Tech-Kollektivs nach und erkunden, was dieser neueste Angriff für Kollektiv und die breitere radikale Bewegung bedeuten könnte.


Vor A/I: Italiens Internet im Untergrund


Autistici/Inventati erschienen nicht aus dem Nichts. Seine Wurzeln liegen in mehr als einem Jahrzehnt italienischem autonomem Organizing, Piratenradio, Bulletin-Board-Systemen, besetzten sozialen Zentren, antikapitalistischen Bewegungen und Experimenten mit Computern als politischem Werkzeug. In den 1990er Jahren boten Netzwerke wie das European Counter Network und Isole nella Rete sozialen Bewegungen Online-Räume, als das Internet einem Grossteil der Öffentlichkeit noch unbekannt war. Italiens Hackmeetings brachten Programmierer*innen, Aktivist*innen, Künstler*innen und technologisch Neugierige in selbstverwalteten Räumen zusammen. Hacklabs ploppten in besetzten Sozialzentren auf, wo die Menschen Linux lernen, Netzwerke aufbauen und technisches Wissen als etwas anpacken konnten, das geteilt und nicht verkauft werden sollte. Die künftigen Mitglieder von A/I kamen aus verschiedenen Teilen dieser Welt. In Mailand verwendeten die mit dem LOA Hacklab verbundenen Personen den Namen

Autistici

, um ihre intensive Faszination für Technologie und ihren Wunsch, die darin verborgene Politik aufzudecken, zu beschreiben. In Florenz war das

Inventati

-Projekt mehr auf Kommunikation, Veröffentlichung und Bewegungsorganizing ausgerichtet. Zu den Projekten …

author: hiphop.de - Paul Kruppa
title: „Nazi Incels“: Kollegahs Alpha Gym nach Vandalismus beschädigt
content:
Kollegah

s Fitnessstudio „Alpha Gym“ hat anscheinend Besuch von Menschen bekommen, die dem Rapper und seinem Geschäftspartner Heidrich Kopelke eher weniger positiv gesonnen sind. So wurde die Fensterfront des Solinger Studios mit einem „

Nazi Incels

„-Graffiti bemalt. Der Polizei zufolge soll das Fitnessstudio zudem im Inneren beschädigt worden sein. Das

Solinger Tageblatt

 ist derweil an ein angebliches Bekennerschreiben gekommen.


„Alpha Gym“: Kollegahs Fitnessstudio wurde mit Graffiti bemalt


Im Rahmen der Tat soll das „Alpha Gym“ auch im Inneren einiges abbekommen haben. Das hat die Polizei dem Solinger Tageblatt gegenüber bestätigt. Im oben genannten Bekennerschreiben findet man dazu weitere Infos. So seien die Beschädigungen in den Innenräumen durch das Verteilen von Buttersäure verursacht worden.


In ihrem Schreiben machen die Verfasser übrigens auch Angaben zur Motivation hinter der Tat. Dort werden Kollegah und seinem Geschäftspartner nämlich Nähe zu „

ultrarechten Kreisen

“ vorgeworfen. Der Ton des Schreibens soll laut dem Solinger Tageblatt recht hämisch sein. So schreiben die Verfasser unter anderem Folgendes:


„Nicht nur die Fassade ist ziemlich schäbig, einige der Fenster (sind) beklebt und andere wiederum nicht. Außerdem merkten wir bei unserer Ankunft direkt einen unangenehmen Geruch. War das der Geruch einer fehlgeschlagenen Bosstransformation?“


Beendet wird das Schreiben, dessen Echtheit sich zum jetzigen Zeitpunkt nicht bestätigen lässt, mit der Nachricht: „

Antifa heißt Kampf.

“


Die Besitzer des Gyms haben laut Polizei übrigens eine Strafanzeige wegen Sachbeschädigung gestellt. Zudem haben die Behörden wohl das Schreiben an den Staatsschutz weitergeleitet.


Kollegah & Heidrich Kopelke: Kontakte ins rechtsextreme Milieu?


Unabhängig von der Echtheit des Schreibens machen schon die Graffiti auf der Fensterfront des Gyms recht deutlich, worum es bei der ganzen Sache geht.


Aller Wahrscheinlichkeit nach beziehen sich die Urheber der Sachbeschädigung dabei unter anderem auf die Kontakte von Heidrich Kopelke. Der Geschäftsmann soll laut einer Recherche der Süddeutschen Zeitung enge Verflechtungen zur rechtsextremen Szene und der Bekleidungsmarke Thor Steinar haben. Letztere gilt laut dem Verfassungsschutz Brandenburg als ein mögliches Erkennungsmerkmal für Personen der rechtsextremen Szene.

title: Commemorating and celebrating Gloria Steinem: The life and legacy of a feminist trailblazer
content:
3rd September 2026


Commemorating and celebrating Gloria Steinem: The life and legacy of a feminist trailblazer


9 min read


The world has lost an extraordinary champion for equality, and Equality Now has lost a beloved friend, mentor and member of our global family.


Gloria Steinem, the pioneering writer, feminist organiser and political activist, passed away at her New York City home on September 2, 2026, at age 92. For more than half a century, she helped shine a light on women’s rights and gave a voice to generations of women’s beliefs around what was possible for themselves and for each other. 


For Equality Now, Gloria’s loss is deeply personal. Our organisation was founded in her home and she stood alongside us from our earliest days, sharing her voice, wisdom, time and encouragement with extraordinary generosity. She was curious about women around the world, shaped especially by her formative years in India post-college.


“Gloria believed in the beauty of shared power. She used her own powerful voice to make space for millions of women’s voices and generations have stepped into their agency because she did. Her legacy is not only the world she shaped but is embedded in all of us who believe in that vision and continue to strive to achieve it,” said

Mona Sinha

, Chief Executive Officer of Equality Now.


“The world has lost one of its best, and I have lost someone who has been a north star in my own life. I first met Gloria when I was a student at Smith College but was blessed to come to know the woman behind her words and activism. What stays with me is her unconditional love of her chosen family, her extraordinary generosity of spirit, her infectious laugh and her curiosity and zest for women’s lives. For someone whose voice carried so much influence, Gloria had the remarkable ability to make space for everyone. 


“She listened to everyone who came to her Talking Circles. She genuinely wanted to hear your thoughts, your experiences and what you were excited to learn. She had this amazing ability to make everyone feel that their stories, their voices and their ideas mattered, which they did. While I will miss her enormously, I know she walks beside us in every movement she has inspired, in women who have stood up for change and the friendships she has nurtured. Each one of us feels a little braver because she embodied what courage looks like.”


Gloria Steinem’s enduring support for Equality Now and women’s rights


Gloria’s involvement with Equality Now as an active supporter of its mission spans the organisation’s entire 34-year history. She played an integral role as a founding member of Equality Now’s Advisory Board in 1992, served on the Board of Directors from 2010 to 2016, in addition to being a Trustee of Equality Now’s UK entity between 2005 and 2019.


At the United Nations, Gloria publicly supported Equality Now’s ongoing 

Words and Deeds

 campaign, which for almost three decades has highlighted sex discriminatory laws around the world and called for legal reform.


She stood with us against Big Apple Oriental Tours, a New York company promoting sex tourism in Asia, helping press authorities to act in a campaign that ultimately led to legal action against the company and strengthened the case for tougher anti-trafficking laws. 


For over 50 years, Gloria fought to strengthen legal protections for women and girls in the US by championing the Equal Rights Amendment (ERA), which would amend the US Constitution to guarantee equal rights under the law, irrespective of sex. In recent years, she worked alongside Equality Now and the ERA Coalition, helping build pressure on the Biden administration to recognise the ERA.

President Biden declared the ERA the law of the land

 in January 2025.


She was also a longstanding co-chair of Equality Now’s annual Make Equality Reality Gala,  helping the organisation to raise much-needed resources to protect and promote the rights of women and girls globally. In recognition of her tireless work to make equality a reality for everyone, Equality Now honoured Gloria for her lifelong commitment at the 2014

Make Equality Reality Gala

. 


A remarkable life


Born on March 25, 1934, Gloria’s life was a testament to her unwavering commitment to advancing gender equality and in the power of people coming together to create change.


In the 1960s, she made her mark as a journalist covering women’s rights and other social issues. She went on to become one of …

title: Hatimoğulları: Peace means freedom for Öcalan and Kurdish
content:
The Democratic Institutions Platform organised a march to mark 1 September World Peace Day, from outside NCity Shopping Centre to AZC Plaza in the Ofis district. Thousands of people joined the march, held under the slogan “We are marching towards peace with a free leadership,” alongside Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) Co-chair Tülay Hatimoğulları and representatives of political parties and civil society organisations.


Participants carried banners reading “Lasting peace is possible with the physical freedom of Abdullah Öcalan,” “Towards peace with a free leadership” and “Lice marches for peace to build a democratic society,” as well as a giant poster of Abdullah Öcalan. The crowd chanted slogans including “There is no life without the Leader,” “Long live Apo (A.Öcalan),” “A thousand greetings to Imrali,” “Long live peace,” “Martyrs never die” and “There can be no peace without the Leader (A.Öcalan).”


 


Applause, ululations and slogans accompanied the march, while participants lit up the streets with their mobile phone flashlights as darkness fell.


Democratic Regions Party (DBP) Diyarbakır (Amed) Provincial Co-chair Ahmet Doğan addressed the crowd outside AZC Plaza and said Abdullah Öcalan had demonstrated his commitment to peace through his persistent efforts over the years.


He said, “Abdullah Öcalan has once again extended his hand for peace and once again proved himself. We are a society that wants peace. No one should therefore test our patience. We have lived without a status for a hundred years. From now on, we will succeed. No one should have any doubt about that.”


Salute to those who build peace


Tülay Hatimoğulları then addressed the crowd, beginning her speech with the following words:


“Greetings from Amed to Imrali. Salute to those who build peace. Salute to those who have paid a price for peace. A thousand salutations to those who fell for freedom, democracy, justice, peace and fraternity.”


Hatimoğulları stressed that the suffering of the past must not be forgotten and continued:


“This process has, of course, begun with the aim of building an honourable peace without forgetting the suffering we experienced in the past, carrying their pain in our hearts and carrying the sacrifices that have been made in our hearts. Today, the martyrdom of many people from Turkey has been announced. Condolence gatherings are being held in many places. On this 1 September, as we speak of peace and intensify our struggle to build peace, I commemorate with respect and gratitude those who gave their lives.”


Peace means freedom for Mr. Öcalan


Hatimoğulları stressed that peace does not simply mean the silencing of weapons and said:


“There is a saying attributed to Mandela, one of the great symbols of peace: ‘Peace is not merely the silencing of weapons; peace is justice.’ Peace means justice. Peace means democracy, equality and fraternity. Peace means that a Kurd can receive education in their mother tongue. It means that all peoples can freely speak their mother tongues. Peace means that no journalist, intellectual, writer or politician is in prison. Peace means freedom for Abdullah Öcalan. Peace means that mine workers can receive their wages. Peace means that young people have a future in this country, that they are free, that they can work and study freely. Peace means a future for the youth. Peace means equality and freedom for women. It means a society without femicide and an end to violence against women. As women, we salute peace from here, and in the words of our own philosophy, peace means ‘Jin, jiyan, azadî’ (Woman, Life, Freedom).”


Mothers are united for peace


Tülay Hatimoğulları said lasting peace could only be achieved through democracy and stressed that peace is not a passive stance:


“The path to lasting peace runs through democracy, and the path to building democracy runs through lasting peace. Peace is never passivity. Peace is not about winning or losing. Peace means genuinely safeguarding democracy in this land. Peace is an active will. Peace is something that must be built with determination and courage. Honourable peace is the work of the courageous. Salute to those who have led this process and those who have paid a price for it.”

title: Inukjuak man accused of murder was ordered to not contact victim
content:
The Inukjuak man charged with first-degree murder for the death of his partner Elisabeth Qumak had been under a court order to not contact her when she was found dead inside a home in the community. 


Police

found

 the 41-year-old woman with stab wounds on Aug. 24, after Charlie Palliser arrived at the community’s police station to report he had committed a crime. She was pronounced dead at a local health centre.


The 45-year-old already faced charges for a break and enter and assault at Qumak’s home on July 17, court documents reveal. He was released on July 22 with conditions, including that he refrain from contacting her.


The Nunavik Police Service declined to comment on what happened on July 17, saying the investigation has since been handed over to provincial police in Quebec.


When reached by Nunatsiaq News, Quebec police also declined to comment.


Palliser had 

also given a curfew and was expected to attend social services meetings as well as activities organized by non-profit Saqijuq at least twice a month.


According to its website, the organization provides “alternatives to incarceration” by “promoting healthy lifestyles, strengthening cultural connections, and rehabilitating individuals.” It offers activities such as hunting, fishing and camping and workshops revolving around Inuit values and traditions. 


Nunatsiaq News asked Saqijuq if Palliser took part in any of their programs but has yet to hear back.


A Montreal-based coalition

of feminists against domestic violence

 has so far recorded 17 suspected

femicides in the province since the beginning of this year.


The figure is higher than what’s commonly reported in the media because the group monitors gender-based violence in situations that exclude romantic relationships, general co-ordinator Julie Antoine said in an interview. 


“It often happens that men are under no contact orders after a separation that they ultimately end up committing a femicide. Either the crime happens when the woman announces she wants to leave him, or the crime happens happens after an order is issued,” she said.


In about half of these 17 cases, she said, the group

 confirmed that the accused had previously been charged with a violent crime. 


“The state is falling in its role of protecting women, and it’s evident when you see that a high percentage of individuals involved in femicide cases were already known to the justice system,” Antoine said.


Palliser’s next court appearance is scheduled for Dec. 14.

author: Saneze Tshayana, Ana Stevenson, and Monica G. Fernandes
title: Wathint’ abafazi 70 years on
content:
The year 2026 marks the 70

th

 anniversary of the 1956

Women’s March

 against extending the

dompas

 to the black women of South Africa. Every August, the commemoration of Women’s Month highlights the inheritances and

unfinished legacies

 of women’s anti-apartheid resistance. This Women’s Month, it is timely to reflect on the legacies of women’s activism in South Africa over 70 years and more.


FEDSAW members in anti-Apartheid meeting


Organised by the

Federation of South African Women

 (FEDSAW), the 1956 Women’s March was a multiracial mass demonstration against pass laws. An estimated 20,000 women descended on Pretoria’s Union Buildings, presenting 14,000 petitions to

Prime Minister J.G. Strijdom

. Established in 1954, FEDSAW’s leadership, under luminaries such as

Lilian Ngoyi

,

Helen Joseph

,

Rahima Moosa

, and

Sophia Williams

, was particularly significant.


Previous women’s organising had arisen within the increasingly strict racial boundaries of the colonial and apartheid state. In 1913,

Charlotte Mannya Maxeke

 had led the

women’s anti-pass campaign

 in Bloemfontein, in the then Orange Free State. This led to the establishment of the

Bantu Women’s League

, which later became the

African National Congress

(ANC)

Women’s League

 in 1948. Similarly, the

Black Sash

, established in 1955, was an organisation of white women, bringing English-speaking women together with a smaller group of Afrikaans-speaking women. Alongside FEDSAW, these anti-apartheid resistance organisations were represented at the Women’s March.


The freedom song ‘

Wathint’ abafazi

, Strijdom!’, with the words ‘

Wathint’ abafazi, wathint’ imbokodo, uzu kufa!

’ (‘You strike a woman, you strike a rock, you will be crushed!’), featured at the 1956 protest. The

political slogan

 ‘

Wathint’ abafazi, wathint’ imbokodo

’ would become one of the liberation movement’s most enduring phrases, ricocheting across its posters and popular culture over the next four decades.


Yet, the slogan’s continued ubiquity into the twenty-first century belies the unevenness with which women’s activism has been recorded and remembered. Often invoked in popular memory, women’s activism has too often been marginalised against a celebration of men’s leadership, armed struggle, and formal political institutions.


A 2025

Special Issue

 of the

South African Historical Journal

, edited by Monica G. Fernandes and Ana Stevenson, centres women’s fight against apartheid. Spotlighting individuals and organisations, authors explore Ngoyi’s

urban roots

 and Williams’ formative experiences in the

youth movement

; uncover lesser known figures such as

Vesta Smith

 and

Joyce Piliso-Seroke

; consider Jewish social scientists Hilda Kuper and Ellen Hellmann’s

relationship

 with  scholar-activists of colour Fatima Meer and Regina Gelana Twala; revisit

Black internationalism

, the

Black Sash

, and the

ANC Women’s Section

; and critique

post-1994 literature

 about women’s experiences in the struggle.


This 70

th

 anniversary also offers a timely opportunity to consider women’s continuing activism towards realising the rights guaranteed in the 1996

Constitution

, 30 years later. Thanks to the efforts of various women’s groups as South Africa democratised, gender rights were enshrined in the final Constitution: in the

Bill of Rights

, gender is named as one of a slew of identifiers in anti-discriminatory legislation. However, the guarantees of gender equality have not gone unopposed, seen in South Africa most tellingly through the perniciously

high rates

 of men’s abuse of women, an enduring and insidious issue, more than 30 years into this democracy.


Legally, according to this Constitution, the status of South African women should be indisputable, protected as they are by gender-specific legislation against discrimination. Paradoxically, however, the ubiquity of men’s abuse of women, particularly in the context of intimate partner relationships, shatters any visions of constitutional equality.


Despite multiple

Presidential Summits

 dedicated to gendered violence, the drafting of the

National Strategic Plan on Gender-Based Violence and Femicide

 in 2020, and the establishment of the

Gender-Based Violence and Femicide (GBVF) Response Fund

author: CMI Argentina
title: Rosario: movilización contra los femicidios y en reclamo de la emergencia en violencia de género
content:
Las organizaciones decidieron movilizarse luego de que se conocieran tres femicidios en 15 días.


Foto: Aire Libre- Rosario


Escuchar el reporte de Darío Uliassi desde Aire Libre Radio Comunitaria.


Concentraron este miércoles a las 17 frente a la Municipalidad de Rosario y finalizaron con un acto en la puerta de la sede de Gobernación de la provincia en la ciudad.


De la movilización participaron organizaciones feministas, sociales y políticas que se expresaron en contra de la violencia machista y reclamaron justicia por los femicidios.


En la provincia de Santa Fe se registraron más de 30 femicidios en lo que va del año. Además, se contabilizaron 10 víctimas más que en el mismo período del año pasado.


“Paren de matarnos” fue la consigna que encabezó la movilización donde las organizaciones advirtieron por la suba de casos, que se profundizan con el desmantelamiento de las políticas de género en los distintos niveles del Estado.


En declaraciones a Aire Libre, Gabriela Sosa, referente del movimiento feminista Mujeres por la Matria Latinoamericana (Mumalá), exigió la sanción de una ley provincial que declare la emergencia en violencia de género y que se cumpla la ordenanza local que declaró la emergencia hace un tiempo.


“Hemos presentado proyectos para que se declare la emergencia en violencia de género en Santa Fe y también que se pueda aplicar aquella ordenanza de hace varios años que ya declaraba la emergencia en Rosario y que disponía de recursos que siguen estando pendientes”.


Foto: Aire Libre- Rosario


Sosa también denunció las consecuencias del desmantelamiento de políticas públicas: “Esta quita de recursos, a la par de los discursos de odios, comienzan a impactar que las mujeres cada vez denunciamos menos, un 9% de la víctimas habían denunciado a su agresor anteriormente”.


Y agregó: “Por supuesto faltan campañas de prevención, faltan que los medios de comunicación tengan pautas de los estados municipales, provinciales y nacionales para informar de qué hacer”.


Fuente:

https://agencia.farco.org.ar/2026/08/27/rosario-movilizacion-contra-los-femicidios-y-en-reclamo-de-la-emergencia-en-violencia-de-genero/


La entrada

Rosario: movilización contra los femicidios y en reclamo de la emergencia en violencia de género

 se publicó primero en

Indymedia Argentina Centro de Medios Independientes (( i ))

title: Llenado del embalse de la central hidroeléctrica Los Lagos, un reconocimiento expreso de la violación a la debida diligencia por parte de Statkraft
content:
La confirmación de Statkraft refuerza la urgencia y la pertinencia de la queja presentada por el Aylla Rewe del Ngen Mapu Kintuantü ante las autoridades noruegas por posibles incumplimientos de las obligaciones de debida diligencia en materia de derechos humanos.


COMUNICADO DE PRENSA.


«Territorio del Pilmaykén, 26 de agosto de 2026. – Como Aylla Rewe del Ngen Mapu Kintuantü, recibimos con profunda preocupación la confirmación formal por parte de Statkraft de que concluyó el llenado del embalse del proyecto hidroeléctrico Los Lagos, en la cuenca del río Pilmaiquén.


Durante años hemos advertido públicamente sobre las consecuencias que este proyecto puede tener para nuestros derechos como pueblo Mapuche Williche, nuestra relación con el territorio, nuestra espiritualidad, nuestra cultura, nuestra memoriay nuestras formas de vida.


También es información pública que, dentro del territorio involucrado, existen espacios de profundo significado espiritual y cultural para nuestro pueblo y que en la zona se realizaron hallazgos arqueológicos y bioantropológicos de los cuales la empresa tenía conocimiento.


La empresa y las autoridades conocían estas preocupaciones antes de que se completara el llenado del embalse. Aun asi, la empresa decidió seguir adelante. La confirmación del llenado del embalse es una prueba flagrante de la violación a los estándares de debida diligencia corporativa en materia de derechos humanos y de la desatención a las voces y llamados reiterados de las comunidades.


Esta confirmación no resta importancia a las acciones legales que hemos impulsado. Por el contrario, confirma precisamente la urgencia y pertinencia de la queja que presentamos hace unas semanas ante la Autoridad de Consumo de Noruega, con el acompañamiento legal del Proyecto de Derechos Económicos, Sociales y Culturales (ProDESC) y de la Iniciativa para la Justicia Transnacional. (IJT), en la que solicitamos que se investigue si Statkraft cumplió adecuadamente con sus obligaciones de debida diligencia en materia de derechos humanos.


Para nosotros, trasladar elementos materiales no sustituye ni repara la relación espiritual, cultural y territorial de la que forman parte.


Como Aylla Rewe, hemos utilizado durante años las distintas vías legales e institucionales disponibles para exigir el respeto a nuestros derechos y que Statkraft cumpla con su obligación de debida diligencia.

Hemos participado e impulsado procesos relacionados con la consulta indígena, recurrido a instancias judiciales nacionales y presentado una queja ante el Punto Nacional de Contacto de Noruega por posibles incumplimientos de las Líneas Directrices de la OCDE para Empresas Multinacionales.


Ante la ausencia de una respuesta capaz de prevenir las afectaciones que veníamos advirtiendo, hace unas semanas nos vimos obligados a acudir nuevamente a las propias instituciones noruegas y presentar una queja al amparo de la Ley de Transparencia.

No llegamos a esta instancia como primera opción.

Llegamos después de años de utilizar mecanismos legales e institucionales para exigir que nuestros derechos fueran respetados antes de que el territorio fuera transformado.


Por eso, la confirmación del llenado del embalse vuelve la queja aún más urgente.

La debida diligencia en materia de derechos humanos no puede reducirse a cumplir procedimientos formales o a elaborar informes. Su función sustantiva es identificar los  riesgos, prevenir sus impactos, mitigarlos y actuar antes de que las afectaciones se materialicen.


Lo informado refuerza nuestra preocupación de que las advertencias de las comunidades y los riesgos para nuestros derechos no hayan sido atendidos de manera efectiva antes de que el proyecto avanzara y produjera transformaciones materiales en el territorio.


Ahora estamos documentando y verificando directamente el alcance de las afectaciones derivadas del llenado. Sin embargo, este proceso es sumamente complejo, pues, como es de público conocimiento, las comunidades no tienen acceso al sitio de construcción de la Central Los Lagos ni a sus zonas aledañas, ya que el área está resguardada por guardias privados de la empresa y por tanquetas apostadas en los caminos.


Esta situación confirma nuevamente que nuestro derecho de acceso a la información y a la participación en las decisiones que afectan nuestro territorio ha sido sistemáticamente vulnerado: ni las autoridades ni la empresa han garantizado su pleno ejercicio. Resulta especialmente grave que …

title: Sumario sin secreto: el “Gordo Leyes”, abogado de Cerimedo en Argentina, debería ser llamado a declarar en Bolivia
content:
Fachos del carajo. El Gordo Leyes y el detenido por intento de femicidio | Captura de video


El fascista Alejandro Sarubbi Benítez asegura que maneja “todo lo que hace acá” el exasesor de Milei y creador de La Derecha Diario que ahora está preso por intentar matar a su pareja. ¿Qué sabe de los hechos y cómo encubre a su “cliente” el stramer que desde la cloaca Carajo destila mensajes de odio y violencia? ¿Podría ser imputado por encubridor?

Por Daniel Satur (La Izquierda Diario).


Desde la medianoche del viernes el 

operador mediático-digital de la ultraderecha latinoamericana

 

Fernando Cerimedo

 cumple prisión preventiva en el penal Palmasola, 

Bolivia

, acusado de haber planificado el femicidio de su pareja 

Nadia Beller

, quien el lunes 17 fue 

acribillada a balazos

 por dos sicarios y salvó su vida de casualidad.


Paralelamente, el Poder Judicial boliviano abrió 

otra causa contra Cerimedo

 por presunto 

“enriquecimiento ilícito”

, ya que en varios allanamientos a sus propiedades en el país vecino se secuestraron 

grandes sumas de dinero

 sin justificar y material más que comprometedor.


Como lo definió 

Fernando Rosso

 en 

su editorial del sábado

, 

Cerimedo

 “encaja bastante bien” como símbolo de

 esa 

lumpen-casta

 

que la ultraderecha continental creó

 a partir del rejunte de “empresarios quebrados, periodistas de dudosa reputación, subcelebridades, 

traders

, 

coaches

 mediocres, policías, militares e influencers que encontraron en la radicalización política la posibilidad de una nueva carrera, no para progresar, sino para trepar”. Ahí están también 

Manuel Adorni

 y 

José Luis Espert

, claro.


En Argentina, parte de esa 

troupe

 que acompaña al Gobierno de 

Javier Milei

 la integran los 

“influencers”

 que a diario destilan violencia y odio a través de sitios como 

La Derecha Diario

 

y canales como 

Carajo Stream

 

. Personajes por demás crípticos que conviven, transan y comparten negocios dentro de un mismo ecosistema mal llamado libertario.


Por caso, el pasquín de 

fake news

 (creado para la “batalla cultural” contra 

La Izquierda Diario

) fue cofundado por le mismo 

Cerimedo

 y su esposa 

Natalia Basil

; mientras que en el canal de 

Youtube

 que regentea 

Daniel “Gordo Dan” Parisini

 despunta el vicio comunicacional el abogado 

Alejandro Sarubbi Benítez

, conocido en redes como 

“Gordo Leyes”

 y nada menos que defendor en Argentina de 

Cerimedo

.


En línea con el estilo libertariano, a 

Sarubbi Benítez

 no le importa quedar como 

un chanta consuetudinario

 con tal de 

propalar cualquier fruta

 como si fuera una “primicia”. En junio pasado llegó a decir que tenía “información” indubitable sobre la ausencia del cuerpo del 

Indio Solari

 en el ataúd ante el que pasaron cientos de miles de ricoteras y ricoteros.


Nadia Beller horas después del atentado contra su vida | Captura de video


“Unas complicaciones”


Sarubbi Benítez

 conduce en 

Carajo

 el programa 

La Trinchera

. El jueves de la semana pasada, cuando

 

su amigo ya llevaba dos días y medio detenido en Santa Cruz de la Sierra, habló por primera vez del tema. Usó unos pocos segundos para decir que venía de 

días complicados

 y con “dolor de cuello” por “todo el quilombo 

Cerimedo

”. Y agregó: “No es ningún misterio que yo 

soy abogado de él acá

, lo que significa básicamente 

asumir yo todo lo que él hace acá

 y eso trae unas complicaciones”. Claramente, los une algo más que una mera relación profesional de letrado-cliente.


Fingiendo serenidad, el 

Gordo Leyes

 agregó: “No hablé mucho de este tema, porque, ehhhh, bueno, hay una causa… Pero ya me pude hacer de esa causa… Todo lo que dijo la mina públicamente, de manera oficial declaró lo contrario. Así que bueno, probablemente es 

algo que termine siendo resuelto en las próximas horas

. Pero, literalmente, fue exactamente al revés. Cuando haya alguna novedad voy a hablar de eso y, además, me voy a quedar con la exclusiva”.


Desde su cuenta de 

X

, 

Sarubbi Benítez

 sumó que “en el informe psicológico de la causa, 

Nadia Beller

 declaró exactamente lo opuesto a lo que dijo públicamente: que el supuesto atentado podría haber tenido a 

Cerimedo 

como objetivo, que nunca la amenazó, ni tampoco se sintió amenazada de algún modo”. Y denunció “una operación bastante obvia” contra su amigo y contra el gobierno de 

Rodrigo Paz

, del que 

Cerimedo

 es influyente asesor.

title: Cinsiyetçi Teknik Direktör'e tepki
content:
Türkiye Futbol Federasyonu 1'nci liginde oynayan Muğlaspor'un geçtiğimiz günlerde basınla tanışma toplantısı vardı. Toplantıda Teknik Direktör Yalçın Koşukavak'ın kadın gazetecilere yönelik cinsiyetçi sözleri tepki topladı. Muğlaspor Teknik Direktörü Yalçın Koşukavak’ın kadın gazetecilere yönelik “Bilsem kısırımı da altınımı da alırdım, gün yapardık” ve “Sizde şimdi soru da yoktur” sözlerine kadın gazeteciler ve kadın örgütleri tepki gösterdi. Muğlaspor Kulübü ise sözlerin “espri amacı taşıdığını” ve bağlamından koparıldığını savundu.


Muğlaspor Teknik Direktörü Yalçın Koşukavak ile 20 Ağustos’ta Muğla’nın Akyaka Mahallesi’nde futbolcular, aileleri, teknik heyet ve basın mensuplarının katıldığı bir kahvaltı etkinliği düzenlendi. Toplantının başında kulüp başkanı ve yöneticiler mekandan ayrıldı. Koşukavak'ın basın toplantısı için hazırlık yapılırken gazetecilerin oturduğu masa teknik direktör için hazırlanmaya başladı. 


Kahvaltığı basın toplantısını 7 kadın ve 4 erkek muhabir takip ediyordu. Koşukavak, sözlerine "Daha önce basın toplantısında bu kadar bayan görmemiştim. Sizde şimdi soru da yoktur. Bilsem kısırımı da altınımı da alırdım, gün yapardık" diyerek başladı.


Etkinlikte yaşananları Mabolla Medya muhabiri Esma Turan; Koşukavak’ın sözlerini ise Bodrum Kadın Dayanışma Derneği’nden Figan Erozan ve Evrim İnan bianet’e değerlendirdi.


Turan: Bu sözleri 'espri' olarak değerlendirmiyorum


Mabolla Medya muhabiri Esma Turan, kahvaltı etkinliğinde bulunan kadın gazetecilerden biriydi. Etkinlik öncesi ve sırasında yaşananları anlatan Turan şöyle konuştu:


“Toplantı öncesinde kulüp başkanı, yöneticiler ve futbolcular ile kahvaltı yapıldı. Kahvaltı sonrasında sadece hocanın açıklama yapacağı söylendi. Aslında bir tanışma ve değerlendirme toplantısıydı. Yalçın Bey ile ilk basın toplantısı ve tanışma olacaktı. Kulüp başkanı ve yönetimi mekândan ayrıldı. Bizim masamız basın açıklaması için hazırlanıyordu. Biz mikrofonları hazırlarken hoca geldi, daha masaya oturmadan ve merhaba bile demeden kısır muhabbetini yaptı.”


Turan’ın aktardığına göre gazeteciler önce ne olduğunu anlamadı, ardından “Biz de gün yapmıyoruz burada” diyerek tepki gösterdi. Bunun üzerine Koşukavak, “Sizde soru da yoktur şimdi” dedi.


Turan, toplantıda yaşananları şöyle anlattı:


“Biz de kaldık, dinledik açıkçası. Ne yapacağımızı bilemedik yani kal geldi o sırada galiba. Sonradan keşke kalkıp gitseydik dedik. Sorularımız vardı, onları da sormadık. Erkek meslektaşlarımız da soru sormadı. Sadece Yalçın Bey konuştu. 7 kadın ve 4 erkekti gazeteciler.”


Tepkilerin toplantı sonrasında gazetecilerin kendi aralarındaki değerlendirmeleri ve konunun haberleştirilmesiyle ortaya çıktığını belirten Turan, “Haber yapmasalar olur mu? Kulübe zarar gelmesin, cumartesi maç var” denildiğini söyledi.


Koşukavak’ı kişisel olarak hedef almak veya Muğlaspor’a zarar vermek gibi bir amaçlarının olmadığını vurgulayan Turan şöyle devam etti:


“Muğlaspor, bu şehrin önemli bir değeri ve hepimiz kulübün başarılı olmasını istiyoruz. Biz orada söylenen sözleri duyduğumuz şekliyle, kayda geçtiği biçimiyle kamuoyuna aktardık.”


Muğlaspor Kulübü’nün olayın ardından yayımladığı açıklamaya katılmadığını belirten Turan, “Sizde şimdi soru da yoktur” ifadesini kadınların mesleki yeterliliğini ve gazetecilik mesleğini cinsiyet üzerinden değerlendiren bir yaklaşım olarak yorumladı.


Kadınları kamusal alandan dışlayan bir pratik


Bodrum Kadın Dayanışma Derneği de sosyal medya hesabından Koşukavak’ın sözlerine ilişkin bir açıklama yayımladı.


Açıklamada, “Bunu bir kişinin nezaketsizliği olarak değil, erkek egemen kurumların kadınları kamusal alandan dışlama pratiği olarak görüyoruz” denildi.


Koşukavak’ın “kısır” ve “altın günü” ifadelerine de tepki gösterilen açıklamada şöyle denildi:


“‘Kısır’ ve ‘altın günü’ üzerinden kurulan alay, kadınların dayanışma pratiklerini ve mesleki kimliklerini aynı anda küçümsemektedir.”


Muğla Barosu ve Menteşe Kadın Platformu: Münferit bir şaka değil


Menteşe Kadın Platformu ile Muğla Barosu Kadın Hakları ve Toplumsal Cinsiyet Eşitliği Komisyonu da Koşukavak’ın ifadelerine ilişkin ortak bir açıklama yayımladı.


Açıklamada Koşukavak’ın sözlerinin “münferit bir şaka” olmadığı belirtilerek şöyle denildi:


“Bu söylem; sporu, basını ve kamusal alanı yalnızca erkeklere ait gören, kadını ev içi rollerle, geleneksel kalıplarla ve edilgenlikle tanımlamaya çalışan ataerkil zihniyetin yansımasıdır.”

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: Right(s) Up: Transfemicide as trans women rights violation
content:
Kierra Apostol. (Contributed photo)

Context: Transfemicide is a word used by trans-led organizations to define the pattern of killings of trans women and transfeminine people rooted in transphobia, misogyny, hatred, and systemic violence often compounded by intersecting forms of discrimination and marginalization

Human rights: Civil and political rights, economic, social, and cultural rights, gender justice

Rights-holder: Trans women and transfeminine people

Duty-bearer: Philippine government

MANILA – The Philippines has the most number of transgender women murder.

The Society of Trans Women of the Philippines (STRAP) raised this point at the launch of Project Kierra, a trans-led initiative that seeks to document the killings and campaign for justice.

The project was named after Kierra Apostol, an 18-year-old trans woman killed in June 2025.

“When it is not documented, it is easily erased in public memory,” STRAP Executive Director Vashti Ortego said. “We hope to transform not only a word, I hope that it will enter the vocabulary of the institutions and revisit their laws and policies.”

Read: Recent killings of trans women prompt groups to push for LGBTQIA protection

According to Trans Murder Monitoring, the Philippines had 107 documented trans women killings since 2009. In contrast, Singapore and Cambodia had 1; Thailand, 27; Indonesia, 13; Myanmar, 5; and Malaysia, 16.

Doms Cordero, co-author of the book Transfemicide in the Philippines published this year, noted that the number may even be higher since the cases are underreported and even misreported. One challenge they identified is the domestic reporting mechanisms remain limiting: the Philippine National Police’s reporting forms remain binary– with only male and female as their markers.

“Some of them are deadnamed even in reports. These are not legal documents. We seek to honor the lived experiences of trans women. They’re already dead, and we are killing them again (by using their legal name),” Cordero said, adding that they have not yet documented transgender women who even used the anti-Violence Against Women and Children (VAWC) desk of the Philippine National Police because of the fear of being misgendered.

Read: Brutal killing of trans woman in Caloocan prompts calls for investigation, passage of SOGIE bill

In 2025, the Commission on Human Rights (CHR) flagged that the pattern of trans killings in the Philippines is already a transfemicide. From 2025 to present, there are 15 documented trans women killings.

On January 15, 2025, Ren Tampus, a 35-year old beauty salon owner, died in hospital after being shot by a gunman who invaded one of her salons. Six days later, trans woman Shalani Dolina suffered a brutal killing. Her severed leg was found stored in an ice cooler, while her body was wrapped in a mattress.

Trans woman revolutionary Dahlia Supelanas was killed by the Philippine military, together with six other people in a clash, on April 27, 2025. While trans rights activist Ali Macalintal was shot several times inside her massage and spa clinic on June 23, 2025, in General Santos City.

Kierra Apostol, an eighteen-year-old trans woman, was found dead in a river two days after she had gone missing, with her body showing signs of physical assault. STRAP said that the suspect behind her killing was already arrested in September 2025.

Jerico Elliorate was killed by stabbing multiple times by a person she met at a party. Her killer then stole her wallet on August 14, 2025. A trans woman named Christine, who was also a 44-year-old therapist, was found dead inside a rented apartment in Valenzuela City, on September 22, 2025.

Another trans activist was killed at the hands of state forces. On April 19, 2026, Filipino American Kai Sorem was killed by the Philippine military, together with 8 civilians and 10 revolutionaries in a massacre in Toboso, Negros Occidental.

On June 20, 2026, 20-year-old trans woman Bella Lutap was found dead in an irrigation canal in Sitio Burnao, Zaragoza after being reported missing for three days. The Nueva Ecija police identified her ex-boyfriend as the primary suspect. He was arrested and charged with murder.

Teddy Federico, a trans woman, indigenous youth leader, and a barangay agricultural worker was found dead eight days after being reported missing, July 15, 2026. The investigation into her death is still ongoing.

Betty Benito, a trans woman from Malaybalay City, Bukidnon, was reported dead in a dense …

title: Συγκέντρωση ενάντια στις πειθαρχικές διώξεις των εκπαιδευτικών του 3ου ΔΣ Ραφήνας, Παρασκευή 4/9, στο ΠΣΑΔΔΤ (Νηρηίδων 10), Αθήνα
content:
Τη Παρασκευή 4/9, στις 09.30, στο Πειθαρχικό συμβούλιο ανθρώπινου δυναμικού δημόσιου τομέα (ΠΣΑΔΔΤ Νηρηίδων 10), 12 εκπαιδευτικοί

 του 

3ου Δημοτικού Σχολείου Ραφήνας

 διώκονται στο

Πειθαρχικό Συμβούλιο Ανθρώπινου Δυναμικού Δημοσίου Τομέα (ΠΣΑΔΔΤ)

 για κατηγορίες όπως η «δυνητική αργία», παράβαση υπαλληλικού καθήκοντος και άρνηση εκτέλεσης καθηκόντων. Σύλλογοι Εκπαιδευτικών, οργανώσεις και τοπικές πρωτοβουλίες καλούν σε συγκέντρωση ενάντια στις διώξεις των εκπαιδευτικών, τις τρομοκρατικές πολιτικές του κράτους απένταντι στους/τις αγωνιζόμενους/ες εκπαιδευτικούς/ες και καλούν τους εργαζόμενους στην εκπαίδευση σε 3ωρη στάση εργασίας κατα τη διάρκεια της κινητοποίησης.


Καλέσματα:


Σύλλογος Εκπαιδευτικών Π.Ε. “Αλέξανδρος Δελμούζος”


Τ

ο Δ.Σ. του Συλλόγου μας καταγγέλλει με τον πλέον κατηγορηματικό τρόπο την πρωτοφανή και αυταρχική δίωξη των μελών του, εκπαιδευτικών, του 3ου Δημοτικού Σχολείου Ραφήνας.


Οι συναδέλφισσές μας παραπέμπονται στο Πειθαρχικό Συμβούλιο την Παρασκευή 4 Σεπτέμβρη με το ερώτημα της «δυνητικής αργίας», επειδή έπραξαν το αυτονόητο παιδαγωγικό τους καθήκον, υπερασπίστηκαν το δικαίωμα των μαθητών τους στη μόρφωση και διαμαρτυρήθηκαν για τις αντιεκπαιδευτικές συγχωνεύσεις τμημάτων και το στοίβαγμα των μαθητών τους, που έγιναν στο σχολείο τους ενώ είχε ξεκινήσει η σχολική χρονιά.


Η απόφαση της διοίκησης και του Υπουργείου να σύρουν τις συναδέλφισσες στο Πειθαρχικό με το ερώτημα της “δυνητικής αργίας” αποτελεί μια άθλια μεθόδευση οικονομικής, επαγγελματικής και ηθικής εξόντωσης. Αποδεικνύεται περίτρανα αυτό που λέγαμε πριν ένα χρόνο στα τέλη Αυγούστου όταν ψηφιζόταν στη Βουλή το νέο πειθαρχικό δίκαιο των Δ.Υ., ότι δεν είναι ένα κανονιστικό πλαίσιο αλλά ένα όπλο μαζικής τρομοκράτησης που επιστρατεύουν το ΥΠΑΙΘΑ και η κυβέρνηση, προκειμένου να επιβάλλουν σιγή νεκροταφείου στα σχολεία και να τσακίσει κάθε εστία αντίστασης απέναντι στον σχεδιασμό της για παραπέρα εμπορευματοποίηση και κατηγοριοποίηση των σχολείων, απέναντι στις περικοπές και συγχωνεύσεις τμημάτων και σχολείων. Άλλωστε είναι γνωστό πλέον ότι τα λεφτά για την παιδεία και την υγεία αποδίδονται στην ενίσχυση της πολεμικής οικονομίας.


Η επιβολή του καθεστώτος της δυνητικής αργίας —που στερεί βίαια από τον εκπαιδευτικό τη δουλειά του και το ψωμί της οικογένειάς του πριν καν δικαστεί— συνιστά ευθεία παραβίαση του τεκμηρίου της αθωότητας και θυμίζει μαύρες εποχές. Θέλουν να εξοντώσουν τις συναδέλφισσες παραδειγματικά για να φοβηθούν οι υπόλοιποι. Δεν θα τους περάσει!


Το εκπαιδευτικό κίνημα έχει αποδείξει ότι δεν σκύβει το κεφάλι. Η τρομοκρατία της αξιολόγησης, των συγχωνεύσεων και των πειθαρχικών διώξεων θα σπάσει πάνω στο τείχος της αλληλεγγύης μας. Αυτή είναι η λύση, όπως αποδείχθηκε και από τις πρώτες απαλλακτικές αποφάσεις για τους διωκόμενους συναδέλφους μας που υπερασπίζονται όπως και όλος ο κλάδος μας το τι και με ποιον τρόπο μαθαίνουν τα παιδιά μας στο σχολείο, για την παιδαγωγική υπόσταση των εκπαιδευτικών, για το δικαίωμα στην απεργία και τη διεκδίκηση.


Μπορούμε να τα καταφέρουμε από κοινού οι εκπαιδευτικοί, με τη στήριξη και των γονιών των μαθητών μας.


Απαιτούμε εδώ και τώρα:


 Να σταματήσουν αμέσως όλες οι πειθαρχικές διώξεις των εκπαιδευτικών στο 3ο ΔΣ Ραφήνας


 Να πεταχτεί αμέσως στα σκουπίδια το απαράδεκτο ερώτημα για θέση σε «δυνητική αργία».


 Να σταματήσει η βιομηχανία διώξεων, ο αυταρχισμός και οι απειλές της διοίκησης ενάντια στους μαχόμενους εκπαιδευτικούς.


Απαντάμε μαζικά – Στον αυταρχισμό αντιτάσσουμε την αλληλεγγύη!


Καλούμε όλους τους εκπαιδευτικούς, τους γονείς που το προηγούμενο διάστημα αγωνιστήκαμε μαζί τους για τα μορφωτικά δικαιώματα των παιδιών και τα σωματεία της Αττικής να δώσουν δυναμικό “παρών” την Παρασκευή 4/9 στις 9:30 στην κινητοποίηση έξω από το Πειθαρχικό Συμβούλιο Ανθρώπινου Δυναμικού Δημοσίου Τομέα (ΠΣΑΔΔΤ)Νηρηίδων 10 (περιοχήHILTON,τέρμα Μιχαλακοπούλου).


Ο Σ.Ε.Π.Ε. “Αλ. Δελμούζος”, προκειμένου να διευκολυνθεί η μαζική συμμετοχή των μελών, του κηρύσσει 3ωρη διευκολυντική στάση εργασίας από 9.00-12.00.


Ακόμα καλεί το Δ.Σ της Δ.Ο.Ε. να δείξει ακόμα μια φορά τη συμπαράσταση και την αλλυλεγγύη του στα διωκόμενα μέλη μας, κηρύσσοντας 3ωρη διευκολυντική στάση εργασίας και να παρευρεθεί στην κινητοποίηση.


Η ΤΡΟΜΟΚΡΑΤΙΑ ΔΕΝ ΘΑ ΠΕΡΑΣΕΙ – ΟΙ ΔΙΩΞΕΙΣ ΘΑ ΜΕΙΝΟΥΝ ΣΤΑ ΧΑΡΤΙΑ!

author: Unknown
title: Symbol of ‘Jin, Jiyan, Azadî’: ‘Braids woven with oak leaves’
content:
On the fourth anniversary of the ‘Jin, Jiyan, Azadî’ uprising, 17 women’s and human rights organizations issued a joint statement.


The statement was signed by numerous organizations, including KJAR, the PJAK Women’s Council, Jîna Academy, the Balochistan Shivar Organization and the International Platform of Democratic Women.


The statement emphasized that the movement had broken deeply rooted social taboos, marked a turning point in the political and social spheres, and placed women’s rights and human dignity at the heart of societal demands.


It stated that, over the four years since the uprising began, social awareness has undergone a transformation and women’s solidarity has emerged as one of its most significant achievements.


The unity of women from different ethnic and national backgrounds gave the movement considerable strength, the statement said, stressing that lasting, just and democratic change would not be possible without recognizing women’s rights and combating discrimination.


The statement also unveiled a shared symbol for this new phase of the struggle: “braids woven with oak leaves.”


According to the statement, the loose braid symbolizes freedom and courage, the tight braid represents solidarity and organization, while the oak tree symbolizes resistance against oppression and putting down roots.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: Gloria Steinem, Feminist Icon & Ms. Magazine Co-Founder, Dies at 92
content:
Feminist icon Gloria Steinem has died at the age of 92. According to her Instagram page, she died Wednesday “at her home in New York City, surrounded by some of the many who loved her.” Steinem was a tireless advocate for the social, economic and political advancement of women. Steinem co-founded

Ms.

 magazine, the first major publication to be owned, run and written by women. She also helped found the National Women’s Political Caucus with a group of women including Shirley Chisholm, Betty Friedan and Fannie Lou Hamer. Before becoming a feminist icon, she served as director of the Independent Research Service, a nonprofit educational foundation secretly funded by the

CIA

. In 2013, she received the Presidential Medal of Freedom from President Barack Obama. She spoke with

Democracy Now!

 at the historic Women’s March in Washington, D.C., on January 21, 2017. We play an excerpt.

title: Khawla - A Trans Woman’s Letter to Trans Women
content:
Author

: Khawla

Title

: A Trans Woman’s Letter to Trans Women

Subtitle

: On struggle, resilience, love, and the trans women’s martial art.

Date

: 2026

Source

: Retrieved on 8-28-26 from https://pandemoniumdistro.noblogs.org/post/2026/05/28/a-trans-womans-letter-to-trans-women/


 Dear sister,


 I love you. I’m so sorry that the world is like this.


 I love you. I want you to be free to be yourself. To love and to live and to have and to hold.


 I love you. None of this is your fault. You deserve so much better.


 Juniper Blessing deserved so much better. Davonta Curtis deserved so much better. Eryka Caldwell deserved so much better.


 We deserve to live. We deserve to make our art. We deserve to dance, and sing, and create. We deserve to be soft and vulnerable. We deserve to feel loved, and safe, and treasured.


 Trans women are a treasure. We have always been a driving cultural force, whether the world was with us or against us. We have always brought so much light and color into the world.


 I love you. You and I are going to have to rip and tear to survive this. We are going to have to burn the world and tear down fortresses.


 Our enemies have made major strides in their plans to erase us. They surround us from every side.


 I know you see it too. I know you’re scared.


 I want to leave too. But I couldn’t do that to you. I couldn’t stomach to leave you here to fend for yourself.


 There are a lot of people who mean well towards us. A lot of people who really believe they would fight for us.


 But I have experienced enough to know we only have each-other. I have experienced enough to know that trans women throw the first brick and they hate us for it. I know that Black trans women pave the way when everyone else wants to give up and turn back.


 Where we’re going there’s no place for organizers and marshals. There’s no place for symbolic victories, good press, or witty signs.


 Where we’re going, we’re going to have to fight for our lives.


 So many of us are already fighting for our lives. V-coding in prisons, stalking, doxxing, harassment, assault, murder.


 Little egg middle schoolers are growing up in a world that makes it known it hates them. Trans children are killing themselves and the lawmakers know it and they celebrate it.


 You and I both know that they want us dead.


 I love you. You don’t deserve any of this. You did nothing wrong.


 I love you. It’s ok to be scared. But you have to get angry. You have to become powerful.


 I love you. When I go to the range, it’s for you. When I throw a stone, it’s for you. When I write, it’s for you.


 I love you. We are going to have to tear down fortresses to survive. We’re going to do it together.


 I’m not leaving you. I’ve got your back.


 We have got to get organized. We have got to get armed. We have got to have a strong defense. We have got to have a strong offense. We have got to get the knife off of our neck and onto theirs.


 Court decisions that rule favorably for our survival are not victories. They are luck at best. Victories are things we bring about by our own hand. Court decisions are something power bestows on us like a gift after reminding us of its intent to erase us.


 Our enemies are pushing at us from every angle. The courts occasionally get in the way by chance like a clumsy, bloated bureaucratic monster. The attacks on us do not stop. Our survival cannot depend on an institution that exists to serve our enemies and to serve a genocidal, carceral, settler-colonial empire.


 It has to depend on ourselves and each-other.


 You should own a gun and you should know how to use it and clean it. You should have trans women friends who do the same.


 If you cannot safely own a gun, support your trans women friends in being armed.


 Support them in training. Pack them lunch on range day.


 When you have a gun and know how to use it, it is a safeguard against the last hour. It is a safeguard for when the police come to your home to take you to a camp.


 When you have a gun and know how to use it, and your friends have guns and know how to use them, it becomes a capacity for strength and to project power. When you and your friends understand fire and maneuver, when you understand how to fight, it becomes a capacity for retaliation against power, a vehicle to secure victories like we haven’t seen before, the ability to put the enemy on the back foot, the ability to punish him for crimes he has committed against …

title: Revolutionärer Block an der Pride Aarau
content:
💥NO QUEER LIBERATION💥


🚩WITHOUT REVOLUTION! 🚩


Auch dieses Jahr wird es an der Pride Aarau einen revolutionären Block geben. Schliesst euch uns an!


🗓 5. September 2026


📍 Bahnhofsplatz Aarau


⏱️ 13:30 Uhr - Besammlung


🚩 14:15 Uhr - Demostart


Pride ist kein Geschenk, das uns gemacht wurde. Pride wurde erkämpft. Die Stonewall-Riots von 1969 waren kein friedliches Fest, sondern ein Aufstand gegen Polizeigewalt, staatliche Repression und die systematische Verfolgung queerer Menschen. Insbesondere trans Personen, queere People of Color und andere marginalisierte Menschen stellten sich gegen eine Polizei, die sie schikanierte und gewaltsam unterdrückte. Pride entstand aus Widerstand. Daran sollten wir uns erinnern, wenn heute versucht wird, Pride zu einem unpolitischen Fest zu machen.


Denn auch heute sind unsere Rechte nicht selbstverständlich. In der Schweiz können gleichgeschlechtliche Paare erst seit 2022 heiraten. Noch 2020 wurde über den Schutz vor homophober Diskriminierung und Hetze abgestimmt, gegen den sich rechte Parteien und Organisationen stellten. 2021 forderte die SVP-Grossrätin Sabina Geissbühler sogar ein Verbot von Schulbesuchen des Vereins ABQ, bei denen queere Menschen Jugendlichen von ihren Erfahrungen erzählen und über Homosexualität und Geschlechtsidentität sprechen. Als Begründung wurde unter anderem angeführt, Jugendliche könnten dadurch verunsichert werden.


Dass solche Positionen nicht einfach der Vergangenheit angehören, zeigt auch die erste Pride im Aargau. 2024 bezeichnete die SVP-Jungpolitikerin Vivienne Huber die Pride auf X als «Parasit», der expandiere. Es ist bezeichnend, dass ausgerechnet eine Veranstaltung, die aus dem Kampf gegen Ausgrenzung entstanden ist, von einer Politikerin mit einem Begriff bezeichnet wird, der Menschen und Bewegungen entmenschlicht. Gleichzeitig wird uns immer wieder erzählt, queere Menschen seien längst vollständig akzeptiert und unsere Kämpfe seien vorbei.


Doch die Realität sieht anders aus. Gerade während der Rechtsruck immer stärker wird, wird auch die Solidarität mit queeren Menschen wieder kleiner. Und das ist kein Zufall. Solange Queerness als bunte, konsumierbare Identität funktioniert, lässt sie sich problemlos vermarkten. Unternehmen hängen Regenbogenflaggen auf, verkaufen Pride-Kollektionen und präsentieren sich als Verbündete. Doch sobald queere Befreiung über ein Logo, ein Produkt oder einen Monat im Jahr hinausgeht, verschwindet diese Solidarität schnell wieder.


Rainbow Capitalism macht aus einer Bewegung eine Marke. Unsere Identitäten werden vermarktet, während die gesellschaftlichen Verhältnisse, die Menschen ausbeuten und voneinander abhängig machen, unangetastet bleiben. Wir wollen nicht einfach besser in eine Gesellschaft integriert werden, die weiterhin auf Ausbeutung, patriarchalen Strukturen und sozialer Ungleichheit beruht. Wir wollen eine Gesellschaft, in der Menschen tatsächlich frei leben können. Queere Befreiung kann deshalb nicht von der Befreiung aller Menschen getrennt werden. Solange Menschen aufgrund ihrer Herkunft, ihres Geschlechts, ihrer Sexualität oder ihrer sozialen Stellung ausgebeutet und unterdrückt werden, bleibt auch unsere eigene Befreiung unvollständig.


Das gilt auch international. Unsere Solidarität darf nicht an den Grenzen Europas enden. In Palästina und Rojava kämpfen Menschen gegen Besatzung, Vertreibung, staatliche Gewalt, patriarchale Strukturen und kapitalistische Ausbeutung. Auch dort kämpfen queere Menschen um Sichtbarkeit und Befreiung. Trotzdem werden Menschen aus dem Nahen Osten in westlichen Debatten häufig auf das Bild der rückständigen, homophoben Gesellschaft reduziert. Gerade queere Menschen werden dabei instrumentalisiert: Ihre Existenz wird benutzt, um ganze Gesellschaften zu entmenschlichen und Widerstand gegen Besatzung und Unterdrückung als grundsätzlich rückständig darzustellen.


Wir lehnen diese Logik ab. Queere Menschen brauchen keine westlichen Staaten, die sich zu ihren vermeintlichen Beschützern erklären, während sie gleichzeitig Krieg, Besatzung und Ausbeutung unterstützen. Islamfeindlichkeit und Rassismus sind keine Formen queerer Befreiung. Ebenso bedeutet Solidarität nicht, patriarchale oder queerfeindliche Strukturen zu verschweigen, nur weil sie in einer Bewegung existieren, mit der wir solidarisch sind. Unsere Solidarität bedeutet, Menschen als handelnde Subjekte ernst zu nehmen und gemeinsam gegen Unterdrückung zu kämpfen, anstatt verschiedene Gruppen …

author: Paige Collings
title: LGBT Q&A: What’s One Thing I Can Do Today to Improve My Safety and Security Online as an LGBTQ+ Person?
content:
This post is adapted from a video recorded by EFF and the Trevor Project. Head over to our 

TikTok

 or

Instagram

 to watch! 


EFF answers all the queer digital rights questions you submit to us through our

LGBT Q&A

. You asked us:

What’s one thing I can do today to improve my safety and security online as an LGBTQ+ person? 


And for this question, we’ve brought in our friends from the Trevor Project to answer together:


Hi, I’m Tommy from the

Trevor Project

! The Trevor Project’s mission is to end suicide among lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, and questioning (LGBTQ+) young people. Our vision is to create a world where all LGBTQ+ young people see a bright future for themselves.


EFF and the Trevor Project know that digital security and online safety can feel overwhelming, especially because we all have different levels of concern for different parts of our online lives. Some might be focused on the dangers of doxxing, another might only want to ensure they're not outed. And queer people can be particularly vulnerable to these kinds of online threats. 


This might seem like a big task, but the one way you can do today to protect yourself is to revise the information you’ve shared with services and platforms to ensure you’re as in control of your information and data as possible:


Protect Your Personal Information


Be cautious about sharing sensitive details like your full name, address, school, phone number, and personal photos as it might expose identifying information you want to keep private. Consider using an avatar as your profile picture to avoid sharing your personal photos if that makes you more comfortable. Keep it lowkey when talking about work stuff or sharing details about where you’re studying.


If you do share personal photos, don’t accompany them with information that identifies your location or frequent whereabouts, and make sure

EXIF data in photos is turned off

 (which could inadvertently include your location); the easiest way to do this is to take a screenshot of the photo and share that instead. Don’t post pictures with obvious spots in the background, like your front door or porch. 


Understand the Importance of Login Information


When you create an account on websites and platforms, you can often use your phone number or a third party account, such as Facebook, Google, or Apple. These external accounts might share data with the apps you're logging into, but they can be helpful if you struggle with managing a lot of logins. Deciding if that trade-off is worth it is up to you but, when you can, use strong, unique passwords for your accounts, and be sure to enable two-factor authentication when offered.

 


Review Permissions with Social Media Apps


Review which apps have access to things like your location and camera roll, and possibly change those permissions in line with what information you would like to keep private. Location is particularly important

.

 For example, some apps might need some location information to function. But you can typically at least deny access to your device's "precise location" or enter in a city or zip code manually.


Consider What You Share When Speaking with Others Online


It’s important to be mindful of what you share with others when you post online or speak with people. Avoid disclosing sensitive information like financial details, and trust your gut if something feels off. It’s also useful to review your profile’s privacy settings and information now and again to make sure you’re still comfortable sharing what you’ve listed there.


Good privacy decisions begin with proper 

knowledge

 about your situation and a 

community-oriented approach

. To dig in deeper, read EFF’s blog post on 

Building a Community Privacy Plan

 and the Trevor Project’s

Guide to Online Safety for LGBTQ+ Young People

.

author: TGEU
title: Joint statement: Bulgaria’s Supreme Court opens the door to legal gender recognition, ending years of judicial deadlock
content:
At the end of July, the Supreme Court decided in favour of four trans applicants seeking legal recognition of their gender identity. The ruling aligns Bulgarian practice with the Court of Justice of the EU, enabling changes to gender markers, names, and personal identification numbers. The judges also concluded that EU law requires Bulgaria to establish a legal procedure for legal gender recognition, which is necessary so that Bulgarian trans citizens can travel and reside freely inside the EU.


TGEU – Trans Europe and Central Asia,

Bilitis

,

Deystvie

 and

ILGA-Europe

 welcome the Bulgarian Supreme Court’s decisions as overdue and a great relief to trans people in Bulgaria. 


Delays in justice


The decisions had been eagerly anticipated. Yet, some EU countries are notoriously slow to implement judgments from the European courts, and Bulgaria’s particularly poor track record had created fears that legal gender recognition would remain out of reach for trans Bulgarians. Failure to implement doesn’t just fail Bulgarian trans people; it erodes the European human rights system for everyone.


K.M.H., the applicant behind the decisive

Shipova

 case at the EU Court, was among the four now granted recognition. She first requested a female gender marker nearly a decade ago. Living in Italy, her old Bulgarian documents have repeatedly outed her and made it harder to find work.


What the Court said


The ruling follows directly from

Shipova

, in which the EU Supreme Court found in March 2026 that Member States must make legal gender recognition possible, so that EU citizens can exercise freedom of movement without restriction.


The Bulgarian judges found that everyone has the right to determine their own gender identity, and that this “cannot be questioned.” Citing the EU’s Charter of Fundamental Rights and the European Convention on Human Rights, they confirmed that the right to a private life includes the right to define one’s own gender identity.


Asked whether Bulgaria’s ban was constitutional, the judges were direct: “The rule of law in Bulgaria implies a universal equality of the dignity of all human beings, including transgender people.” Denying recognition, they found, would fail to respect the dignity every trans person is entitled to and which courts have a duty to protect.


Key points from the ruling:


Nothing in the Bulgarian Constitution actually prohibits legal gender recognition. Previous courts had simply read ‘sex’ too narrowly.


EU law applies directly in Bulgaria, and national law must be interpreted in line with it.


Trans and intersex people have an equal right to legal gender recognition.


Blanket bans are unlawful. Each case must be judged on its own merits. A narrow reading of ‘sex’, moral judgment, or the simple absence of a legal procedure cannot justify unequal treatment.


No proof of medical or surgical intervention can be required. The Court found this incompatible with the European Convention on Human Rights. However, the Court also confirmed the requirement of hormone treatment, which is concerning, as the European Court of Human Rights has found that requiring sterility, or treatment likely to lead to sterility, is incompatible with human rights. 


Courts must recognise a person’s gender identity once presented with a mental health diagnosis (F.46.0) and a clear, sustained wish to live according to that identity. This is significant in itself: without a proper legal procedure, the Court is effectively establishing a legal pathway for how lower Bulgarian courts should handle gender recognition requests going forward.


Bulgaria has long been obligated to introduce a legal procedure allowing people to formally update their gender marker, first name, and (per Bulgarian naming convention) father’s name. What’s new is that this obligation has now been formulated as a direct demand to the Bulgarian legislator by the country’s own Court of Cassation, which is a striking reversal from previous rulings by this same court and the Constitutional Court.


Reactions


Civil society welcomed the ruling while pressing for fast follow-through:


“It is a deep relief and a source of satisfaction to see that the system delivers. Trans people are equal in dignity and rights. They can rely on the CJEU and the courts to claim their rights. The Bulgarian government must now swiftly start the legislative process with meaningful civil society involvement. A quick, transparent and accessible …

author: Emma Anderson
title: Support Is Growing in the Push to Recognize Gender Apartheid as a Crime Against Humanity
content:
The movement for the rights and freedom of Afghan women and girls is picking up momentum in the halls of the United Nations. Feminist Majority Foundation (FMF) and other feminist civil society leaders and activists are currently engaged in the historic process of negotiations for a crimes against humanity treaty, which will provide a formal mechanism for recognizing, codifying, and holding perpetrators accountable for a suite of atrocities that have fallen through the gaps of existing international laws for decades. Crucially, the negotiations for this treaty provide a window for feminists to ensure that all forms of gender-based persecution are defined, recognized, and punished for what they are: global atrocities and systematic violence permeating all levels of society.

On July 28, the UN released an updated version of the draft articles, which includes amendments and additions that ensure gender apartheid is recognized throughout the text. On June 4, Australia, Afghanistan (UN mission), Iceland, Mexico, Timor-Leste, Uruguay, and Spain agreed to include gender apartheid in their amendments; the draft released in July reflects these commitments in writing. These 7 states join Austria, Portugal, Malta, Philippines, Chile, Brazil and Luxembourg as champions in the global fight for the rights and dignity of Afghan women and girls living under the oppressive Taliban regime.

There were also multiple additions and amendments to include forced marriage as its own category, put forward by several states: Canada, the Netherlands, Sierra Leone, Germany, Belgium, Colombia, the UK, Andorra, Cyprus, Ukraine, and Poland, in addition to states also proposing to include gender apartheid. This same group of states, in addition to the Nordic states, also proposed to expand the definition of sexual violence to cover specific types of reproductive violence, like forced sterilization and forced birth.

The show of support by some states for forced marriage and reproductive violence, while stopping short of “gender apartheid,” presents an opportunity for feminist organizations to keep advocating for the full breadth of gender-based oppression to be appropriately recognized by the UN. At FMF, we call on these states to embrace this fight to the fullest extent. The totality of Afghan women and girls’ oppression needs to be unequivocally condemned by the international community in all its forms.

FMF will continue to push for full recognition of gender apartheid as the UN continues the long process of creating a new legal instrument for identifying and punishing crimes against humanity. FMF’s advocacy on this issue draws from the real voices and leadership of women and girls in Afghanistan, and we echo their calls for a refusal to recognize or normalize the Taliban.

Countries that have demonstrated solidarity and leadership in this urgent fight for humanity and freedom are setting an important example. This is a critical moment to engage more partners and representatives at the UN and beyond, build on this momentum, and advance a Crimes Against Humanity Convention that recognizes gender apartheid and accurately reflects the voices, experiences, and lives of women and girls in Afghanistan.

title: [Roanne] Faisons taire le canon français ! Pas de canon français, ni à Riorges, ni ailleurs !
content:
Un banquet régional du Canon français est programmé le samedi 5 septembre, de 12 heures à 17 heures, au Scarabée de Riorges, dans le nord du département de la Loire (Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes).


Ces banquets constituent des manifestations d'extrême droite, qui utilisent la gastronomie, le patrimoine et la prétendue «

 

identité française

 

» pour banaliser les idées nationalistes et racistes, recruter des sympathisant-es et tisser des liens entre militant-es, élu-es, personnalités et réseaux de la droite radicale et de l'extrême droite.


Le Canon français est financé pur le milliardaire Pierre-Édouard Stérin, qui met sa fortune au service de la progression de l'extrême droite.


À travers son projet Périclès, doté de 150 millions d'euros, il entend favoriser la conquête culturelle, médiatique et électorale de la droite radicale et de l'extrême droite, former des centaines de candidat-es et contribuer à leur accession au pouvoir.


Plusieurs enquêtes journalistiques, témoignages et vidéos confirment que les banquets du Canon français sont des lieux de sociabilité, de recrutement et de mise en réseau de l'extrême droite

 [

1

]

. On y retrouve des militant-es identitaires, des cadres ou sympathisant-es de Reconquête

 

!, du Rassemblement national et d'autres organisations nationalistes, dans un climat où le racisme est banalisé.


Le 18 avril 2026, lors du banquet organisé à Caen, des saluts nazis ont été effectués au cours de la Marseillaise et de nombreux propos racistes ont été tenus. Les vidéos et les enregistrements rendus publics ont montré des appels à la violence contre les personnes musulmanes, racisées ou d'origine étrangère, illustrant la véritable nature de ces rassemblements.

 [

2

]


Nous refusons que ce genre de rassemblement puisse se tenir en toute tranquillité. Nous lançons une campagne pour obtenir l'annulation de cet événement.


Dans plusieurs villes, des banquets du Canon français ont déjà été annulés ou contraints de changer de lieu à la suite de la mobilisation d'associations, de syndicats, d'élu-es et de citoyen-nes.


À cette fin, nous appelons à interpeller l'ensemble des institutions qui rendent possible la tenue de cet événement : les pouvoirs publics, qui permettent sa tenue

 

; les entreprises prestataires, celles qui fournissent l'évènement et les partenaires qui y contribuent

 

; ainsi que les élu-es locaux, afin qu'ils prennent publiquement position.


Nous appelons l'ensemble des organisations syndicales, associatives, politiques, ainsi que tous-tes les habitant-es attaché-es aux valeurs d'égalité, de solidarité et d'antifascisme à amplifier cette campagne.


Si, malgré cette mobilisation, le banquet n'était pas annulé,

nous appelons d'ores et déjà à préparer un grand rassemblement antifasciste

, contre le racisme, l'extrême droite et ses idées, le

samedi 5 septembre à 11 heures à Riorges

.


Faisons taire le Canon français

 

!

title: K. C. Sinclair - Little Tel Aviv
content:
Author

: K. C. Sinclair

Title

: Little Tel Aviv

Subtitle

: How Portland Got Progressive Through Ethnic Cleansing

Date

: July 12, 2026

Source

: Retrieved on August 28, 2026, from an offline backup of censored site https://historyiswhat.noblogs.org/2026/07/12/little-tel-aviv-how-portland-got-progressive-through-ethnic-cleansing-k-c-sinclair-2026/


 Portland, Oregon, has long been America’s whitest major city, yet its progressive activists, since the early 1990s, have embraced its branding as “Little Beirut” by the George H. W. Bush administration due to its boisterous protests. In reality, it’s no coincidence that Portland is so white, and a brief (non-comprehensive) overview of its history of ethnic cleansing reveals the city as more akin to Tel Aviv than Beirut.


 Unlike its less white fellow Pacific Northwest cities, Seattle, Washington, and Vancouver, British Columbia, where the original Native communities persist in some form within the newer settler metropolitan boundaries, Portland’s colonizers long ago ethnically cleansed the area of its Indigenous peoples.


 As detailed by David G. Lewis of the Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde, in 1851, the Indigenous peoples of the Portland area (the Multnomah, Clackamas, Tualatin, etc.) and the rest of the Willamette Valley initially refused to move, negotiating treaties that would have established reservations within their homelands, but those treaties were never ratified when taken back to the federal government in the District of Columbia. In 1855, the Willamette Valley peoples signed a treaty which resulted, by the following year, in their tribes being removed to the Grand Ronde Indian Reservation, some 50 miles (now more than 60 miles) southwest from Portland.


 Armed settlers claimed the entire Willamette Valley and would brook no compromise. In 1847 they had formed a militia in response to the killing of missionaries by Cayuse persons at Waiilatpu, more than 200 miles up the Columbia River from Portland. In Oregon City, now a suburb of Portland, five Cayuse individuals who’d offered themselves up in the name of peace were quickly tried and publicly hanged by the settler government in 1850.


 The Oregon Donation Land Act of 1850 has been described by the state’s online encyclopedia as “arguably the most generous federal land act in American history,” since it allowed for claims as large as 640 acres (320 for a white male citizen and an equal portion for his wife) for couples already living in Oregon, and 320 acres for newly arriving settlers and individual “half-breed” Natives willing to become citizens, so long as the land was resided upon and “improved” for four years. The law expired in 1855 and was replaced in 1862 with the less generous Homestead Act, allowing settlers to claim as much as 160 acres at $1.25 per acre, with the option of expanding to contiguous adjacent land up to the same acreage.


 The Grand Ronde reservation, originally some 60,000 acres in size, was allotted in the 1890s, allowing for allotments to eventually fall into settler hands. In 1901, US official James McLaughlin declared 25,791 acres of the reservation to be surplus and the government eventually sold it off for $1.16 per acre.


 Considering this level of intensity to Oregon’s settler colonial expansion, the state has something more in common with its overtly genocidal southern neighbor of California than it does with its northern neighbors of Washington and British Columbia, though the latter were certainly not innocent of genocidal displacement and repression either.


 Portland’s historic and ongoing racism, furthermore, has never been limited to anti-Native sentiment. As Black scholar Walidah Imarisha explains, a series of exclusionary anti-Black laws were enacted in Oregon between 1844 and 1859, with the intention of building a “racist white utopia.”


 The lives of several historic Black individuals illustrate the effect of these racist laws and of the white supremacist mindset they reflected. George Bush, a Black man who had been born in Pennsylvania and had been a farmer in Missouri, tried to move with his family to Oregon in 1844, but given its first exclusion law, he decided instead to move north across the Columbia River to present-day Tumwater, Washington, which was territory still shared with the British Hudson’s Bay Company at the time.
