author: Monic Moll
title: Tiere in extremer Hitze: Statistik zeigt Tierleid auf Weiden
content:
In den Monaten Juni bis August erhalten wir von PETA Deutschland jedes Jahr viele Meldungen zu Tieren, die nicht ausreichend vor der

Hitze geschützt

 werden. Durch die langanhaltenden und ungewöhnlich hohen Temperaturen war die Anzahl der Meldungen in diesem Jahr auffällig hoch. Besonders häufig wurde uns von sogenannten Weidetieren berichtet, denen es an ausreichendem Schutz vor Hitze oder an genügend Trinkwasser fehlte. Diese Vorfälle haben wir an die zuständigen Veterinärbehörden weitergeleitet und die eingegangenen Meldungen anschließend ausgewertet.


Wie viele „Weidetiere“ betroffen waren und welche Missstände besonders häufig gemeldet wurden, erfahren Sie hier.


Insgesamt über 60 Meldungen zu „Weidetieren“ während der Hitzeperioden


So viele Meldungen vernachlässigter Tiere auf Weideflächen erreichten uns bei PETA Deutschland von Juni bis Juli 2026.


In diesem Jahr erreichten uns insgesamt 62 Meldungen zu „Weidetieren“, die unter den hohen Temperaturen litten. Darunter:


32 Meldungen zu

Schafen

/Ziegen


18 Meldungen zu Rindern


8 Meldungen zu Pferden


2 Meldungen zu Schweinen


2 Meldungen zu gefiederten Tieren


Besonders häufig fehlten den Tieren

ein baulicher Unterstand oder schattenspendende Bäume

. Zudem wurden uns Fälle gemeldet, in denen Tiere

ohne Wasser

 auskommen mussten oder ihnen nur

verschmutztes und stark erwärmtes Wasser

 zur Verfügung stand. Darüber hinaus

starben Tiere

 aufgrund der hohen Temperaturen

in Ställen

 oder

auf Transportern.


Die sich stauende Hitze sorgt dafür, dass viele Tiere noch während des Transports ins Schlachthaus sterben.


PETA meldet Vorfälle an zuständige Behörden


Wir meldeten Hinweise auf Tiere in lebensgefährlichen Situationen umgehend an die zuständigen Veterinärbehörden. Diese gingen sehr unterschiedlich mit den offensichtlichen Missständen um: Nicht von allen Veterinärbehörden erhielten wir Rückmeldungen zu den gemeldeten Fällen – immer wieder nicht einmal eine Antwort, die bestätigt, dass die Meldung bearbeitet wird.


In einigen Fällen führte auch eine wiederholte Meldung an die zuständige Behörde zu keiner sichtbaren Veränderung oder Verbesserung der Haltung. Selten wurden sofort Maßnahmen getroffen und Weidezelte aufgestellt – und selbst damit reicht der erzeugte Schatten nicht immer für alle Tiere auf der Weide aus.


Unsere Beobachtungen in diesem Bereich zeigen leider deutlich, dass auf Deutschlands Weiden größtenteils von Behördenversagen auszugehen ist. Es kann und darf nicht sein, dass das Wohlergehen der Tiere von der Sorgfältigkeit der Behörden abhängig ist.


Daher fordern wir die zuständigen Behörden dazu auf, das geltende Tierschutzrecht konsequent durchzusetzen und gemeldeten Missständen konsequent und zeitnah nachzugehen.


Bei diesen vernachlässigten Schafen auf einer Weide in Bresegard wurde offensichtlich keine Schur durchgeführt. Zudem befanden sich die verwesenden Überreste zahlreicher Tiere auf dem Grundstück.


Darum leiden Tiere bei Hitze auf der Weide


Fehlt es an ausreichendem Schutz oder einer angemessenen Versorgung und Pflege, können die hohen Temperaturen für Tiere auf der Weide zur

Belastung

 werden. Sie leiden insbesondere unter folgenden Missständen:


Keine ausreichende Wasserversorgung


„Weidetieren“ muss täglich ausreichend sauberes Wasser zur Verfügung stehen. Bei Hitze steigt der Bedarf deutlich: Schafe benötigen unter normalen Bedingungen etwa zwei bis vier Liter Wasser am Tag, bei großer Hitze und während der Aufzucht ihrer Jungtiere jedoch bis zu

zehn Liter.


[1] Bei

Kühen in der Milchindustrie

 kann der Wasserbedarf bei Hitze auf bis zu

200 Liter

 pro Tag steigen. [2]


Die Wasserbehälter müssen zudem an die Größe und Bedürfnisse der Tiere angepasst sein. [3] Leider stellen wir oft fest, dass das nicht der Fall ist. Besonders Jungtiere können aus zu tiefen

Behältern nicht trinken

. Wir empfehlen daher mehrere geeignete Trinkmöglichkeiten, die den unterschiedlichen Bedürfnissen der Herde gerecht werden. Tierhalter:innen sind zudem verpflichtet, die Herde mindestens einmal täglich zu kontrollieren. Dennoch erleben wir immer wieder, dass „Weidetiere“ tagelang

sich selbst überlassen

 werden und dann – mit viel Glück – von besorgten Passant:innen versorgt werden. Auch hier erhielten wir immer wieder die Rückmeldung, dass Augenzeug:innen die Umstände zwar bei der Polizei meldeten, jedoch nicht ernst genommen wurden.

content:
This morning (01/09/26) Animal rights campaigner Michelle Farnham entered a pig farrowing crate outside the National Gallery in Trafalgar Square where she will remain for 21 days, as Animal Rising launches its campaign to end factory farming in Britain by 2040.

The action coincides with the release today of never-before-seen footage following a month in the life of Luna, a sow confined in a farrowing crate on a British factory farm. Animal Rising are calling for the release of Luna from Red Court Farm in Ipswich. [1]

author: hsa_oryx
title: LE SHUTTLE – TRANSPORTING CRUELTY
content:
The Hunt Saboteurs Association (HSA) has just launched a campaign to ask Le Shuttle to stop facilitating the transportation of game birds from Europe to the UK.


Le Shuttle is a significant route for bringing

live pheasants and red-legged partridges

 into Britain from European hatcheries. Around 10 million birds are imported annually, representing roughly a quarter of the birds bred for shooting.


Cacabrava rearing site based in Portugal which we previously reported as suppling the UK shooting industry


These birds will ultimately be destined for one of the shoots and game farms across the country. The vast majority of birds shot for sport in Britain are pheasants. Originally native to Asia, pheasants have been introduced to numerous countries, and are now bred on an industrial scale to supply the shooting industry.


Since 2016 estimates show that around 47 million pheasants are released in the UK annually ahead of the shooting season, alongside a further 10 million red-legged partridge. Added to birds remaining from previous releases which are estimated in the region of 3-5 million, the total population is estimated at about 50 million pheasants in the wild at the time of release.


Those numbers will decline through the seasons. Birds will die from predation, disease, environmental factors, collisions with vehicles and ultimately, shooting. Approximately a quarter of released birds will die before the shooting season even begins on the 1

st

 October.


The ecological and environmental consequences of releasing millions of non-native, intensively reared birds are considerable. Large concentrations alter the availability of food for other species, and affect local wildlife, such as reptile species which may themselves become prey for the birds.


The other way in which local wildlife is affected is through predator control. Predator numbers respond to the sudden abundance of food sources created by the annual releases. It is estimated that foxes account for a significant proportion of the birds that fail to survive until the start of the season. Predators that have benefited from the abundance of prey remain long after the birds have gone, they must then find alternative sources of food.


A larsen trap is a familiar sight on game shoots


Foxes and other perceived predators are subsequently targeted by gamekeepers, farmers, and hunts. Animals including foxes, birds of prey and corvids may be poisoned, trapped, snared, shot, while foxes are also pursued by hunts, all to deal with a ‘problem’ of their own making.


A fox about to be rescued from a snare on a Wiltshire shoot estate


The consequences of widespread use of anti-coagulant poisons go far beyond the species being targeted,

lead to secondary poisoning

 in scavenger species who include carrion in their diets such as red kites, buzzards, corvids, even invertebrate scavengers such as beetles, blowflies and ants.


A red kite was found dead in June 2025 with lethal amounts of a banned rodenticide


There is an obvious contradiction here. As the artificially inflated numbers of available prey decline through the shooting season, the predatory species that benefitted from the abundance remain, and are further regarded as problems that need to be controlled, creating a completely artificial landscape where wildlife does not stand a chance.


Anti-coagulant poison found on a shooting estate


Game shoots are not about food, this is not subsistence hunting – it is entertainment.


Historically shooting is closely associated with aristocratic and royal privilege. The transformation of the British countryside during the 18

th

 and 19

th

 centuries, including the enclosure and consolidation of common land, saw land ownership become more concentrated and helped to create the shooting-estate culture we see today.


Shooting is extremely expensive. Driven shoot days can cost hundreds or more likely – thousands of pounds depending upon the shoot and the number of birds involved, yet the end product has very little value.  Some are sold to game dealers for about 30 pence per bird, with the vast majority ending up in stink pits, or end up on bonfires, because the fact is that there is little appetite to eat the lead riddled birds.


A significant number of game birds will die before the shooting season starts


The reality is that this is an archaic and cruel pastime enjoyed by a minority, whose enjoyment is prioritised over the welfare of animals and the …

title: Cruauté et infractions à l’abattoir de Perpignan
content:
Entre mai et juillet 2026, des caméras ont filmé ce qui se passe à l'abattoir de Perpignan. Des cochons frappés à coups de poing. Un opérateur qui enfonce son avant-bras dans l'incision de saignée d'un cochon encore conscient. Des moutons balancés par la toison et par les pattes. Des vaches et des moutons découpés alors qu'ils sont encore en vie.

Rien de tout cela n'est accidentel : le couloir des cochons est en angle droit, le box de contention des bovins n'immobilise pas assez les animaux pour un étourdissement précis. Et tout se passe sous les yeux des services vétérinaires de l'État, présents chaque jour d'abattage.

L214 porte plainte pour actes de cruauté et demande la fermeture immédiate de l'abattoir.

Aujourd'hui, vous pouvez agir en une minute en signant la pétition. Merci 🙏

author: A.N.A.
title: [Itália] Antiespecismo, veganismo e crise climática
content:
O verão que estamos vivendo está nos mostrando de forma tremendamente tangível o quanto nossas atividades destrutivas estão impactando o clima terrestre. Não há parte do mundo que não esteja sofrendo com desconfortos, ou mesmo verdadeiros desastres, climáticos. Em nosso país, ondas de calor tropical se sucedem, causando cada vez mais incêndios (quando não são criminosos), eventos climáticos extremos e fazendo diminuir assustadoramente o nível da água dos rios e lagos.


Nossa casa comum, a Terra, está doente e o vírus que a infectou somos nós.

 Um conceito mais que banal e totalmente evidente. Apesar de tudo isso, no âmbito antiespecista e vegano, este assunto tão dramaticamente urgente quase nunca é abordado. No entanto, toda vez que uma floresta pega fogo, morrem milhões de Animais, assim como também ocorre com deslizamentos, enxurradas, alagamentos, transbordamentos, longos períodos de seca e tempestades. As zonas climáticas estão mudando rapidamente e isso também significa o desaparecimento de muitas espécies animais que não conseguirão mais se adaptar ao novo clima. Como é que não paramos para refletir sobre tudo isso?


A 

Questão Animal

 diz respeito a todas as áreas da ação humana, a todas as suas implicações e consequências, portanto, também e principalmente, aos desastres climáticos que estamos causando com a poluição, o enorme desperdício de energia, as atividades extrativistas, a poluição, a exploração dos ecossistemas e a antropização e destruição dos habitats naturais. Não considerar tudo isso sob uma ótica antiespecista e vegana, para tentar combater este fenômeno gravíssimo e complexo que produzimos diretamente, é simplesmente uma loucura.


Se a nossa função, enquanto pessoas humanas antiespecistas, é retirar os Animais da exploração humana e, por fim, chegar à tão almejada libertação, não podemos nos eximir de compreender o quanto a crise climática está impactando de forma devastadora a vida dos seres vivos terrestres.


Cada vez mais, a mídia nos mostra imagens de rios secos; toda vez que um rio desaparece, deixando apenas um leito vazio e seco, desaparecem também milhões de Animais, plantas, muitos outros organismos vivos que o habitavam e outros que dependiam de sua presença: quando um rio morre, com ele morre um mundo inteiro, é um grande e vital amigo que se foi. Não podemos ser tão estúpidos e insensíveis a ponto de não compreender isso.


Temos o dever e a urgência de incluir no leque de reflexões e intervenções do nosso ativismo conceitos básicos de ecologia: certamente não aquela especista, antropocêntrica e superficial que nos é empurrada diariamente, mas a 

ecologia profunda

 não antropocêntrica, útil para nos ajudar finalmente a entender o quão frágil e ameaçada está a rede da vida na Terra.


Adriano Fragano


Fonte: 

https://www.manifestoantispecista.org/web/antispecismo-veganismo-e-crisi-climatica/

title: 1,500 mink escape from Oregon farm after fence is cut open reportedly by extremist animal rights group
content:
Roughly 1,500 mink escaped an Oregon farm after a hole was cut in a fence — with an extremist animal rights group linking themselves to the plot to free the creatures, according to authorities and reports.

The scores of mink were intentionally let loose from Cascade Farm in Turner late last Wednesday night as the farm’s manager, his wife, children, and other employees were sleeping, KOIN reported.

The suspected intruders cut a hole in a chain-link fence enclosure, allowing the mink to roam free, the local outlet said.

The Animal Liberation Front — a decentralized group of international animal rights advocates labeled as extremists by the FBI — appears to have taken responsibility for the break-in, the outlet reported.

In a press release, the radical group said they have yet to receive an “anonymous communique” officially taking credit for the action.

But Jerry Vlasak, a spokesperson for the North American Animal Liberation Front, told the outlet that the mink escape plot was consistent with their group’s actions and that communiques from activists claiming responsibility are not always sent.

The farm owners have since recovered about 90% of the cute, semiaquatic mammals, the Marion County Sheriff’s Office told the outlet.

“This wasn’t activism. It was a criminal act against a legally operated, certified farm,” Challis Hobbs, Executive Director of Fur Commission USA, an organization that represents mink farmers including Cascade Farm, told the outlet.

“The farm manager and his wife and children live on this property, along with other employees and their families,” he said. “It’s deeply unsettling to have people cut through a fence in the middle of the night with children sleeping just steps away.”

Cascade Farm raises mink legally for pelts and is Humane Care Certified. Any of the mink that aren’t recovered within 24 to 48 hours also face risk of starvation and death, Fur Commission USA added.

The animal activists, however, claimed the mink would be subjected to “egregiously cruel and violent” treatment in captivity.

“The animals liberated last night have a fighting chance at life; they faced a 100 percent death rate if they stayed on the farm,” the Animal Liberation Front wrote in a statement.

The group previously claimed responsibility for cutting open a fence at Olsen Fur Farm in Wisconsin in 2023, allowing about 3,000 mink to escape, CBS reported.

title: Drohnenangriff in der Ukraine: Helfer von PETA-Partnerorganisation bei Tierrettung verletzt
content:
Symbolbild.


Bei einem

Rettungseinsatz in der Ukraine

 ist am Nachmittag des 31. August 2026 ein Fahrzeug der PETA-Partnerorganisation

Animal Rescue Kharkiv (ARK)

 von einer Drohne angegriffen worden. Dabei wurden zwei Tierschützer verletzt. Zum Zeitpunkt des Angriffs befanden sich außerdem

gerettete Tiere

 im Fahrzeug.


Das Team war in einem vom Krieg betroffenen Gebiet unterwegs, um Tiere in Sicherheit zu bringen.


Drohnenangriff auf Tierrettungsteam: Zwei Helfer wurden verletzt


Bei dem Angriff wurden ein Helfer von

Animal Rescue Kharkiv

 (ARK) sowie ein Tierschützer der französischen Organisation

Crisis France

 verletzt. Letzterer erlitt zahlreiche Verletzungen durch Splitter und musste operiert werden.


Auch der ARK-Helfer wurde durch den Angriff verletzt. Zunächst bestand unter anderem Sorge wegen einer Verletzung am Auge. Nach jüngsten Informationen von

Animal Rescue Kharkiv

 sind seine Augen glücklicherweise in Ordnung, die Wunde am Arm wurde genäht.


Der Helfer von

Crisis France

 hat die Operation überstanden.

Nach aktuellem Kenntnisstand besteht bei beiden Tierrettern keine Lebensgefahr.

 Nun stehen ihre weitere medizinische Versorgung und Genesung im Vordergrund.


Das Team von

Animal Rescue Kharkiv

 organisierte nach dem Angriff gemeinsam mit weiteren Helfer:innen die Versorgung und den Transport der Verletzten.


Gerettete Tiere nach Drohnenangriff in Sicherheit gebracht


Die geretteten Tiere befanden sich während des Angriffs noch im Fahrzeug. Ein weiterer Helfer machte sich anschließend auf den Weg, um sie zu übernehmen. Mittlerweile wurden die traumatisierten Tiere an einen sicheren Ort gebracht.


Der Vorfall zeigt erneut, welchen

lebensgefährlichen Bedingungen

 die Tierschützer:innen in der Ukraine bei ihren Einsätzen ausgesetzt sind. Trotz der anhaltenden Gefahren begeben sich die Teams weiterhin in betroffene Gebiete, evakuieren zurückgelassene Tiere und bringen sie an sichere Orte.


Das ARK-Team rettet Tiere in den Kriegsgebieten der Ukraine, oft unter großer Gefahr. Symbolbild.


PETA und Animal Rescue Kharkiv retten weiterhin Tiere in der Ukraine


Seit Beginn des Krieges arbeiten wir von PETA Deutschland mit

Animal Rescue Kharkiv

 und weiteren Partnern zusammen, um möglichst viele Tiere zu retten. Die Helfenden versorgen Tiere mit

Nahrung und medizinischer Hilfe

, evakuieren sie aus gefährlichen Gebieten und

bringen sie in Sicherheit

.


Der aktuelle Angriff macht auf erschütternde Weise deutlich, dass die Rettungseinsätze nicht nur für die Tiere, sondern auch für die Menschen, die ihnen helfen, mit erheblichen Gefahren verbunden sind.


Unterstützen Sie unseren Einsatz in der Ukraine: Helfen Sie jetzt mit Ihrer Spende und retten Sie Tierleben


Die Lage in den ukrainischen Kriegsgebieten bleibt angespannt und lebensgefährlich – für alle Lebewesen. Wir werden gemeinsam mit unseren Partnern vor Ort weiterhin alles in unserer Macht Stehende tun, um den Tieren in der Ukraine zu helfen und ihnen eine bessere Zukunft zu ermöglichen. Sie können uns dabei mit Ihrer Spende an den Global Compassion Fund zielgerichtet unterstützen.


Jetzt PETAs Ukraine-Einsatz unterstützen

title: Shut Down The Stowe School Beagles!
content:
Today the Hunt Saboteurs Association can exclusively reveal the full footage that led to the recent conviction of Stowe School Beagles Kennel Huntsman Philip Kennedy for killing a hare in November 2025.


This is the first step in our campaign to shut down this hunt.


The footage shows both the extent of the cruelty of the Stowe School Beagles and the catastrophic failure of safeguarding at the £47,000 per year school.


Unbelievably, Kennedy is employed as a ‘Games Coach’ at Stowe and the hare hunting shown in the video is essentially a PE lesson, just like the rugby and hockey that is also offered at the school.


The Stowe School Beagles pursue the hare across a car park.


As the video opens, unsupervised Stowe pupils are looking for hares in the open Northamptonshire countryside. On their return to Crockwell Farm, the hounds are put into a strip of woodland by the farm’s car park. The hunters are there for some time – they obviously know a hare is present – before the hounds flush the terrified animal out across the car park.


Huntsman pats hounds as they rip into the hare.


The pursuit continues through a larger wood, with Kennedy positioning himself on its far side in case the hare breaks cover. The video next picks up the last moments of the doomed animal: she sprints across open ground – closely pursued by the whole pack – before crashing into a fence. She is obviously gravely injured but limps on before being overwhelmed by the pack.


Handshakes all round as the hare is ragged by the hounds.


The hunters arrive on the scene, patting the hounds and exchanging congratulatory handshakes as the hare is ripped to pieces. Back at the hound van and Stowe School minibus, the celebrations continue.


With the hare hunting season about to begin we cannot allow this cruelty to continue: the HSA will shortly be asking you – our valued supporters – to take action.

Please keep an eye on our socials over the next few days.

Shut Down The Stowe School Beagles!

 appeared first on

Hunt Saboteurs Association

title: ‘They’re still there’: Activists warn of more mink raids after break-in at Oregon farm
content:
PORTLAND, Ore. (KOIN) — After a late-night break-in last week led to the escape of 1,500 mink from an Oregon farm, some animal rights activists say more intrusions could be on the way.

The Animal Liberation Front, a decentralized group of extremist animal rights advocates known for sabotage, vandalism and even arson, has claimed responsibility in a press release shared on its website for the Aug. 13 break-in at Cascade Farms of Oregon mink farm in Turner, Oregon.

That claim has been unconfirmed by officials. The Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Portland office declined to comment on whether it is investigating the break-in.

The Marion County Sheriff’s Office said there have been no arrests related to the case, and they have no information indicating the ALF’s involvement.

The owner of Cascade Farms of Oregon, Randy Lucas, did not respond to multiple phone calls seeking comment about the break-in. Cascade Farms was established by Lucas’ father, John Lucas, as a meat business and ranch in 1980. The meat business has since closed, and John Lucas passed away, but the ranch remains in business.

But Joseph Buddenberg, a former member of the Animal Liberation Front, said the break-in at Cascade Farm in Turner is consistent with an ALF action. Jerry Vlasak from the North American Animal Liberation press office, which represents the ALF in North America, also said it was consistent with an ALF action but has not received an anonymous communique taking credit for the action. Vlasak also said communiques are often submitted by activists days or even weeks after an event but sometimes aren’t sent at all.

“There have been over 100 fur farm raids in the United States dating back to the 1990s,” Buddenberg said. “Cutting the fences, opening cages, and destroying breeding records have been tactics historically utilized by the ALF.”

Buddenberg pleaded guilty in 2016 to conspiracy to violate the Animal Enterprise Terrorism Act after he and a partner were accused of terrorizing the fur industry during cross-country road trips. He has since completed his sentence and said he hopes speaking out can help people understand why activists go to such extreme lengths.

“Every summer we see activists break in to free mink from farms,” he said. “Every November, they’re pelted.”

Farmed mink are typically bred and raised early in the year until around November, when they’re harvested for their pelts, which are sold for luxury fur apparel and other items. The industry generated $28.1 million in pelts in 2024, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Mink Survey.

Humanely certified operations use carbon monoxide gas, which immediately renders them unconscious and ensures they die quickly and without pain, according to the trade organization Fur Commission USA. The group estimates there are approximately 275 mink farms in 23 states across the U.S., and has said mink that are released often don’t survive.

“If they stayed on the farm, they’d have a 100% death rate,” he said. “Release at least gives them a chance at survival. Fur farmers should definitely expect to see more of this before November.”

Despite his previous felony conviction and time served, Buddenberg remains steadfast in his views.

“Opening cages and freeing these animals is the most compassionate thing you can do,” he said. “My mind hasn’t changed on that at all.”

Oregon’s mink farming industry is a shadow of what it once was. Data from the U.S. Department of Agriculture show Oregon had 37 mink farms in 1978. A decade later, in 1998, that number dropped to 30. By 2006, there were only 18 mink farms in Oregon. Since then, the USDA has stopped including the number of ranches in its reports. Some estimates say Oregon currently has around 11 mink farms. Others, including Buddenberg, estimate there are only about five left in the state, including Cascade.

“Actions like this have a history of closing fur farms,” Buddenberg said. “My hope is that this farm will close. Actions like this are very effective.”

The ALF claimed responsibility for multiple mink farm break-ins in Oregon in 2008, according to several reports published in the Oregonian and the Daily Astorian. They included a break-in at Jefferson Mink Farm in Jefferson, a break-in at S&N Fur Farm in Scio, and a break-in at Ylipelto’s Fur Farm in Astoria. In all three cases, fencing around the farm was cut, and the mink were released into the wild.

title: Erfolg: Emma Matratzen beendet Zusammenarbeit mit HKTVmall
content:
Seit 2022 finanziert die Hong Kong Technology Venture Company Limited (HKTV) dutzende tödliche

Tierversuche

: Dabei werden Schweinen und Schafen in Experimenten Gliedmaßen und ihre Köpfe abgetrennt. Das Unternehmen ist die Muttergesellschaft von HKTVmall, einer der bekanntesten Online-Shopping-Plattformen Hongkongs.


Mit den Experimenten soll Technologie entwickelt werden, um Organe von Tieren für eine mögliche

Transplantation in Menschen

 zu nutzen. Dabei räumt HKTV selbst ein, dass die Versuche in hohem Maße spekulativ seien und es „keine Garantie“ für einen künftigen Nutzen für Menschen gebe.[1]


PETA USA und PETA Asien machen seit Frühjahr 2026 mit Protesten, Gesprächen mit Geschäftspartnern und weiteren Aktionen Druck auf HKTV. Die Kampagne zeigt Wirkung: Mehrere Unternehmen haben ihre Zusammenarbeit mit HKTVmall beendet oder angekündigt, dies zu tun. Im August 2026 kam mit dem deutschen, international agierenden Matratzenhersteller Emma ein weiteres großes Unternehmen hinzu.


Erfolg nach PETA-Gesprächen: Emma beendet Zusammenarbeit mit HKTVmall


Im August 2026 gab der Matratzenhersteller Emma bekannt, seinen Onlineshop auf HKTVmall bis Ende des Jahres zu schließen und die Geschäftsbeziehung vollständig zu beenden. Zuvor hatte PETA das Unternehmen darüber informiert, dass die Muttergesellschaft von HKTVmall tödliche Experimente an Schweinen und Schafen finanziert. 


Damit reiht sich Emma in eine wachsende Zahl von Unternehmen ein, die nach Bekanntwerden der Tierversuche Konsequenzen gezogen haben. Nach Beendigung der Geschäftsbeziehung sollen auch keine Provisionen oder Gebühren von Emma mehr an die Shopping-Plattform fließen. 


Die Emma

 Matratzen GmbH

 erklärte zu der Entscheidung: 


„Bei Emma wissen wir, dass guter Schlaf auch bedeutet, ein reines Gewissen zu haben. Sobald wir von den besorgniserregenden Tierversuchen erfahren haben, die von der Muttergesellschaft von HKTVmall finanziert werden, haben wir entschieden, unsere Geschäftsbeziehung mit HKTVmall nicht fortzusetzen. Der Shop wird geschlossen und die Geschäftsbeziehung bis Ende des Jahres vollständig beendet. Wir schätzen und unterstützen es, dass PETA uns darauf aufmerksam gemacht hat.“ 

Emma Matratzen GmbH

 


Weitere Unternehmen beenden Zusammenarbeit mit HKTVmall


Emma ist nicht das erste Unternehmen, das die Zusammenarbeit mit HKTVmall wegen der Tierversuche beendet. Bereits im Frühjahr 2026 hatten mindestens drei weitere Unternehmen öffentlich Konsequenzen gezogen: 


das Kosmetikunternehmen Lush Asia Limited, 


das Unternehmen für Gesundheitsprodukte für tierische Mitbewohner Pawfect Reborn, 


der Essenslieferdienst Fitasty. 


Lush Asia Limited begründete seinen Rückzug ausdrücklich mit Bedenken wegen der Tierversuche innerhalb der Unternehmensgruppe. Das Unternehmen erklärte, auch eine indirekte finanzielle Unterstützung solcher Experimente vermeiden zu wollen. 


Die Reaktionen zeigen: Öffentlicher Druck und die direkte Ansprache von Geschäftspartnern können konkrete Veränderungen bewirken.


Was passiert bei den von HKTV finanzierten Tierversuchen? 


Nach Informationen von PETA USA und PETA Asien finanziert HKTV seit 2022 dutzende Experimente, bei denen Schweine und Schafe verstümmelt und getötet werden. Dabei werden den Tieren unter anderem ihre Gliedmaßen und Köpfe abgetrennt.


Mit den Versuchen sollen Technologien für Organtransplantationen entwickelt werden. Organe von Tieren sollen dabei auf ihre Eignung für eine mögliche Transplantation in Menschen untersucht werden.


Wir von PETA Deutschland und unsere internationalen Partnerorganisationen kritisieren diese Experimente nicht nur aus

ethischen Gründen

. Es stehen auch

tierversuchsfreie Methoden

 zur Verfügung, um menschliche Gesundheit, Organerhaltung, Geweberegeneration und Transplantationsverfahren zu untersuchen.


PETA USA und PETA Asien fordern das Unternehmen daher auf, die Finanzierung der Tierversuche unverzüglich zu beenden und auf tierfreie Methoden umzusteigen.


April 2026: Proteste und erste Unternehmen wenden sich von HKTVmall ab 


Im April 2026 wandte sich PETA Asien schriftlich an die Unternehmensleitung und forderte ein sofortiges Ende der Experimente. 


Auch vor der Zentrale von HKTVmall machten Aktive auf das Leid der Tiere aufmerksam. Bei einer Protestaktion trugen sie blutverschmierte Overalls sowie übergroße Schweine- und Schafsmasken. Mit symbolischen Tierköpfen, einer riesigen Spritze und einem blutverschmierten Messer …

title: Leveret Hunting Underway Across The Country
content:
The recent conviction of packs such as the Stowe School Beagles, the Pipewell Foot Beagles and the Dorset & Somerset Bassets have highlighted the ongoing issue of illegal hare hunting.


But far from being deterred by their paltry fines, these and other packs will shortly be beginning their programme of illegal leveret hunting.


Low key: beaglers head out into the killing fields.


What Is Leveret Hunting?


As with fox hunting, beagles must be trained to hunt and kill their quarry. Leverets – young hares – present an easy target for the new and inexperienced hounds. The pack of beagles are taken to open fields and encouraged to search for hares and leverets. Unlike in main season hunting, the hunters do not want a long chase. They will even turn escaping leverets back towards the hounds to ensure a quick kill.


Leveret hunting usually takes place in September and early October but can start as soon as crops are cleared. The hunters meet early in the morning – from 6am onwards – because that is when the scent is best for new, inexperienced hounds and because the countryside is very quiet.


The Sandhurst & Aldershot Beagles keep a low profile.


“The Hare Hunters Equivalent of Cub Hunting”


Fox hunters have tried to rebrand their cub hunting as ’autumn’ hunting. However, beaglers recognise that hunting young hares is so horrendous that they simply deny it exists. A brief look at their literature – from the days when they were a little more open and honest – reveals otherwise:


“…young hounds should be allowed to get away on a well-grown leveret rather than an old, experienced hare.” –

‘Early Hunting Lessons’ chapter in ‘Beagling’ by J.C. Jeremy Hobson.


“…hounds are taken out in the early morning or late afternoon. This is for the hare hunters equivalent of cub hunting; some masters, in fact, call the period “leveret hunting.” –

‘Hunts and Countries’ chapter in ‘Beaglers’ by Jack Ivester Lloyd


“In order to get young hounds trained to hunt they start hunting in the very early morning or evening once the harvest is clear usually in August or September. They are accompanied only by invitation of the Master for this beagling equivalent of the foxhunter’s cub-hunting.” –

An Introduction To Beagling by Iain Clarke.


Typical leveret hunt meet: note hound trailer to the left.


What does it look like?


Obviously, a pack of small beagle hounds in the middle of a field is a give-away. There will be few people present as only the most trusted supporters are invited to attend these secret hunts. Don’t expect the hunters to be in uniform – they don’t usually wear this until the main season.


Stowe School Beaglers congratulate each other after tearing a hare to pieces.


What should I do if I see a suspected leveret hunt?


If it is safe to do so, filming the hunters will often be enough to stop them in their tracks. Try to film key individuals and their vehicles. Please then pass this information to the Hunt Saboteurs Association tip-off line on:

07443 148426

.


Hunting leverets with dogs is illegal so, if you believe a crime is in progress, call the police straight away.

Leveret Hunting Underway Across The Country

Hunt Saboteurs Association

author: Peter Höffken
title: Landtagswahlen Sachsen-Anhalt 2026: Parteien im Tierschutz-Check
content:
Wahlen sind ein wichtiges Ereignis für alle

Tierfreund:innen

, um auch den Tieren ihre Stimme zu verleihen. Die Wahlprogramme der Parteien sind jedoch oft kurz gehalten und nicht immer eindeutig formuliert. Um den Bürger:innen die Wahl zu erleichtern, haben wir von PETA Deutschland die wichtigsten Parteien in Sachsen-Anhalt vor den Landtagswahlen am 6. September 2026 gebeten, ihre Positionen zu acht wichtigen Tierschutzthemen zu offenbaren.

author: Alex Baumhardt
title: The Public Supports Climate Superfund Bills. The Oil Lobby Is Tanking Them.
content:
The bills target companies directly linked to 80 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions over the past decade.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Oregon lawmakers next week will confront another record bill for the costs of fighting massive wildfires across the state, which have been exacerbated by unseasonable heat and ongoing drought.

These are byproducts of a warming planet, decades of scientific study has proven, as increasing amounts of greenhouse gas pollution from burning fossil fuels gets trapped in Earth’s atmosphere.

If previous years are any indication, Oregon’s Legislative Emergency Board will dip into taxpayer revenues to try to cover the costs, pulling away public dollars that could otherwise be spent on education, healthcare and other critical services and infrastructure.

But testimony submitted on behalf of proposals to create so-called climate Superfunds in Oregon and in 11 other states — modeled after the federal Superfund program that requires polluters to pay for cleanup at the nation’s most contaminated sites — show widespread public support for making some of the most profitable fossil fuel companies in history contribute to damages.

Two proposals in Oregon in 2025 and 2026 from retiring state Sen. Jeff Golden, D-Ashland, garnered packed public hearings and testimonies in support, but ultimately died in committees before getting to the House or Senate floors for a vote.

Across states, public support for climate Superfund bills has been no match for the behind the scenes lobbying of the fossil fuels industry, according to a recent report from Brown University’s Climate and Development Lab. The state Superfund bills target companies like Exxon Mobil, Chevron, and about 50 other oil, gas, coal and cement producers that are directly linked to 80% of the world’s global greenhouse gas emissions during the past decade alone.

“These are companies that have, for at least 40 or 50 years now, known the impacts of their products and have nevertheless worked actively to undermine the science and the reporting and the political understanding and action,” said Timmons Roberts, a Brown environmental studies and sociology professor who worked on the report. “I mean, they’ve thrown everything they have against it.”

Roberts and researchers at Brown pulled together over 4,000 lobbying and committee testimony positions on climate superfund bills submitted across 12 states since 2022, including on 2025 and 2026 proposals in Oregon, to better understand who is opposing climate Superfund bills and what they are arguing.

They found that supporters of climate Superfunds dominated public hearings about the proposals, and the ratio of support to opposition was roughly 3:1 in nearly every state. California and Oregon saw more than twice the amount of testimony in favor of climate superfund bills as any other state.

But behind the scenes, they found powerful industry groups lobbied against the bills across states, including in Oregon. Among them are the National Federation of Independent Business, funded in part by petrochemical company Koch Industries, the American Chemistry Council and the Western States Petroleum Association.

Most of the powerful opposition testimony was not given in person, Brown researchers found, but in submitted documents and behind the scenes lobbying.

During committee hearings for both of Golden’s attempts to pass climate Superfund bills in Oregon, he most remembers hearing from kids worried about their futures under growing climate change-related disasters.

“Then we had some industry lobbyists come into our hearing and just flatly say: ‘If it passes, every Oregon business would pay much more in energy costs.’ And I’d say, ‘What’s your data? What substantiates that?’ And I haven’t been shown anything,” he said.

Golden said he was particularly frustrated by the fact that bill supporters contributed detailed studies about the potential benefits of the climate Superfund, including one from Nobel-prize-winning Economist Joseph Stiglitz, who challenged lobbyists’ assumptions that oil companies would thrust Superfund costs onto consumers.

“It’s like a lot of public policy disputes,” he said. “One side is prepared with sound data from reputable sources, and the other is just shouting platitudes.”

author: The Canadian Press
title: Global warming will exceed limit, UN says in a report that maps path to get back below danger zone
content:
In a strategic retreat in the fight against climate change, the United Nations has acknowledged that Earth has lost its chance to prevent some of the worst of global warming’s harms. So now the world must figure out how to get temperatures below the danger zone and back to safety, officials say.


Earth is soon going to exceed the safe temperature threshold agreed upon by the world in the 2015 Paris climate accord because of warming from the burning of coal, oil and gas, according to a bleak first-of-its-kind report issued by the United Nations Environment Programme Wednesday.


Instead of giving up, scientists and U.N. officials recommend trying to limit excessive warming and then bring the temperature back down to the agreed-upon threshold. But it still will mean decades of increased weather-related disasters, rising seas, extinctions and melting ice and glaciers.


“Humanity is speeding past the limit to avoid climate catastrophe,” United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres said.


After a period of over-the-limit warming, the new strategy envisions getting back below the limit by ending fossil fuel use and developing some kind of way to suck industries’ carbon dioxide out of the air.


“It’s a reality check. We have to live with this warmer world,” said report co-author Richard Betts, a climate scientist at the University of Exeter. “But there’s still a lot we can do to limit warming.”


Passing the longtime warming threshold


After the Paris climate accord, the United Nations ordered its climate science arm to study different warming limits. A goal of 1.5 Celsius (2.7 Fahrenheit) above mid-19th century temperatures became generally accepted after the scientists found dramatic impacts that affect people and the planet at 2 degrees Celsius (3.8 degrees Fahrenheit) but not at 1.5 degrees.


The world is now at 1.4 C (2.5 F) above pre-industrial levels, some scientists have calculated. The measure is based on a 20-year average, rather than a single year’s temperatures.


Despite experts saying there’s no way to limit warming to 1.5 degrees, U.N. officials long maintained the 1.5 window was still open. Wednesday’s report finally admitted that the world will cross the 1.5 threshold “in the next few years.”


The report said the most optimistic scenario has warming peaking at 1.8 C (3.2 F) around mid-century if countries pursue ambitious climate goals, but that governments’ current policies should push temperatures to 2.6 C (4.7 F) above pre-industrial levels by 2100.


So instead of preventing warming of 1.5 degrees, now the U.N. said it wants policymakers to “prepare for and navigate a future” in which the globe crosses that limit and then corrects course and cools temperatures. The report envisions that global temperatures will pass 1.5 “within the next few years,” follow a hump-shaped path of more warming, peak, then gradually cool to below the 1.5 mark, ideally by the end of the century. The report and experts call it “overshoot.”


“Let’s be very clear, 1.5 target is still the goal. But now we need to approach it differently from above,” said UNEP Executive Director Inger Andersen.


The 1.5 limit is not “some magical climate cliff” where it’s just game over, said University of Victoria climate scientist Andrew Weaver, who wasn’t part of the study. “Every tenth of a degree we avoid still means less damage.”


Limiting how high temperatures go past threshold is key


It’s most important to first limit the new peak temperature and then reduce the amount of time above 1.5 degrees, Andersen said.


But the world likely will be in that overshoot period for “many, many decades,” Betts said.


Every five years of delay in reducing emissions adds at least a tenth of a degree to peak warming, said report co-author Joeri Rogelj, a climate scientist at Imperial College London.


“If we act now we can limit overshoot,” the report said. “Not a safe world, but safer than remaining above” 1.5 degrees for the long term.


“This is among the bleakest U.N. climate reports I have read. It carries the unmistakable tone of desperation, frustration and urgency — but not resignation,” Weaver said.


Climate scientist Bill Hare, CEO of Climate Analytics, said that “although UNEP does a good job of describing the hole we’ve dug ourselves into, it does a poor job of showing us that there’s a way out.”


Adapting to a deadlier, hungrier, thirstier world

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: City of Iqaluit recycling proposal sitting in limbo with Department of Finance
content:
Work to re-establish a beverage recycling program in Iqaluit seems to have stalled with the Nunavut government, after the city presented territorial officials with a feasibility study earlier this year.


Iqaluit residents lost the program in July 2025 after local business Northern Collectables discontinued the service. Iqaluit city council

passed a motion

 in December, asking administration to embark on a feasibility study for the municipality to take over the program.


The study analyzed adding a reverse vending machine and other container deposit options for the city, along with cost estimates.


The city then met with territorial officials, said city spokesperson Geoffrey Byrne, but can’t move forward without financial support.


“Council has been clear that any such program would need to be cost-neutral to the municipality,” he said in an email.


Nunatsiaq News asked the Finance Department what came of these talks but only received a statement from spokesperson Hala Duale that the department

“does not have plans to reintroduce a refundable container deposit program at this time.”


Derek Allerton, an Iqaluit resident who says he collected approximately 14,000 cans off the streets in the past year, said the Government of Nunavut’s response is frustrating.


“Tens of thousands of alcohol aluminum beverage cans litter the streets of Iqaluit, and millions of aluminum cans are going to landfill,” he said.


Some of these cans have made it to a fundraising bin managed by Aqsarniit middle school’s environmental club, which

started

 a beverage drop off this spring with help from the Department of Environment. But the club only accepts non-alcoholic beverage containers.


“In my personal experience, one in four cans littering the city are pop cans, and the rest are alcohol beverage cans,” Allerton said, adding the

 most popular brands he sees littering the streets are Molson Dry, Budweiser and Molson Canadian. 


The environmental club’s initiative is far from a solution, Allerton said. For many, it’s too far out of the way.


“There’s a lot of pop consumed in the city, so I think there could be easily multiple drop-off points for pop cans to be recycled,” Allerton said.


He added he was previously feeling hopeful 

about the prospects of the territorial government resolving the issue after Premier John Main wrote to him in June to assure him the city and territory were “actively working together” to resume a “successful long-term program.”


“The Government of Nunavut (GN) has received a proposal from the City of Iqaluit with several different program options and there is a group which has been meeting regularly to develop a city-led program,” Main wrote to Allerton in a letter dated June 22.


“As of today, there is no confirmed funding model or program structure, because the parties are still analyzing the different program options with their respective funding needs,” the premier wrote.


“We are committed to continuing our work with the city to develop a program with clearly defined roles and responsibilities.”


Main also shared with Allerton that the territory’s liquor commission is no longer collecting a waste management fee on alcoholic beverages until a “new solution” can be found.


Nunatsiaq News has reached out to the premier’s office to clarify his position on the funding of a new recycling program for the city but did not immediately hear back.


Nunavut’s Finance Department did not respond to follow up questions regarding whether it is committed to funding a program at some point in the future.

author: Aaron Ernest Cruz
title: Groups condemn violence in Nueva Vizcaya, 11 arrested residents released on bail
content:
Mass arrests in Kasibu spur calls to suspend Nueva Vizcaya mine exploration. (Photo from Nordis)

MANILA – Progressive groups condemned what they described as worsening state violence against the anti-mining community in Kasibu, Nueva Vizcaya.

The most recent incident was the arrest of 11 individuals on August 28. After posting bail for grave coercion at resistance and disobedience cases, the 11 have been released.

Police claimed that they only responded to a 911 call from the North Luzon Mineral Resource Center (NLMRC). The residents blocked the entry of crude oil to the mining site.

According to the Center for Environmental Concerns (CEC), 13 were initially arrested but two of them were rushed to the hospital.

This is but the latest in the series of harassment against those who are guarding the barricade as opposition to the mining exploration of the NLMRC.

Three members of Kasibu Inter-Tribal Response towards Ecological Development (KIRED) were arbitrarily arrested on August 19. Lei Jin Dugay, Don Dugay, and June Fiataccag posted bail for charges of grave coercion and violation of the Article 151 of the Revised Penal Code.

Lawyers defending the community are also slapped with criminal charges.

Read: 3 anti-mining Nueva Vizcaya residents released on bail, groups decry harassment

The incident has called the attention of the international community. Astrid Puentes Riaño, United Nations Rapporteur for the environment, said that she is alarmed over the situation of the environment defenders and Indigenous leaders facing threats and harassment by state forces in the Philippines.

For Kalikasan People’s Network for the Environment (KPNE), it is alarming that the community is continuously facing state violence when they are just only protecting their livelihood and the environment.

“This pattern confirms that mining operations threaten not just the land, but the very lives of those defending it. It further exposes how the police are failing their duty to protect the people, instead acting as enforcers for plunderous mining corporations,” KPNE stated.

KATRIBU Kalipunan ng Katutubong Mamamayan ng Pilipinas asserted that defending their land is their right and should not be treated as a crime, especially in defending ancestral land.

“NLMRC’s mining incursion is being enforced through state violence. The deployment of police to facilitate its operations and arrest residents resisting its entry proves that the PNP [Philippine National Police] serves the interests of the mining company instead of protecting the people,” the group said.

For many months, the community has continued to defend their land by setting up seven barricades across Kasibu. The groups claimed that the Mines and Geoscience Bureau granted the NLMRC a 4,456 hectares of mining exploration without genuine consultation with the community which will be affected.

The community asserted that the mining exploration will affect the ancestral land recognized by the National Commission of Indigenous People. The commission also granted them a Certificate of Ancestral Domain Title.

Read: Indigenous community rising up against mining in Nueva Vizcaya

In a statement, Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan) condemned the mining surge under the Ferdinand Marcos Jr. administration where he enabled the intensified extraction of critical minerals through mining.

Recently, Marcos Jr. met with executives of Canadian-based mining corporation Didipio Gold-Copper Mine and secured a P1.9 billion ($30.73 million) investment for them to operate until 2037.

According to Bayan, such a move is selling out the land and environment to foreign plunderers that led to the massive flooding and landslide in the country.

“Over the past year, we saw how the people of Dupax and Kasibu defended their communities by protesting the entry of extractive companies. Those who profit from mining plunder retaliated by filing SLAPP suits and weaponizing state machineries to undermine local resistance,” Bayan said.

SLAPP stands for Strategic Lawsuit Against Public Participation. According to the lawyers of Kasibu residents over 30 SLAPP cases were filed against the Indigenous Peoples and environmental defenders who are defending their land against mining in Nueva Vizcaya alone.

The groups called for a “halt to destructive mining activities in Kasibu and make Marcos Jr accountable for letting the state violence happen to the community who are only protecting their land and livelihood.” (AMU …

title: 9,000-year-old mining workshop unearthed in Ergani
content:
Excavations carried out at Kotaberçem (Çayönü Mound) in the Ergani district of Amed (Diyarbakır) have uncovered a mining workshop of approximately 5 square meters, dating to 6900–6800 BCE. Raw and processed pieces of malachite, as well as copper objects, were found at the site. The excavations, wrote Mezopotamya Agency (MA), were led by Çanakkale Onsekiz Mart University, and identified at least six postholes around the workshop, which was uncovered in the western part of the settlement, as well as a stone-paved work area at its center.


The postholes possibly indicate that the production area may have been covered with a canopy or shelter. Raw and semi-processed malachite, processed malachite samples, copper beads, and various copper objects were found in the workshop. Including finds from the center of the workshop and its immediate surroundings, the number of malachite and copper fragments identified across the wider excavation area has reportedly reached approximately 42.


Shedding light on the history of mining


The discovery of raw materials, semi-processed pieces, and finished products in the same area indicates that mining activities were carried out in an organized manner within a designated work area. Earlier evidence of the use of copper and malachite at Kotaberçem dates back as far as 9100 BCE. The new discovery is said to demonstrate that the region’s mining tradition developed and continued for approximately 2,000 years.


Located within the Ergani and Tigris River Basin, Kotaberçem is among the important settlements of the Neolithic period, with finds providing evidence of the development of settled life, agriculture, and animal husbandry.

author: Unknown
title: Uşak'ta 6 köyün sakinlerinden Murat Dağı'ndaki maden çalışmalarına tepki
content:
Uşak'ta Murat Dağı çevresinde yaşayan 6 köyün sakinleri, bölgede maden sahalarının ruhsatlandırılmasını protesto etti.

Dağdemirler Köyü yakınlarında bir araya gelen köylüler, maden faaliyetlerinin bölgedeki su kaynaklarına, tarım ve hayvancılık faaliyetlerine zarar vereceğini belirtti.

Dağdemirler Köyü Muhtarı Mustafa Kozak, burada yaptığı açıklamada, köylerinin de içinde bulunduğu geniş bir alanın maden sahası olarak ruhsatlandırıldığını öğrendiklerini belirterek, söz konusu bölgenin Murat Dağı'ndaki su kaynakları açısından önem taşıdığını söyledi.

Kozak, ruhsatlandırılan alanlara ilişkin hukuki süreç başlattıklarını ifade etti ve şunları kaydetti:

"Yakın zamanda köyümüzün de içinde olduğu büyük bir sahanın maden sahası olarak ruhsatlandırıldığı ve ihalesinin yapılıp satıldığını öğrendik. O günden bugüne herkeste bir telaş, bir sıkıntı doğdu. Aynı zamanda işin arkasını bırakmadık. Köy halkını bilgilendirdik. Konuyla alakalı köyümüze gerek maden firmaları gerek başka vatandaşlar gelip dağımızın taşından, toprağından örnek, numune almaya kalktılar. Daha iki gün önce kendi kapımın ağzında maden araştırması yaptılar. 7-8 köyün etkilendiği bir alandayız. Burası Dağdemirler, Yaşamışlar hududu içerisinde. Bu gördüğümüz alan tamamen ruhsatlandırılmış, ihalesi yapılmış, TÜPRAG Madencilik tarafından da alınmış. İki, üç gün önce yeni bir sahanın daha ruhsatlandırılmaya hazırlandığı bilgisine ulaştık. Erişim numarası üzerinden araştırdık, gerçekten de doğru. Bulunduğumuz alan Dağdemirler, Dağyenice, Bağbaşı, Yaşamışlar köyü hududuna, parseline bitişik ikinci bir saha. Burası satılan bölge, dört köyün arası. Aynı zamanda yeni saha da bu sahaya bitişik, ihaleye hazırlanmış. Dağdemirler yerleşim alanı ile birlikte tamamını içine alıp Belkaya hudutları, Kızıldağ sınırlarını, arkada Eğlence, Eski Köy'e kadar inen bir hududu kapsamakta. Toplamda 3 bin 600 hektara yakın bir alan ruhsatlandırılmış. Haritada küçük gibi görünen devasa alan Uşak'a kuş uçuşu 8 kilometre uzaklıkta. Biz burada sadece civar köyler ve köy halkı olarak kendi arazilerimizin gideceğinden korkmuyoruz. Burası sadece köy halkını, civar köyleri etkilemiyor. Burası Murat Dağı'nın arkasında. Murat Dağı'nın Eskişehir, Kütahya, Manisa, Aydın'a kadar besleme yapan su kaynaklarının olduğu ana damarları üzerinde. Buranın altında jeolojik olarak oynanmaması gereken yer altı suları var. Uşak'ın altındaki ovayı da buralar besliyor. Yarın buralarda maden açılır, buralardaki damarlar, jeolojik yapı bozulduğunda Uşak halkı hiç kimseye şikayet etmesin suyu kesildiğinde. Çünkü su kaynakları Murat Dağı'ndan, buranın altından geliyor. Biz bu konuda Uşak halkından da duyarlılık bekliyoruz. Nasıl ki civar köyler TÜPRAG altın madeninin olduğu Eşme sınırları içerisinde doğanın nasıl tahrip edildiğini gördüğü için her şeyin farkında, Uşak halkının da farkına varmasını istiyoruz."

TEMA Uşak İl Temsilcisi Barış Metin ise çok hayati bir mücadele için birlikte olduklarını belirterek, şöyle konuştu:

"Maalesef Türkiye'nin birçok bölgesinde dağlarımız, su havzalarımız, ormanlarımız vahşi madenciliğin yok etme tehlikesiyle karşı karşıya. Uşak çepeçevre çevrelenmiş bir durumda. 20 yıldır vahşi madenciliğin her türlü sorunuyla karşı karşıya kalan, geçen yıl susuzluğu evlerinde günlerce yaşayan Uşak, çok daha büyük bir tehlikeyle karşı karşıya. Biz burada baktığımızda sadece bir orman görmüyoruz, bir dağ görmüyoruz. Burada yaşam var. İnsan her şeyin üstünde değil, her şeyle beraber. Orman yoksa insan yaşayamaz. Su yoksa insan varlığını sürdüremez. Dağ yoksa ovada domatesini yetiştiremez, karnını doyuramaz. Bu insanlar yaşamak istiyor. 'Yaşamak istiyoruz' diyor. Lütfen Uşak'ımızda, Türkiye'mizde dağlarımıza, su kaynaklarımıza, ormanlarımıza vahşi madenciliğin baskısını kaldıralım. Bu ülke ormanıyla, suyuyla, havzasıyla var olabilir, gelecekte de çocuklarını yaşatabilir. Orman yoksa, dağ yoksa, köylü üretmezse hiçbir canlı, özellikle de insan hayatta kalamaz."

Uşak Murat Dağı Yok Olmasın Platformu Sözcüsü Funda Öz Akcura da Murat Dağı'nın bölgenin su kaynakları açısından önem taşıdığını belirterek, "Şu gördüğümüz sadece bir dağ değil, bir su deposu. Bu su deposu sadece Uşak'ın, sadece köylerin değil, Batı Anadolu'nun, Ege Bölgesi'nin her yerinin su deposu. Menderes Havzası da Gediz Havzası da Sakarya Havzası da buradan besleniyor. author: Frederich Kirsten and Mduduzi Biyase
title: Why Lesotho’s remittance ‘safety net’ was never really its own, and why it is failing again in 2026
content:
Lesotho is two years into a national state of disaster: US tariffs have gutted its garment factories, unemployment has passed 30%, and its main trade lifeline is guaranteed for less than a year. To understand how the mountain kingdom keeps ending up here, start almost forty years earlier.In 1987, something extraordinary happened in this small kingdom, completely surrounded by South Africa. Money sent home by Basotho men working in South African gold mines reached

236% of Lesotho’s entire GDP

. Not 23%. Not 60%. More than double the value of everything the country itself produced in a year. Today, that figure sits at around a fifth of GDP. The money didn’t slow down gradually. It collapsed, and it has never recovered. To understand why, you have to understand what that money actually was.


A mountain village in Lesotho.


Why one country’s economy ran on someone else’s mines


For over a century, Lesotho had almost no domestic industry of its own. What it had instead was proximity: a small, mountainous, landlocked territory sitting right next to the richest goldfields on Earth. South African mining houses needed enormous numbers of workers willing to do dangerous, underground labour for low pay, and they built an entire recruitment system to draw men from Lesotho, in their hundreds of thousands, to fill that need.


This wasn’t diversification. It was concentration. An entire national economy came to depend not on a sector but on the hiring decisions of one industry, in one neighbouring country, that Lesotho had no ownership of and no influence over. The arrangement generated enormous sums of money. But it meant Lesotho’s prosperity was never really Lesotho’s to control. It belonged to the price of gold, the depth and cost of South African ore bodies, and the mining houses’ own calculations about profitability: decisions made in boardrooms far from Lesotho.


Why the mines emptied out


South Africa’s gold mining industry has been declining for decades. Ore grades have thinned, extraction has moved ever deeper and more expensive, and profitability has steadily eroded. Industry data shows gold mine employment falling from around

536,000 workers in the late 1980s to roughly 94,000 in 2023, a loss of more than 440,000 jobs

. What is far less well understood is when that decline first showed up on the ground in Lesotho. That is what our research set out to trace.


The illusion of insurance


Here is the idea we set out to test, in ongoing research that is not yet peer-reviewed: a common assumption in development economics holds that remittances act like insurance for vulnerable countries. When disaster strikes at home, such as a drought or a bad harvest, the theory goes, migrant workers send extra money to cushion their families. It appears again and again in World Bank reports and climate-adaptation policy documents. If it were true anywhere, it should have been true in Lesotho. So we tested it every way we could think of: immediate effects and delayed ones, good mining years and bad, average years and the very worst.


So far, we have found nothing. At no point did Lesotho’s own climate conditions appear to move the money flowing into the country. This work is ongoing. But that absence is the whole point. Real insurance responds to your shocks: your drought, your bad year. What Lesotho had was money that moved in response to conditions entirely outside its own borders. That isn’t insurance. It’s exposure to a risk you don’t control, wearing the appearance of a safety net.


What the sequence suggests, and what it does not prove


Our analysis cannot show that the mining industry’s decline directly caused Lesotho’s remittance collapse. Establishing causation from national data alone is genuinely difficult, and we want to be honest about that limit. What we can show is a sequence, dated using statistical tools that detect when a long-running trend breaks.


Net migration out of Lesotho reversed course in

1986

: families were already pulling back from the mines before anything else in the data moved. Just two years later, in

1988

, around the same time mine employment across the industry peaked before its long decline, Lesotho’s remittances began their long, uninterrupted fall. It would be a full decade, until

1998

, before international aid to Lesotho showed any measurable shift. That was also the year of Lesotho’s post-election crisis and SADC intervention, so donors may have been answering the political …

title: Nachhaltigkeit oder Müllproblem? Billig-Kleidung/Fast Fashion – was Mode zum Klimafaktor Nummer 1 macht
content:
Dossier


“… Die Schränke sind voll, die Modeindustrie boomt: Seit dem Jahr 2000 hat sich der Absatz an neuer Kleidung mehr als verdoppelt. Es wird immer billiger und immer schneller produziert. Fast Fashion heißt dieses Phänomen. (…) Dieser Konsum hat seinen Preis. Den bezahlen nicht wir, sondern andere, rechnet uns Thomas Seibert vor. (…) „Sie können mit der Baumwolle anfangen, mit den Pestiziden, die gebraucht werden, mit dem ungeheuren Wasserverbrauch. Jede Menge Flüsse und Seen sind mittlerweile einfach umgekippt, wegen der Einleitung von Abwässer aus der Produktion. Das Wasser was verbraucht wird, um diese Baumwollproduktion aufrecht zu erhalten, wird den Leuten einfach weggenommen, niemand zahlt dafür.“ Ein Rechen-Beispiel: Ein T-Shirt aus 100 Prozent Baumwolle gibt es bei den großen Ketten schon für 1,99 Euro. Aber Baumwolle ist durstig. Für die Baumwolle eines solchen T-Shirts werden dreitausend Liter Wasser benötigt. Die werden häufig einfach dem Grundwasser entzogen…“


Video und Beitrag von Anke Heinhaus vom 12.03.2020 beim Hessischen Rundfunk

 


, siehe dazu:


Shein und Co.: Frankreich erhebt Sondergebühr für Wegwerfmode


„

Zwölf Euro Abgabe pro Jacke, neun Euro für eine Jeans, zwei Euro für ein T-Shirt: Frankreich will die Verbreitung von Billigmode mit Strafzahlungen einschränken. In den kommenden Jahren sollen sie noch weiter angehoben werden.


Eine Billigjacke eines Onlinehändlers wie Shein oder Temu kostet in Frankreich künftig bis zu zwölf Euro mehr. Die Regierung veröffentlichte am Freitag im Amtsblatt die neuen Regeln, die die Verbreitung sogenannter Wegwerfmode einschränken sollen und ab dem 1. September gelten. Im laufenden Jahr werden demnach auch 50 Cent für Unterhosen oder Socken, zwei Euro für ein T-Shirt und neun Euro für Jeans fällig, die bestimmten Kriterien entsprechen. Frankreich wolle auf diese Weise gegen ein Geschäftsmodell vorgehen, »das darauf beruht, dass ein Kleidungsstück in Rekordzeit von der Ladenfläche in die Mülltonne wandert«, schrieb der Umweltstaatssekretär Mathieu Lefèvre im Onlinedienst X.


»Die schädlichen Auswirkungen der Ultra-Fast-Fashion auf unsere Umwelt und unsere Wirtschaft sind bekannt und dokumentiert«, fügte er hinzu. Die Kriterien sind so formuliert, dass sie in erster Linie asiatische Onlinehändler wie Shein und Temu treffen, nicht aber Ketten wie Zara, H&M oder Uniqlo, die in Frankreich Arbeitsplätze bieten. Entscheidend ist die Menge der Modelle, die auf den Markt gebracht werden, und deren Preis im Verhältnis zu einer Reparatur.


Anstieg programmiert


Die Strafzahlungen sollen bis 2030 ansteigen und dann etwa zwei Euro für Unterhosen und 19,50 Euro für eine Jacke erreichen. Das Geld soll in einen Fonds fließen, mit dem vorbildliche Unternehmen unterstützt werden sollen. Dazu sind bislang keine Details bekannt

author: Andrés
title: Contra el extractivismo y el despojo territorial, las Warmis marchan al Congreso
content:
Este jueves al mediodía, mujeres de pueblos originarios de Jujuy se movilizan desde Plaza Miserere hacia el Congreso de la Nación para exigir el cese del saqueo minero. Por ANRed.


Las Warmis del Kollasuyu marcharán durante la mañana del jueves 03 de septiembre por la Ciudad de Buenos Aires. Provenientes de la Puna, la Quebrada y los Valles jujeños, las mujeres originarias trasladan su reclamo para presentar un petitorio formal ante el Congreso de la Nación, frente a la falta de respuestas por parte de la Dirección Provincial de Minería, la Dirección de Recursos Hídricos y el Ministerio de Ambiente de Jujuy, tras la Caminata de Mujeres del 2025.


Tal como adelantaron en su comunicado a la prensa, bajo el lema “Caminatas de Mujeres en defensa de la Pachamama 2026”, las voceras comunitarias exponen en esta jornada la contaminación que afecta a la Laguna de Pozuelos por el impacto de la actividad minera. “Exigimos el cese de la contaminación de nuestros territorios y el respeto a nuestros derechos como Pueblos Originarios”, señalaron en el documento.


Iniciada el 3 de agosto en Rinconada (Jujuy), la movilización al Congreso marca el cierre de la «Segunda Caminata de Warmis». Tras recorrer unos 2.000 kilómetros a pie durante todo el mes, con una reciente escala en Rosario, las manifestantes trasladan sus demandas a Buenos Aires. Denuncian la contaminación de la Laguna de Pozuelos y exigen la intervención de las autoridades nacionales ante la falta de respuestas del gobierno provincial.


Apuntan específicamente contra los daños generados por la Mina Pan de Azúcar, la Mina Pirquitas y la Mina Chinchillas. A este escenario se le suma la amenaza de desalojo que pesa sobre decenas de comunidades de sus tierras ancestrales debido al avance de pedimentos mineros a lo largo de toda la cuenca.


Las organizaciones exponen la violación del derecho a la Consulta Previa, Libre e Informada, consagrado en el Convenio 169 de la OIT, así como el incumplimiento del Acuerdo de Escazú (Ley 27.566) en materia de acceso a la información y justicia ambiental.


A través del petitorio que entregarán, las comunidades interpelan directamente al Poder Legislativo. Quieren: “saber si las comunidades originarias somos tratadas verdaderamente como sujetos de derecho colectivo» Y además, sostienen que: «cuestionamos el favorecimiento del extractivismo por encima del bienestar de las comunidades”.


La postura de las defensoras de la tierra es clara, y así lo dieron a conocer en su comunicado a los medios: «Las mujeres de la Puna, Quebrada y Valles no permitiremos que continúe la fragmentación de nuestras comunidades ni la destrucción de nuestros territorios ancestrales. Exigimos el derecho a permanecer y desarrollarnos en paz en nuestra tierra».

title: Keep It In The Ground August Report
content:
Tamarack Sulfide Copper Mine Meeting – Blaine, MN (August 14, 2026)

A public meeting on the proposed Tamarack sulfide copper mine was held in Blaine, Minnesota. Upon entering, attendees were greeted by eight tables staffed by mining company representatives, positioned next to a tray of lemon-and-cucumber water, cookies, and baked goods. The testimonies, however, were powerful and sobering. A miner from the Iron Range spoke about how cleanup from mining operations conducted fifty years ago is still incomplete, even though that era was considered when they “did it right.” Representatives from the Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe tribal administration testified that the proposed mine sits within two miles of their Minnomem (sp?) ricing beds, presenting an existential threat to the tribe’s land, water, and long-term survivability. Environmental advocates spoke about the track record of mining companies, noting that promises of responsible mining consistently fall short when measured against the devastation of contaminated water, spills, and Superfund sites left unattended for generations.

Northern Arapaho Chairman Opposes Bridger Pipeline (August 18, 2026)

Chairman Keenan Groesbeck of the Northern Arapaho Business Council issued a public statement of opposition to the Bridger Pipeline and expressed support for the Fort Peck Assiniboine and Sioux Tribes. The proposed crude oil pipeline crosses the Canadian border into Montana and Wyoming, traversing treaty lands and the Fort Peck Indian Reservation. The Northern Arapaho stand in solidarity with the Fort Peck Tribes in their opposition, and it is a welcome display of intertribal unity.

Red Stone Movement Meeting Pipestone, MN (August 18, 2026)

The Brave Heart Society, Indigenous Protector Movement, Indigenous Environmental Network, NDN Collective, Minnesota Environmental Affairs Council, the Chairman of the Cheyenne River Sioux Tribe, and others gathered in Pipestone, Minnesota for the Red Stone Movement meeting. The day began with prayers and ceremony at the Sundance grounds. The united message from the group was clear: the survey process for the proposed Magellan pipeline was not conducted correctly, remains incomplete, inadequate, and unacceptable. The movement is calling on regulators to deny the pipeline permit.

Minnesota PUC Pipestone Comment Period Accepted Until September 11, 2026

The Minnesota Public Utilities Commission initial public comment period regarding the Magellan pipeline closed on August 21.

However, reply and final comments will be accepted until September 11. To leave a comment, email the PUC at consumer.puc@state.mn.us, referencing Docket 23-109.

Tribal leaders, Elders, and grassroots defenders are urging even more protectors and the public to comment in OPPOSITION to the Magellan/OneOK pipeline options proposed. The first permit was rescinded when it appeared the opposition was fierce, when 25,000 in opposition flowed in from across the country. Oceti Sakowin Native people and supporters expect that number will be exceeded with this extended deadline. These numbers reflect the sacred nature of the Sacred Site of the Pipestone Quarry, held in reverence and practice by thousands for centuries.

Online: https://mn.gov/puc/consumers/public-comments

Email: consumer.puc@state.mn.us – Reference Docket 23-109

Consumer Affairs Office Minnesota Public Utilities Commission

Governor Walz Signs BWCA Mining Ban Executive Order (August 18, 2026)

Governor Tim Walz signed an executive order banning copper-nickel mining in the Rainy River Headwaters Watershed. The ban preserves vast areas of some of the most pristine and widely used wilderness in Minnesota. Anyone who has canoed, camped, or walked through the Boundary Waters knows it is a life-changing and life-affirming experience that provides a spiritual connection to the natural world. The order effectively canceled the Twin Metals proposed mining project near Ely, Minnesota, and the Bois Forte Reservation.

Trump Administration Opens 62,000 Acres of Superior National Forest (August 19, 2026)

In what appears to be direct retaliation for Governor Walz’s mining ban, the Trump administration opened 62,000 acres of the Superior National Forest to potential mining and development. It is unclear how planned out this move was, but the timing suggests it was a response to the governor’s efforts to protect the area.

author: Darío Aranda
title: Una ciudad con menos árboles y más extractivismo urbano
content:
Por Natalia Concina


La docente y química María Angélica Di Giacomo comenzó en 2010 a enviar notas al Gobierno de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires denunciando que observaba podas indiscriminadas. También contactó a periodistas que cubrían temáticas porteñas, pero durante dos años esas acciones no tuvieron eco. “Un día pasé frente a un árbol que estaban podando y me senté sola a llorar. Me di cuenta que para cambiar algo iba a tener que juntarme con otras personas y abrí un grupo de Facebook al que le puse ‘Basta de Mutilar Nuestros Árboles”. Inmediatamente empezó a sumarse gente”, recuerda Di Giacomo a Tierra Viva.


Y continúa: “Nuestra primera actividad callejera fue cuando sacaron los árboles de la Avenida 9 de Julio para construir el Metrobús. No logramos frenar la remoción, pero fue un punto de inflexión porque comenzamos a tener contacto con quienes defienden el arbolado y el patrimonio natural y cultural de la ciudad”.


Desde entonces el grupo no paró de crecer. La poda tampoco.


El miedo a otros seres vivos


“El árbol no necesita ser podado, no le reporta ningún beneficio. Esta idea de que si le cortas ramas crece con más fuerza es un mito —explica Di Giacomo— La poda se hace por necesidad humana y debería reducirse a la más mínima expresión. Por ejemplo, la poda de refaldado, para que los peatones puedan caminar por la vereda y los autos pasar por la calle, o si tapa un semáforo; en cambio, si tapa una luminaria, ésta podría cambiarse de lugar”.


Sin embargo, desde la organización advierten que en las ciudades existe una percepción del árbol como riesgoso y la poda es vista como una solución: “Muchas personas prefieren los árboles mutilados porque los ven más prolijos. Existe un afán de control sobre la naturaleza y muchos miedos”, dice.


La mujer, que profesionalmente decidió no hacer carrera de investigadora para dedicarse a la docencia, afirma que uno de esos miedos es “a los otros seres vivos”: “Puede ser desde el muchacho que duerme en la puerta del edificio, hasta las abejas, los murciélagos, las palomas o los pajaritos porque les cagan el auto, las cucarachas, las ratas…todo lo vivo da miedo”.


Y agrega: “El otro factor que veo, que es mucho más grave, es que hay una imagen de que la ciudad es un domo. No se sabe de dónde viene el agua, a lo sumo se preocupan si llega el humo de algún incendio desde Rosario o de los humedales del Paraná. Pero no hay noción de que estamos formando parte de un sistema mucho más grande”.


Foto: Basta de Mutilar Nuestros Árboles


Conocer para proteger


Guillermina Bruschi llegó a Basta de Mutilar Nuestros Árboles en 2019 cuando intentaron sacar árboles centenarios en el Barrio Nazca, al oeste de la ciudad, ubicado dentro de los límites de Villa Santa Rita: seis manzanas con edificaciones de más de cien años que en lugar de calles tiene pasajes angostos, un oasis en medio de la ciudad más ruidosa del país.


“En ese camino de defender estos árboles conocimos a María Angélica. Ella nos orientó sobre qué podíamos hacer como vecinos y logramos salvarlos”, cuenta Bruschi.


Con el impulso de ese proceso organizativo, después de la pandemia las y los vecinos retomaron una demanda histórica de Santa Rita: tener una plaza. “El primer documento de pedido de una plaza está en un diario de 1927. No sabemos por qué no se hizo, porque cada uno de estos barrios se hacía con una plaza y con una biblioteca”, relata. Después de varios años de movilización, la lucha tuvo un final feliz: en abril de 2025 se inauguró oficialmente este espacio público para el barrio.


Bruschi reconoce que en estos siete años descubrió muchas cosas que van más allá del arbolado. “Si consideramos que hay

20.000 personas muriendo en Europa por el calor extremo

, uno pensaría que los gobiernos tendrían como prioridad en la agenda la infraestructura verde y sucede exactamente lo contrario”, dice Guillermina, quien describe que en los últimos 20 años, se hicieron

40 millones de metros cuadrados de construcciones

 nuevas.


E indica que “eso significa que, además del calentamiento global, en la ciudad tenemos más hormigón y más cemento que años atrás que retienen más la temperatura y provoca lo que se llama el

efecto ‘isla de calor’

 que implica entre uno y seis grados más que en un entorno urbano donde hay menos cemento y hormigón”.

crisis ambiental

content:
